faqPairs.question: How do multiple bands and venues connect to the same show?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Every event in BandMath generates a unique **6-Character Show Access Code**. Any free Band, Venue, or Tour Manager can create the event (`[ + CREATE EVENT ]`) and share the 6-character code with everyone on the bill. Bands can join (`[ JOIN SHOW ]`) as Headliner, Co-Headliner, Support, or Opener at any time—even mid-show! See [Creating & Joining Multi-Band Shows](/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Creating_and_Joining_Shows).

faqPairs.question: Who claims online ticket sales on a multi-band bill, and when does it lock?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Any participant on the show with an active Pro subscription and connected Stripe account (Venue, Tour Manager, or Band) can click **`[ CLAIM ONLINE TICKETING ]`**. It remains switchable while `0` tickets have been sold, and permanently locks (`🔒`) the instant the first online ticket is purchased so all pre-sale funds and ticket tax set-asides remain unified in one merchant account. Learn more in [Online Ticketing & Promo Links](/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links).

faqPairs.question: How do we track how many pre-sale tickets each band sold?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: When any band on the bill taps **`[ Share Link ]`** on the event page, BandMath automatically attaches their band's attribution tag (`?ref=`) to their checkout link and QR flyer so the Closing Table tracks exact pre-sale tickets sold per band. Fans and street-team promoters can also share their own referral pass to climb the event's **Referral Leaderboard**! See [Online Ticketing & Promo Links](/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links#2-automatic-per-band-promoter-attribution-links-ref).

faqPairs.question: Can I hand my phone to a door person to scan QR tickets without showing them our band's money?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Yes! Open **Bouncer Mode** and enable the **Bouncer Safety Lock** before handing your phone to door staff. They will be able to scan QR tickets with the mobile camera (on iOS and Android) and check off the Guest List all night, but exiting Bouncer Mode requires your device's Face ID, Touch ID, or Passcode. Read more in [Door Tickets & Bouncer Mode](/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Door_Tickets_and_Bouncer_Mode#2-bouncer-mode--the-hand-off-safety-lock).

faqPairs.question: What happens when a band member pockets the cash payout envelope at the end of a show?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: When your band's payout or expense share is marked settled in [The Closing Room](/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room#4-granular-settlement-to-ledger-commits), you choose **`Cash` vs. `Bank Transfer`** and select who received or paid it (`Cashbox`, `Band Bank`, or a specific active member like `John`). If John pockets the cash envelope, BandMath automatically credits every bandmate their share of the show income and records that John is holding the cash—updating your **Standings** immediately.

![Apple Tap to Pay on iPhone Lifestyle](/doc-assets/fr/Accept_Payments/assets/apple_tap_to_pay_goods.jpg) Accepting in-person contactless payments is easier than ever with **Tap to Pay on iPhone** and **Tap to Pay on Android**. These technologies turn your standard smartphone into a secure contactless card reader. This allows **Bands**, **Venues**, and **Tour Managers** to accept physical contactless credit and debit cards, as well as digital wallets like **Apple Pay** and **Google Pay**, directly on your device—no extra terminals or dongles needed. :::warning International Touring Limitation Due to strict banking regulations, Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android will **only function in your home country** (the country where your bank account is registered). If you are embarking on an international tour, you must use the [Stripe QR Codes](/fr/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) workflow to accept card payments. ::: ## Selling Merch vs. Selling Door Tickets You can use Tap to Pay across both in-person checkout flows in BandMath: * **At the Merch Stand (Bands):** Ring up shirts, vinyl, and hoodies in the **Shop / Cart** tabs. * **At the Box Office / Door (Venues, Tour Managers & Bands):** Tap **`[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`** on any event to ring up walk-up admissions via Tap to Pay directly into your own connected Stripe Merchant Account. See [Multi-Custodian Door Ticket POS](/fr/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Door_Tickets_and_Bouncer_Mode) for details on how door card sales reconcile in the Closing Room. :::tip Connecting Stripe for Venues & Tour Managers Operating in the **Venue** or **Tour Manager** persona? Open **User Settings** and use the **`MERCHANT & STRIPE PAYOUTS`** card to connect your Stripe account in minutes. ::: ## How to Accept a Payment (iPhone) When you are ready to check out a fan at the merch table or box office: 1. Complete your checkout flow in the BandMath **Cart** as usual. 2. Select **Tap to Pay on iPhone** as the payment method. 3. Present your iPhone to the customer. The screen will clearly indicate the charge amount, your merchant name, and an instruction for the customer on where to tap. 4. Ask the customer to hold their contactless card horizontally, or their device (like an iPhone or Apple Watch), at the **top edge of your iPhone**, over the contactless symbol. 5. When you see the "Done" checkmark, the transaction is complete! ## How to Accept a Payment (Android) 1. Complete your checkout flow in the BandMath **Cart** as usual. 2. Select **Tap to Pay on Android** as the payment method. 3. Present your Android phone to the customer. 4. Ask the customer to hold their contactless card or smart device against the **back of your phone**. 5. When the payment is approved, the transaction is complete! ### PIN Collection (SCA) If the customer's bank requires a PIN for security (common in Europe), the Android interface will automatically transform into a secure PIN pad, allowing the customer to type their PIN directly on your screen. *Note: This requires the customer's physical card to support "Online PINs". Older cards that only support "Offline PINs" will be rejected because your smartphone does not have a physical microchip slot to read the offline PIN data.* ## Processing Fees When you accept a payment via Tap to Pay on iPhone or Android, the transaction is processed securely through Stripe Terminal. It can be confusing because Stripe batches some of these fees together at the end of the day. Here is exactly how the fees break down for European cards: 1. **Standard Transaction Fee (1.4% + €0.10)**: This is Stripe's standard payment processing fee, taken out of every single transaction individually at the time of the sale. (e.g., on a €15 charge, the fee is €0.21 + €0.10 = €0.31). 2. **Terminal "Tap on Mobile" Fee (€0.10)**: Stripe charges an additional flat fee of €0.10 per physical tap/authorization. Instead of taking this out of each transaction, Stripe batches them up and bills you once at the end of the day (e.g., 9 taps = €0.90 billed for that day). 3. **Radar Fraud Fee (€0.05)**: Normally, in-person Tap to Pay transactions do not incur this fee because the physical card is present. However, if a tap fails and you manually type the card number in, or you send the fan a payment link to pay on their own phone, Stripe treats it as an "online" transaction. This triggers their machine-learning fraud protection tool, Radar, which charges a single €0.05 fee per screened transaction. ## Security and Privacy Tap to Pay uses the built-in features of your smartphone to keep your business and your customers' data private and secure. * **Encrypted Transactions:** All transactions are encrypted and processed securely. * **No Stored Data:** Card numbers are not stored on your device or on merchant servers. ## Accessibility Features The Tap to Pay PIN entry screen includes built-in accessibility options. This ensures that customers who are blind or have low vision can securely and independently enter their PIN with audio assistance if required. ## Requirements **For iPhone:** * You must have an iPhone XS or later. * Your device must be running the latest version of iOS. **For Android:** * Your device must have NFC enabled. * **Developer Options must be turned OFF** in your Android Settings. If Developer Options are enabled, Stripe's security protocols will block PIN collection and fail the transaction.
[Terms apply.](/fr/docs/Terms_of_Service#apple-disclaimers)
articles.plainText:
Merchant Education for Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android

Accepting in-person contactless payments is easier than ever with Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android. 

These technologies turn your standard smartphone into a secure contactless card reader. This allows Bands, Venues, and Tour Managers to accept physical contactless credit and debit cards, as well as digital wallets like Apple Pay and Google Pay, directly on your device—no extra terminals or dongles needed.

 International Touring Limitation
Due to strict banking regulations, Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android will only function in your home country (the country where your bank account is registered). If you are embarking on an international tour, you must use the Stripe QR Codes workflow to accept card payments.

 Selling Merch vs. Selling Door Tickets

You can use Tap to Pay across both in-person checkout flows in BandMath:
 At the Merch Stand (Bands): Ring up shirts, vinyl, and hoodies in the Shop / Cart tabs.
 At the Box Office / Door (Venues, Tour Managers & Bands): Tap [ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ] on any event to ring up walk-up admissions via Tap to Pay directly into your own connected Stripe Merchant Account. See Multi-Custodian Door Ticket POS for details on how door card sales reconcile in the Closing Room.

 Connecting Stripe for Venues & Tour Managers
Operating in the Venue or Tour Manager persona? Open User Settings and use the MERCHANT & STRIPE PAYOUTS card to connect your Stripe account in minutes.

 How to Accept a Payment (iPhone)

When you are ready to check out a fan at the merch table or box office:
1. Complete your checkout flow in the BandMath Cart as usual.
2. Select Tap to Pay on iPhone as the payment method.
3. Present your iPhone to the customer. The screen will clearly indicate the charge amount, your merchant name, and an instruction for the customer on where to tap.
4. Ask the customer to hold their contactless card horizontally, or their device (like an iPhone or Apple Watch), at the top edge of your iPhone, over the contactless symbol.
5. When you see the "Done" checkmark, the transaction is complete!

 How to Accept a Payment (Android)

1. Complete your checkout flow in the BandMath Cart as usual.
2. Select Tap to Pay on Android as the payment method.
3. Present your Android phone to the customer. 
4. Ask the customer to hold their contactless card or smart device against the back of your phone. 
5. When the payment is approved, the transaction is complete!

 PIN Collection (SCA)
If the customer's bank requires a PIN for security (common in Europe), the Android interface will automatically transform into a secure PIN pad, allowing the customer to type their PIN directly on your screen.

Note: This requires the customer's physical card to support "Online PINs". Older cards that only support "Offline PINs" will be rejected because your smartphone does not have a physical microchip slot to read the offline PIN data.

 Processing Fees

When you accept a payment via Tap to Pay on iPhone or Android, the transaction is processed securely through Stripe Terminal. It can be confusing because Stripe batches some of these fees together at the end of the day. Here is exactly how the fees break down for European cards:

1. Standard Transaction Fee (1.4% + €0.10): This is Stripe's standard payment processing fee, taken out of every single transaction individually at the time of the sale. (e.g., on a €15 charge, the fee is €0.21 + €0.10 = €0.31).
2. Terminal "Tap on Mobile" Fee (€0.10): Stripe charges an additional flat fee of €0.10 per physical tap/authorization. Instead of taking this out of each transaction, Stripe batches them up and bills you once at the end of the day (e.g., 9 taps = €0.90 billed for that day).
3. Radar Fraud Fee (€0.05): Normally, in-person Tap to Pay transactions do not incur this fee because the physical card is present. However, if a tap fails and you manually type the card number in, or you send the fan a payment link to pay on their own phone, Stripe treats it as an "online" transaction. This triggers their machine-learning fraud protection tool, Radar, which charges a single €0.05 fee per screened transaction.

 Security and Privacy

Tap to Pay uses the built-in features of your smartphone to keep your business and your customers' data private and secure. 
 Encrypted Transactions: All transactions are encrypted and processed securely.
 No Stored Data: Card numbers are not stored on your device or on merchant servers.

 Accessibility Features

The Tap to Pay PIN entry screen includes built-in accessibility options. This ensures that customers who are blind or have low vision can securely and independently enter their PIN with audio assistance if required. 

 Requirements

For iPhone:
 You must have an iPhone XS or later.
 Your device must be running the latest version of iOS.

For Android:
 Your device must have NFC enabled.
 Developer Options must be turned OFF in your Android Settings. If Developer Options are enabled, Stripe's security protocols will block PIN collection and fail the transaction.

<br /
<small

Terms apply.

</small

articles.title: Stripe QR Codes
articles.body:
Stripe QR Code Checkout provides a secure, reliable way to accept card payments from fans without relying on physical Tap to Pay hardware. It is the required workflow for [Multi-Currency Touring](/fr/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Multi_Currency_Touring) when your band travels abroad, as Tap to Pay requires you to be in your home country.

## How It Works

When a fan makes a purchase at the merch table:
1. In the BandMath Merch Stand, complete the checkout flow as usual.
2. Select **Card** as the payment method, and then tap **Show QR Code**.
3. A unique, 30-minute expiring QR code is generated on your screen.
4. The fan scans the QR code with their own smartphone camera.
5. They are seamlessly redirected to a Stripe Hosted Checkout page on their device.
6. The fan pays securely using **Apple Pay**, **Google Pay**, or by manually entering their physical card details.

## Real-Time Sync & Fulfillment

The BandMath app automatically listens to your backend database via real-time websockets. 

As soon as the fan completes their payment on their device, Stripe alerts our servers. The BandMath app instantly detects this, automatically dismisses the QR code screen, and displays your success receipt. 

Behind the scenes, BandMath automatically deducts the inventory, creates the transaction ledger entry, and handles complex band member splits—all atomically and securely.

### Check Payment Status (Fallback)

If you are playing in a basement club or a venue with spotty Wi-Fi, the real-time websocket connection to your app might drop. If the fan has completed the payment but your app hasn't updated yet, simply tap the **Check Payment Status** button on the QR code screen. This forces the app to manually poll the database and fetch the updated order status immediately.

## Canceling an Order

If the merch line is moving fast and a fan changes their mind (or takes too long), you can simply dismiss the QR code modal in the app. 

When you dismiss the modal, BandMath automatically reaches out to the Stripe API and **explicitly invalidates the checkout session**. This ensures the fan cannot accidentally (or maliciously) complete the payment on their phone five minutes later after you've already moved on to the next customer. The order is safely marked as failed in your ledger.

articles.title: Accepting Cash
articles.body:
BandMath's cash management system is built around the concept of **Cash Custody**. Because BandMath tracks every penny your band, venue, or tour package earns, it needs to know exactly who is holding the physical cash at the end of the night so the ledger stays perfectly balanced.

## How to Accept a Cash Payment

When a fan wants to pay with physical cash at the merch table or box office:

1. **Build the Cart:** Add merchandise items in the **Merch Stand** (or tap **`[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`** to add door admission tickets to your cart).
2. **Select Cash:** Choose **Cash** as the payment method.
3. **Assign Custody:** You will see a dropdown asking **"Who received it?"** Select your own name, the **Cashbox**, or the name of the band member physically taking the money.
4. **Pocket the Cash:** Take the physical cash from the fan and place it in your cash box, lockbox, or pocket.
5. **Complete the Sale:** Tap to finalize the order.

## How the Ledger Handles Cash

When you select your own name as the person who received the cash, you are taking "custody" of that money. 

Behind the scenes, BandMath automatically does the heavy lifting:
* It logs the total revenue for the band (and routes any applicable tax set-aside into the [VAT Bank](/fr/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank)).
* It deducts the items from your inventory (or increments the Door Ticket count on the event).
* It instantly calculates the profit splits for the rest of the group.
* It debits your personal account in the ledger, because you are now holding the band's money. 

At the end of the tour, you don't have to worry about counting up huge stacks of cash and dividing it manually. The **Standings** page will simply show that you owe the band money, which is perfectly offset by the cash already sitting in your pocket!

:::tip Multi-Custodian Door Cash & The Cashbox
When a **Venue**, **Tour Manager**, or **Band** rings up cash Door Tickets via `[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`, BandMath tracks those cash receipts under `Door Tickets by Custodian` in [The Closing Room](/fr/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room) and automatically nets that already-collected cash against your final settlement envelope. For foreign cash tours, see our [Multi-Currency Touring](/fr/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Multi_Currency_Touring#the-merch-float--foreign-cash-walkthrough) guide.
:::

articles.title: The "At-Cost" Member Purchase
articles.body:
**The Scenario:** 
A band member wants to buy one of the band's shirts for themselves, but they only want to pay the wholesale cost (e.g., the shirt costs $5 to print, but retails for $25). They want to take the shirt, ensure the inventory stays accurate, and properly reimburse the rest of the band for the wholesale cost.

**The Nightmare:** 
In a spreadsheet, you'd have to manually deduct the inventory, calculate the cost basis, and then somehow inject a $5 debt for that specific member without inflating your gross retail sales numbers.

**The BandMath Solution (The "At Cost" POS Checkout):**
Because BandMath handles inventory and double-entry routing seamlessly, this is processed exactly like a normal fan sale, but utilizing the built-in "At Cost" toggle.

1. Go to the **Point of Sale (POS)** and add the shirt to the cart.
2. Under the Merch Total, toggle the pricing selector from **Retail** to **At Cost**. This automatically reduces the cart total to match the exact wholesale cost of the items.
3. Tap **Cash**, ensure the active band member is set to the person taking the shirt, and tap **Go!** to checkout.
*Note: No physical cash actually needs to change hands.*

![POS At Cost Toggle](/doc-assets/fr/Advanced_Workflows/assets/pos-at-cost-toggle.png)

**Why this works flawlessly:**
* **Inventory & Analytics:** The POS system automatically deducts the shirt from inventory and logs the sale at $5. This ensures the Sales Analyzer's ROI and profit margins remain 100% accurate (it doesn't look like a shirt was "lost" or stolen).
* **The Settlement Routing:** The algorithm registers that the band member "collected" $5 in cash. Since no actual cash was put into a lockbox, that member is personally holding the $5. The algorithm will automatically split that $5 revenue among the band, meaning the member will effectively "owe" the rest of the band out of their share, perfectly reimbursing the group for the cost of the shirt!

articles.title: Multi-Currency Touring
articles.body:
When your band embarks on an international tour, dealing with foreign currencies, fluctuating exchange rates, and cross-border payment processing can quickly become an accounting nightmare. 

BandMath simplifies this entirely: **You do not need to create a new workspace or change your base currency when touring abroad.**

Instead, keep logging all of your transactions in your primary Band Workspace exactly as you would at home. 

## In-Person Card Payments Abroad

Due to strict international banking regulations, **Tap to Pay on iPhone** and **Tap to Pay on Android** will **only function in your home country** (the country where your bank account is registered). The physical address associated with your payout bank account must match the geographical location where the payment is being taken.

If you attempt to use Tap to Pay while in a foreign country, the transactions will be blocked by Stripe.

### The Solution: Stripe QR Codes

To accept card payments seamlessly when touring internationally, BandMath uses the **Stripe QR Code Checkout** workflow. 

When a fan wants to pay with a card:
1. Select **Card** at checkout and choose **Show QR Code**.
2. The fan scans the QR code with their own smartphone camera.
3. They are taken to a secure, localized Stripe checkout page on their device, where they can pay using Apple Pay, Google Pay, or by manually entering their credit card details.

Because the fan is initiating the payment on their own device rather than your hardware, this bypasses the strict hardware location restrictions of Tap to Pay. 

### Automatic Currency Conversion

When using Stripe QR Codes abroad, you will continue to price your merchandise in your home currency inside the BandMath app. 

Stripe handles the complex foreign exchange (FX) conversion dynamically behind the scenes. The fan is charged the equivalent amount in their local currency, while the funds are deposited into your band's bank account in your home currency. This keeps your BandMath ledger perfectly unified and clean, completely shielding you from the headache of manual exchange rate calculations!

For full technical details, see the [Stripe QR Codes](/fr/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) guide.

## The Merch Float & Foreign Cash Walkthrough

While card payments are converted automatically by Stripe, you will inevitably collect a pile of physical foreign cash at the merch table. To handle this, you need a "Merch Float" (a starting pool of local currency to make change). 

Here is the recommended workflow to handle foreign cash flawlessly using BandMath’s double-entry accounting. 

### 1. Create a "Cashbox"
First, create a [Shadow Profile](/fr/docs/Team_Management/Shadow_Profiles) in your band called **Merch Cashbox**. This acts as a virtual band member that "holds" your physical cash during the tour.

### 2. Fund the Float
When you arrive in the foreign country, one member (e.g., Alice) goes to an ATM, withdraws money from her personal checking account (e.g., $220 USD), and receives local currency (e.g., €200 EUR) to put in the physical lockbox.
* **In BandMath:** Alice logs a **Cash Transfer** from herself to the *Merch Cashbox* for $220. 
*(Alice is credited $220. The Cashbox now owes the band $220).*

### 3. Log Nightly Sales
Every night, log your cash sales normally in your home currency. Do not worry about exact daily exchange rates—just estimate! 
* **In BandMath:** Select *Merch Cashbox* as the person who "collected" the cash. If you sell $2,000 worth of merch, the Cashbox balance grows.
*(The Cashbox now owes the band $2,220 total).*

### 4. Exchange Before You Leave
Before you cross the border or board your flight home, take the massive pile of foreign cash to a currency exchange desk and convert it all back into your home currency. Suppose after exchange rates and fees, you are handed **$2,150 USD** in physical cash.

### 5. Assign Custody
Another band member (e.g., Bob) puts that $2,150 USD in his backpack to take home.
* **In BandMath:** Log a **Cash Transfer** from the *Merch Cashbox* to *Bob* for $2,150.
*(Bob now owes the band $2,150. The Cashbox is left owing the band $70).*

### 6. The True-Up
That missing $70 is the cost of doing business. It acts as a "catch-all" bucket that absorbs the bank fees, market fluctuations, and any mental math errors you made when logging sales over the tour!
* **In BandMath:** Log an **Expense** called "Foreign Exchange Fees" for $70, marked as Paid By: *Merch Cashbox*.
*(The Cashbox balance drops exactly to $0!)*

By doing this, the ledger balances perfectly without anyone having to do manual currency conversions on the road.

:::tip FX Gains
If the foreign currency *strengthens* during the tour, you might get back more than the Cashbox owes (e.g., $2,250 USD). In this edge case, the Cashbox would have a $30 surplus. Instead of an Expense, you would log a $30 **Income** (FX Gain) collected by the Cashbox to zero it out!
:::

articles.title: Working with Hired Merch Sellers
articles.body:
If your band frequently hires local hourly workers to sell merchandise at shows, it might seem complicated to track their cash tills and credit card sales. However, you can perfectly track their cash custody without needing to invite temporary workers to your BandMath workspace using their personal phone numbers or emails.

Instead, we recommend setting up dedicated, generic "Merch Station" accounts.

## 1. Creating Generic Accounts

Rather than inviting the individual, an Admin can create a generic **Active Profile** for the merch table.

1. Create a dummy email address or use a band alias (e.g., `merch1@yourband.com`).
2. Generate an invite code from the **Band Settings** page for a new member named "Merch Station 1".
3. Download the BandMath app on your dedicated merch iPad or mobile device.
4. Use the dummy email to create an account and join the band using the invite code.
5. The device can now remain permanently logged into this generic account.

:::tip

If you run multiple merch tables at large venues, you can create "Merch Station 2", "Merch Station 3", etc., each with its own device.

:::

## 2. Working the Table (POS)

During the show, the hired seller uses the POS on their dedicated device just like any other band member.

* **Cash Sales:** When the seller logs a cash sale, BandMath automatically attributes that cash to the "Merch Station 1" profile. In the ledger, Merch Station 1 now "owes" the band that cash because they are physically holding it in their cash box.
* **Credit Card Sales:** When they log a card sale, the money goes straight to your Band Bank (or the connected Stripe/bank account). Credit card transactions do not affect the seller's physical cash balance in BandMath.

## 3. End-of-Night Cash Handoff

At the end of the night, it's time to reconcile the till and collect the cash. The BandMath ledger will show exactly how much cash "Merch Station 1" is supposed to be holding based on their cash sales.

1. The hired seller counts their cash box and physically hands the cash over to a bandmate or the Tour Manager.
2. In BandMath, log a **Transfer** transaction:
   * **Who Paid:** Merch Station 1
   * **Who Owes:** Tour Manager (or whoever took the cash)
   * **Amount:** The total cash handed over (e.g., $500)
3. **The Magic:** This instantly zeroes out the Merch Station's balance (they no longer owe the band anything) and transfers that cash custody to the Tour Manager, who is now responsible for depositing it or keeping it safe!

:::note

Since the hired sellers are paid separately (e.g. hourly via an eventual paycheck), their pay is completely decoupled from the nightly merch till reconciliation. When you eventually pay them, you can just log that as a standard Expense paid for by the Band Bank!

:::

sections.content:
If your band frequently hires local hourly workers to sell merchandise at shows, it might seem complicated to track their cash tills and credit card sales. However, you can perfectly track their cash custody without needing to invite temporary workers to your BandMath workspace using their personal phone numbers or emails.

Instead, we recommend setting up dedicated, generic "Merch Station" accounts.

sections.heading: 1. Creating Generic Accounts
sections.content:
Rather than inviting the individual, an Admin can create a generic **Active Profile** for the merch table.

1. Create a dummy email address or use a band alias (e.g., `merch1@yourband.com`).
2. Generate an invite code from the **Band Settings** page for a new member named "Merch Station 1".
3. Download the BandMath app on your dedicated merch iPad or mobile device.
4. Use the dummy email to create an account and join the band using the invite code.
5. The device can now remain permanently logged into this generic account.

:::tip

If you run multiple merch tables at large venues, you can create "Merch Station 2", "Merch Station 3", etc., each with its own device.

:::

sections.heading: 2. Working the Table (POS)
sections.content:
During the show, the hired seller uses the POS on their dedicated device just like any other band member.

* **Cash Sales:** When the seller logs a cash sale, BandMath automatically attributes that cash to the "Merch Station 1" profile. In the ledger, Merch Station 1 now "owes" the band that cash because they are physically holding it in their cash box.
* **Credit Card Sales:** When they log a card sale, the money goes straight to your Band Bank (or the connected Stripe/bank account). Credit card transactions do not affect the seller's physical cash balance in BandMath.

sections.heading: 3. End-of-Night Cash Handoff
sections.content:
At the end of the night, it's time to reconcile the till and collect the cash. The BandMath ledger will show exactly how much cash "Merch Station 1" is supposed to be holding based on their cash sales.

1. The hired seller counts their cash box and physically hands the cash over to a bandmate or the Tour Manager.
2. In BandMath, log a **Transfer** transaction:
   * **Who Paid:** Merch Station 1
   * **Who Owes:** Tour Manager (or whoever took the cash)
   * **Amount:** The total cash handed over (e.g., $500)
3. **The Magic:** This instantly zeroes out the Merch Station's balance (they no longer owe the band anything) and transfers that cash custody to the Tour Manager, who is now responsible for depositing it or keeping it safe!

:::note

Since the hired sellers are paid separately (e.g. hourly via an eventual paycheck), their pay is completely decoupled from the nightly merch till reconciliation. When you eventually pay them, you can just log that as a standard Expense paid for by the Band Bank!

:::

articles.title: Live Music Touring Tax, Ticket VAT & Nightly Settlements (EU & US)
articles.body:
When the lights come up after an encore and everyone gathers in the back office to settle the show, the fastest way for a band, promoter, or venue to accidentally lose money is by splitting **Gross** receipts without backing out consumer tax first.

Whether you are dealing with **Value-Added Tax (VAT)** in the European Union and UK or **Sales Tax** across state lines in the United States, tax collected from fans at the door or the merch table is **not** show revenue—it is money held in trust for the government.

This guide breaks down how live music taxes work in the real world across Europe and North America, why ticket tax and merch tax are almost never the same rate, and how BandMath's **Two-Tier Tax Model** protects every band, tour manager, and venue at the closing table.

---

## 1. Why Tax Matters at the Night-of-Show Closing Table

Every ticket or T-shirt sold to a fan in a taxable jurisdiction includes a portion owed to the tax authority. To find the true **Net Revenue** from a tax-inclusive sale, you divide the gross price by `1 + Tax Rate`:

```text
Net Revenue = Gross Receipts / (1 + Tax Rate)
Tax Set-Aside = Gross Receipts - Net Revenue
```

### The "Gross Split" Trap

Imagine a venue processes **€5,350** in ticket sales in a country with **7% Ticket VAT** (`€5,000` Net Revenue + `€350` VAT):
* **If you split Gross (`80% / 20%` of €5,350):** The band walks out with €4,280 and the venue keeps €1,070. At the end of the quarter, the venue (as the merchant of record who processed those sales) still owes the government the full **€350** in VAT—leaving the venue with only €720 (`14.4%` instead of `20%`).
* **If you split Net (`80% / 20%` after backing out 7% VAT):** The **€350** tax set-aside stays with the merchant who processed the tickets so they can pay the government. The remaining **€5,000 Net Ticket Pool** is split cleanly: **€4,000** to the band and **€1,000** to the venue.

### Venue Merch Cuts (`15%–25%`)

The exact same rule applies when a venue takes a percentage of a band's merchandise sales (a "venue merch cut" or "hall fee"):
* Because the band is the merchant of record on their own **Merch Stand**, the band is legally responsible for remitting the VAT or sales tax on every shirt sold, plus absorbing any Stripe card processing fees.
* Standard industry practice calculates the venue's merch commission **Net of Tax and Card Processing Fees**. Otherwise, the band would be paying the venue a 20% commission on tax money that belongs to the government and processing fees already kept by Stripe!

:::tip
In BandMath, every settlement calculation—both for **Ticket Pools** and **Venue Merch Cuts**—automatically backs out the applicable tax set-aside and card processing fees first, ensuring neither the band nor the house ever pays commission on government tax money.
:::

---

## 2. How Touring Tax Works in the European Union (EU & UK)

Under EU VAT law, live concerts and in-person merchandise sales follow the **Place of Supply Rule**: both event admission (tickets) and physical goods sold to fans on-site (merch) are taxed at the rates of the country where the venue is physically located.

When touring Europe, two critical tax realities affect nearly every show settlement:

### Crucial EU Nuance #1: Ticket VAT ≠ Merch VAT

Almost every EU member state treats live concert admission as a protected cultural activity with a **reduced VAT rate**, while taxing physical merchandise (T-shirts, hoodies, vinyl, hats) at the **standard goods rate**:

| Country | Concert Ticket VAT (Reduced Cultural Rate) | Physical Merch VAT (Standard Goods Rate) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Germany** | `7%` | `19%` |
| **France** | `5.5%` *(or `2.1%` for qualifying early runs)* | `20%` |
| **Netherlands** | `9%` | `21%` |
| **Belgium** | `6%` | `21%` |
| **Spain** | `10%` | `21%` |
| **Austria** | `13%` | `20%` |
| **Poland** | `8%` | `23%` |

Because of this gap, a single "Show Tax Rate" can never accurately settle both the box office and the merch table in Europe.

### Crucial EU Nuance #2: VAT-Registered Headliners vs. VAT-Exempt Openers (`0%` SME)

On a multi-band bill, different bands on the exact same stage often have completely different legal tax statuses:
* **VAT-Registered Touring Acts & Venues:** Established touring bands and venues registered for VAT must back out `19%–21%` VAT on their merch sales.
* **VAT-Exempt Indie & Support Bands (`0%`):** Emerging bands operating under their country's small-business exemption (such as Germany's *Kleinunternehmerregelung*, France's *Franchise en base de TVA*, or the **EU Cross-Border SME Scheme**) are legally **VAT-exempt (`0%`)**. They do not charge VAT on their merch and cannot deduct input VAT.

If a closing room forced a flat `20%` merch VAT rate onto a VAT-exempt opener, it would artificially shrink their net merch total before calculating a venue cut. Conversely, if it forced `0%` onto a VAT-registered headliner, the headliner would overpay the venue cut out of their VAT liability.

---

## 3. How Touring Sales Tax Works in the United States

In the United States, there is no federal VAT. Instead, retail sales are governed by state, county, and municipal **Sales Tax** (plus local **Admissions / Amusement Taxes** on tickets in certain cities and states).

### Physical Presence Nexus on Tour

When your band sets up a merch table inside a venue in another state, selling physical goods in person generally creates temporary **physical presence nexus** in that jurisdiction for the night of the show:
* **Local Rate Variations:** A Tuesday night show in Austin, Texas (`8.25%` combined state + city sales tax) has a completely different rate than a Thursday night show in Portland, Oregon (`0%` state sales tax).
* **Product-Specific Exemptions:** A few US states exempt everyday clothing (like T-shirts and hoodies) below a certain dollar threshold while still taxing vinyl, posters, and accessories (for example, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Massachusetts, and New York below `$110`).

### Tax-Inclusive Flat Pricing at the Merch Table

No band wants to make change with coins in a dark club because a `$30` T-shirt rang up at `$32.48` with tax. Working bands across the US price their merch in clean, round, **tax-inclusive** numbers (`$30 T-Shirt`, `$40 Vinyl`).

During the show, fans pay flat round prices. At the end of the night, BandMath uses tax-inclusive math (`$30 / 1.0825 = $27.71 Net`, `$2.29 Tax Set-Aside`) to route the exact tax portion into your [VAT Bank](/fr/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank) and compute the venue's merch cut strictly on your `$27.71` net revenue.

---

## 4. How BandMath Models This Cleanly: Two-Tier Transparency

To support both EU reduced-ticket / standard-merch VAT rules and multi-band bills with mixed tax statuses, BandMath separates show taxation into two transparent, independent tiers:

### Tier 1: Standardized Event Ticket Tax Rate

Ticket tax applies to admission to a specific event in a specific venue, so it is standardized across the entire show:
1. **Set Upfront on the Event:** The Event Organizer (Venue, Tour Manager, or Originating Band) sets the **Event Ticket Tax Rate** when creating or editing the event.
2. **Visible in the Event Header:** Every participant on the bill can see the active ticket tax badge (e.g., **`[ TICKET TAX 7% ]`**) right in the Event Header, and the organizer can adjust it prior to locking the final settlement.
3. **Protects Every Ticket Collector:** Every ticket sold for that event—whether an online pre-sale or a Door Ticket rung up in cash or Tap to Pay by the Venue, Tour Manager, or any Band—uses that single agreed **Event Ticket Tax Rate**. Whoever processed the ticket sale retains the exact tax set-aside in their own account so they are never left short when filing taxes, while the **Net Ticket Pool** flows into the Closing Room for the split.

### Tier 2: Per-Band Merch Tax Rate with Deal Sheet Transparency

Because every band is the legal merchant of record for their own merchandise, each band controls their own **Merch Tax Rate** inside their Band Settings (or directly from their **Show Call Sheet** card):
1. **Automatic VAT Bank Routing:** Whenever a band sells merch in the **Merch Stand** at a show, their configured Merch Tax Rate automatically sets aside the tax liability into their band's [VAT Bank](/fr/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank) in **Standings**.
2. **Call Sheet & Deal Sheet Transparency:** In a multi-band closing room, a venue or promoter should never have to guess why two bands with similar gross merch sales have different net numbers. BandMath prints each band's declared Merch Tax Rate directly on:
   * Their **Show Call Sheet Info Card** (visible to the Closing Officer and band).
   * Every **Deal Sheet** merch cut line item—displaying the exact math in plain sight (for example, `15% of €228.77 (Net of 19% VAT & Stripe)` for a VAT-registered headliner, or `15% of €142.50 (0% VAT · Net of Stripe)` for a VAT-exempt opener).

:::note
Need to change your band's Merch Tax Rate when crossing a border on tour? Update your tax rate in **Band Settings** before opening your Merch Stand for the night, and BandMath will apply the new rate to that night's sales and Deal Sheet without altering any of your previous shows!
:::

articles.title: Upgrading and Downgrading
articles.body:
BandMath offers flexible plans built for working musicians, independent venues, and tour managers. For garage bands and local acts, the core financial ledger, band calendar, setlist organizer, and show creation tools are 100% free. When you are ready to process live card payments—whether via **Tap to Pay**, **Stripe QR Codes**, or **Online Event Ticketing**—you can upgrade in seconds via our Web Accounts Portal.

![Accounts Portal Billing](/doc-assets/fr/Billing_and_Account/assets/pricing-tiers-upgrade.png)

## The Web Accounts Portal (`account.itsbandmath.com`)

To keep subscription costs low for independent artists and venues and avoid 30% App Store surcharges, all billing activities are managed through our dedicated Web Accounts Portal at **[account.itsbandmath.com](https://account.itsbandmath.com)**.

### Logging In with 6-Digit Email OTP
You can sign in to **[account.itsbandmath.com](https://account.itsbandmath.com)** from any desktop or mobile browser using:
* **6-Digit Email One-Time Code (OTP):** Enter your email address and input the 6-digit verification code sent to your inbox.
* **Google or Apple Sign-In:** One-click OAuth authentication.

## Subscription Tiers

All Core Ledger and Event Planning features in BandMath are 100% free. Upgrading unlocks live merchant payment processing and advanced commercial tools:

* **Free Tier (Core Ledger & Events):** Unlimited expense/income tracking, Automated Debt Settlement, Band Calendar, Setlist Organizer, creating or joining multi-band shows via Show Code, and participating in nightly Closing Room settlements.
* **Pro Merchant Plan (`€20/mo`):** Unlocks the commercial **Merch Stand** Point-of-Sale (POS), **Tap to Pay** on iPhone & Android, **Stripe QR Codes**, **Online Event Ticketing**, the **Sales Analyzer**, and the **Inventory Analyzer**.
* **The Bootstrapper's Club (`€100` One-Time Lifetime Pass):** Strictly capped at **100 public founding spots**, the Bootstrapper's Club unlocks lifetime Pro access for a single one-time payment with zero recurring monthly fees.

## Band Workspaces vs. Venue & Tour Manager Portals

The Web Accounts Portal automatically adapts to your active account persona:
* **For Bands:** Select which of your administrated bands you want to upgrade from the band selector, then open the **Billing** tab. Remember: **only one subscription is required per band workspace**, unlocking Pro features for every member of that band!
* **For Venues & Tour Managers (Billing-Only Merchant Portal):** When logged in as a **Venue** or **Tour Manager**, `account.itsbandmath.com` presents a focused **Billing-Only View** tied directly to your external Merchant Account. You can also jump straight to this portal from the **`MERCHANT & STRIPE PAYOUTS`** card inside **User Settings** in the mobile app.

## How to Upgrade

1. Navigate to **[account.itsbandmath.com](https://account.itsbandmath.com)** and log in via **6-Digit Email OTP** or OAuth.
2. For Band accounts, select your band from the dashboard and open the **Billing** tab (Venues and Tour Managers land directly on their Billing view).
3. Choose **Pro (`€20/mo`)** or **Bootstrapper's Club (`€100` Lifetime)** and click **Subscribe** / **Get Lifetime**.
4. Complete checkout through our secure Stripe Checkout page.

![Stripe Customer Portal](/doc-assets/fr/Billing_and_Account/assets/stripe-customer-portal.png)

:::warning
For Band accounts, only **Admins** have permission to manage the band's subscription tier. If you are a standard Member and need to upgrade, ask a band Admin to log in at `account.itsbandmath.com`.
:::

## Downgrading or Pausing Between Tours

If your tour is over and you want to pause your monthly subscription until your next run of shows, you can downgrade at any time:

1. Go to **[account.itsbandmath.com](https://account.itsbandmath.com)** and open the **Billing** tab.
2. Click **Customer Portal** under "Manage Billing".
3. Cancel or pause your subscription inside the secure Stripe Customer Portal.

Your Pro features remain active until the end of your current billing cycle. All of your historical merch sales, event settlements, and ledger data are 100% preserved so you can pick right back up whenever you hit the road again.

articles.title: Managing Payment Methods
articles.body:
BandMath partners with **Stripe** to securely handle all billing and subscription data. This ensures that your credit card information is never stored directly on BandMath servers.

## Updating Your Credit Card

If your credit card has expired, or you simply want to switch the billing to a different card, you can do so through the Stripe Customer Portal.

1. Navigate to **[account.itsbandmath.com](https://account.itsbandmath.com)** in your web browser.
2. Log in and select **Manage Subscription**.
3. This will open the secure Stripe Customer Portal.
4. Under the **Payment Methods** section, you can add a new card, delete an old card, or set a new default payment method.

![Stripe Customer Portal](/doc-assets/fr/Billing_and_Account/assets/stripe-customer-portal.png)

## Failed Payments

If a recurring subscription payment fails, Stripe will automatically attempt to retry the charge a few days later. You will receive an email notification prompting you to update your payment method.

If the payment continues to fail after several retries, your band workspace will automatically be downgraded to the free/core tier until the payment issue is resolved.

articles.title: Cancellations and Data Export
articles.body:
If the band breaks up (we hope not!) or you simply no longer need to use BandMath, you can cancel your subscription and export your data at any time.

## Canceling Your Subscription

To stop future billing:
1. Navigate to the web portal at **[account.itsbandmath.com](https://account.itsbandmath.com)**.
2. Select **Manage Subscription** to open the Stripe portal.
3. Select **Cancel Plan**.

Your premium features will remain active until the end of your current billing cycle. After that, your workspace will be downgraded to the free tier. Your data is not deleted when you cancel a premium subscription.

## Exporting Your Data

We believe your financial data belongs to you. You can export your entire ledger to a CSV file for your accountant or for your own records.

1. Go to the **Settings** page.
2. Select **Data Export**.
3. Choose the date range you wish to export, and tap **Download CSV**.
4. The generated CSV will contain every transaction, including the date, amount, payer, receivers, and itemized merch sales.

![Data Export and Deletion](/doc-assets/fr/Billing_and_Account/assets/data-exports-screen.png)

## Deleting Your Workspace

If you want to permanently erase your band's data from our servers:

:::danger

Deleting your band workspace is **irreversible**. All ledger history, merch inventory, and member profiles will be permanently erased.

:::

1. Go to **Band Settings**.
2. Scroll to the very bottom and tap **Delete Band Workspace**.
3. You will be prompted to type the name of your band to confirm the deletion.

Only an Admin can delete a band workspace.

articles.title: Creating & Joining Multi-Band Shows
articles.body:
Live shows are rarely solo operations. On any given night, a show brings together a **Venue**, a **Promoter / Tour Manager**, a **Headliner**, and one or more **Support / Opener** bands. BandMath connects every party on the bill into a single shared event using a **6-Character Show Access Code**.

![Venue Settlement Hub](/doc-assets/fr/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/venue-settlement-hub.png)

---

## 1. Anyone Can Create the Show (100% Free)

You never need to wait on a specific person to set up the show in BandMath:
* **Bands:** Tap **`[ + CREATE EVENT ]`** inside the **Events** tab to create a show for your band or a multi-band bill.
* **Venues, Promoters & Tour Managers:** Tap **`[ + CREATE EVENT ]`** inside your 3-tab settlement hub to create the event on behalf of the house or tour package.

Creating an event, adding ticket tiers, inviting bands to the lineup, and running the **Closing Room** math is **100% free** for every account type.

---

## 2. The 6-Character Show Access Code (`[ JOIN SHOW ]`)

Every event in BandMath automatically generates a unique **6-Character Show Access Code** visible in the event details header.

### Joining as a Band (`Headliner`, `Co-Headliner`, `Support`, `Opener`)
When your band arrives at the venue (or when advancing the show weeks beforehand):
1. Open the **Events** tab and tap **`[ JOIN SHOW ]`**.
2. Enter the 6-character Show Access Code shared by the Venue, Promoter, Tour Manager, or originating Band.
3. Choose your billing role (`Headliner`, `Co-Headliner`, `Support`, or `Opener`) and optional stage time.

### Joining Mid-Show (Retroactive Merch & Split Sync)
Forgot to join the show code before doors opened? **No problem.** A band can join a show via **`[ JOIN SHOW ]`** at any time—even mid-show or right before walking into the settlement room:
* **Retroactive Merch Pickup:** BandMath automatically links any POS merchandise sales your band rang up during that day's **Event Merch Window** (`3:00 PM – 4:00 AM`) to your band's Show Call Sheet.
* **Dynamic Shared-Pot Rebalancing:** Any unsettled equal-split (`1/N`) shared show expenses or incomes automatically rebalance from `1/N` to `1/(N+1)` across the updated lineup without disturbing any items that were already marked settled.

### Unlocking as a Venue, Promoter, or Tour Manager
If a band created the event first, the Venue, Promoter, or Tour Manager can enter the exact same **6-Character Show Code** in their **Events** hub to unlock the show, ring up Door Tickets, scan fans in Bouncer Mode, and coordinate the Closing Room.

---

## 3. Run-of-Show Stage Times vs. The Event Merch Window

BandMath cleanly separates **when a band is on stage** from **when a band is selling merch**:

| Schedule Window | How It Works |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Run-of-Show Stage Slot** (`set_start_time` & `set_duration_minutes`) | Optional stage time (e.g., `8:15 PM · 45 mins`) displayed on the Show Call Sheet and linked to your [Setlist Organizer](/fr/docs/Features/Setlist_Organizer). |
| **Event Merch Window** (`3:00 PM – 4:00 AM`) | The shared full-night window during which every band on the bill sells merchandise at the venue. Your stage slot **never** restricts when your Merch Stand sales count toward the show! |

:::tip Next Step: Claiming Online Ticketing
Once your event is created, who processes the online pre-sale tickets? Read [Online Ticketing, First-Sale Lock & Promo Links](/fr/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links) to see how any connected merchant on the bill can claim online ticketing.
:::

articles.title: Online Ticketing, First-Sale Lock & Promoter Attribution Links
articles.body:
On DIY and independent tours, the person who creates the event on the calendar isn't always the merchant who holds the Stripe account for online ticket pre-sales. Sometimes the **Venue** sells the pre-sale tickets, sometimes the **Promoter / Tour Manager** runs the box office, and sometimes the **Headliner** handles ticketing for a local bill.

BandMath handles all three scenarios seamlessly with our **3-State Online Ticketing Claim** and automatic **Promoter Attribution Links**.

![Fan Ticketing WebCheckout](/doc-assets/fr/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/fan-ticketing-checkout.png)

---

## 1. The 3-State Online Ticketing Claim & First-Sale Lock (`🔒`)

Every event with ticket tiers moves through three clear states:

### State 1: Unclaimed (Free Setup)
Any free `Band`, `Venue`, `Promoter`, or `Tour Manager` account can create an event and configure ticket tiers, pricing, capacities, VIP promo codes, and the [Event Ticket Tax Rate](/fr/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Touring_Tax_and_Nightly_Settlements#tier-1-standardized-event-ticket-tax-rate) before a merchant is assigned.

### State 2: Claimed & Switchable (`0` Tickets Sold)
Any participant on the show with an active Merchant subscription and connected Stripe account—whether the **Venue**, the **Promoter**, the **Tour Manager**, or **any Band on the bill**—can tap **`[ CLAIM ONLINE TICKETING ]`**.
* As long as **`0` tickets have been sold**, the designated ticketing merchant can still be switched if the promoter and bands decide a different party should run the online box office.

### State 3: Permanently Locked on Ticket #1 (`🔒`)
The exact instant the **first online ticket is sold** (`total_sold >= 1`), BandMath triggers a permanent database lock (`🔒`):
* The online ticketing merchant can **no longer be changed** for that event.
* This guarantees that all online pre-sale funds, Stripe processing fees, and ticket tax set-asides remain 100% unified inside a single Merchant of Record account for clean nightly settlement.

:::danger Why Locking on Ticket #1 Matters
Splitting online pre-sales across multiple Stripe merchants mid-campaign creates a nightmare of fractured payouts, duplicate tax liabilities, and confused fan refund paths. Locking on Ticket #1 guarantees a single authoritative pre-sale pool at the Closing Table.
:::

---

## 2. Automatic Per-Band Promoter Attribution Links (`?ref=`)

When four bands share a bill, the promoter and bands almost always want to know: **"How many pre-sale tickets did each band actually bring in?"**

BandMath tracks this automatically without requiring separate ticket tiers for every band:
1. Open the event inside the BandMath app and tap **`[ Share Link ]`**.
2. BandMath automatically appends your active band's attribution tag (`?ref=<yourBandId>`) to both your shareable checkout URL and your downloadable **Promoter QR Flyer**.
3. Whenever a fan buys tickets through your link or scans your poster QR code, the sale is credited to your band's **Promoter Attribution Counter** right on the **Closing Table**—making it effortless to settle promoter bonuses or draw-based splits.

---

## 3. Fan / Street-Team Share Pass & Referral Leaderboard

Word of mouth is what fills independent rooms. Alongside band-level attribution, BandMath empowers your fans and street-team promoters to share the show and climb the **Event Referral Leaderboard**:

* **The Fan Share Pass:** After purchasing a ticket on the BandMath WebCheckout portal (or grabbing a promoter share pass), fans receive a personalized referral link and QR pass they can post to their stories or send to friends in group chats.
* **Live Referral Leaderboard:** Every ticket purchased through a fan or street-team promoter's referral link automatically increments their tally on the event's **Referral Leaderboard**—letting bands and venues reward their top street-team advocates with guest list upgrades, free merch at the stand, or VIP perks at the door.

articles.title: Door Ticket POS, QR Hardware Terminals & Bouncer Mode
articles.sidebarLabel: Door Terminals, Cash Drops & Bouncer Mode
articles.body:
Once doors open at a venue or festival, walk-up fans are buying **Door Tickets** while pre-sale ticket holders are getting their **QR Tickets** scanned. BandMath gives venues, promoters, tour managers, and bands a complete box-office hardware and door-staff ecosystem—without ever exposing private financial ledgers.

---

## 1. Multi-Custodian Door Ticket POS (`[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`)

At a live show, the person who ran online pre-sales isn't always the person sitting at the door with a cash box or phone terminal. Sometimes the **Venue** rings up door tickets, sometimes the **Tour Manager** runs the door, and sometimes a **Band** member sells walk-up tickets next to the merch table.

1. Any authorized participant on the show (**Venue**, **Promoter**, **Tour Manager**, or **Band**) can tap **`[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`** (or use the **Cart** tab in the 3-icon Venue/TM bar).
2. Select the ticket tier and ring up the fan via **[Tap to Pay](/fr/docs/Accept_Payments/Tap_to_Pay)** or **[Cash](/fr/docs/Accept_Payments/Accepting_Cash)**.
3. **Zero Cross-Merchant Bleed:** Whoever rings up the Door Ticket collects those funds directly into **their own Merchant Account or Cashbox**.
4. **Automatic Closing Table Netting:** In [The Closing Room](/fr/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room), BandMath breaks down `Door Tickets by Custodian` and automatically deducts whatever cash or card funds each party already collected at the door from their final **Net Closing Envelope** (while keeping the agreed [Event Ticket Tax Set-Aside](/fr/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Touring_Tax_and_Nightly_Settlements#tier-1-standardized-event-ticket-tax-rate) with the custodian who processed the sale).

---

## 2. QR Hardware Door Terminal Pairing ("The Box of 25 Phones")

Large venues and festivals often keep a fleet of dedicated box-office smartphones or iPads at the entrance. You shouldn't have to create 25 fake email accounts or type your master admin password onto staff devices.

![Terminal QR Pairing Sheet](/doc-assets/fr/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/terminal-qr-pairing-sheet.png)

### How Zero-Email QR Terminal Pairing Works
1. **Generate a Pairing QR Code:** In your main **Venue / Promoter User Settings**, open the **Hardware Door Terminals** panel and tap **Pair New Terminal** (e.g., `Terminal 1 — Sarah` or `Box Office East`).
2. **Scan from the Door Device:** On the hardware phone, tap **Pair as Door Terminal** on the login screen and scan the pairing QR code.
3. **Instant Scoped Provisioning:** The device is immediately bound to your Venue/Promoter merchant account in restricted **Door Terminal Mode**—ready to ring up door tickets via Tap to Pay or Cash and scan QR tickets, with zero access to admin settings or payout bank details.

---

## 3. Active Shift Float & End-of-Shift Cash Drop Reconciliation

When multiple box-office staff members work the door across a night, tracking physical cash tills is critical:

![End Shift Cash Drop Modal](/doc-assets/fr/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/end-shift-cash-drop-modal.png)

* **Starting Cash Float:** When a staff member opens a shift on a paired terminal (e.g., `Terminal 1 — Sarah`), they log their starting change float (e.g., `€100.00`).
* **Live Cash Accumulation:** Every cash door ticket rung up during their shift automatically increments their expected drawer total (e.g., `€100.00 Float + €320.00 Cash Sales = €420.00 Expected`).
* **End-of-Shift Cash Drop Modal:** When closing out their shift, the operator counts the physical cash envelope and submits the **End-of-Shift Cash Drop**. BandMath automatically flags any over/short variance and logs the verified cash drop directly into the night's box office settlement.

---

## 4. Bouncer Mode & The "Hand-Off" Safety Lock

### The Real-World Door Problem
At an independent club or DIY show, a Band Admin, Tour Manager, or Venue Operator often needs to hand their own smartphone to a hired door person or volunteer at the entrance to scan tickets for two hours—**without** letting that person snoop through band bank balances, member standings, or settlement numbers.

![Bouncer Scanner Live](/doc-assets/fr/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/bouncer-scanner-live.png)

### How the Bouncer Lock Solves It
1. Open the **Bouncer** tab (from the Event page or the 3-icon Venue/TM navigation bar).
2. Toggle on the **Bouncer Safety Lock** and hand your phone to your door staff.
3. While locked in **Bouncer Mode**, the screen is strictly restricted to:
   * **Live Camera QR Ticket Scanner:** Instant validation of fan QR tickets with clear visual and haptic feedback for valid check-ins, duplicate scans, or wrong-date tickets.
   * **Wrong-Date / Wrong-Show Guard:** If a fan presents a ticket for tomorrow night's show on a multi-night run, Bouncer Mode triggers an unmistakable **Wrong Show Date** alert showing the ticket's actual event date so door staff never let the wrong ticket through.
   * **Live Guest List & Manual Check-In:** Searchable guest list and ticket holder roster for fans whose phone battery died.
   * **Headcount Progress Bar:** Real-time `Checked In / Total Sold` counter.
4. **Authentication Required to Exit:** If the door person taps to exit Bouncer Mode or tries to switch back to `Standings`, `Home`, or `Settings`, BandMath requires **biometric / device authentication (Face ID, Touch ID, or Passcode)** before unlocking the rest of the app.

![Bouncer Wrong Show Date Guard](/doc-assets/fr/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/bouncer-wrong-show-date.png)

:::note Mobile Camera Requirement for Live QR Scanning
Live camera QR ticket scanning in **Bouncer Mode** is a native mobile app feature available on **iOS and Android**. On desktop web browsers, you can view and search the live Guest List and check in attendees manually.
:::

articles.title: The Multi-Band Closing Room & Nightly Settlement
articles.body:
At the end of the night, the back-office settlement shouldn't require a messy spreadsheet, three calculators, and scribbled paper napkins. BandMath's **Closing Room ("The Closing Table")** brings the Venue, Promoter, Tour Manager, and every Band on the bill into a live, mathematically verified Deal Sheet and settlement engine that connects directly to each band's internal Ledger.

![Closing Room Deal Sheet](/doc-assets/fr/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/closing-room-deal-sheet.png)

---

## 1. Shared Show Pot vs. Band-Specific Deal Sheet Items

In a multi-band settlement, some costs and revenues belong to the **entire show**, while others belong to a **single band** or the **house**:

### A. The Shared Show Pot (Dynamic Rebalancing)
The **Closing Officer** (the Tour Manager, Promoter, Venue, or originating/merchant Band) can log shared event incomes and expenses—such as a sound engineer fee, door security, shared backline rental, or a hospitality buyout—and split them across the bill by:
* **Equal Split (`1/N`):** Automatically divides the item equally across all bands on the bill (utilizing the [Penny Catcher](/fr/docs/Features/The_Penny_Catcher) so no cent is ever lost).
* **Custom Percentage (`%`):** Splits according to agreed deal percentages (e.g., `60% Headliner / 25% Support / 15% Opener`).
* **Fixed Amount (`€ / $`):** Assigns exact dollar/euro amounts per party.

:::tip Dynamic Mid-Show Rebalancing
If another band joins the bill via `[ JOIN SHOW ]` after shared items have already been entered, BandMath dynamically rebalances all unsettled `1/N` shared items to `1/(N+1)`—while strictly preserving any band rows that have already been marked settled (`is_settled = true`)!
:::

### B. Venue Merch Cuts & Two-Tier Tax Transparency
The standalone Venue Split Calculator is built right into each band's **Deal Sheet** inside the Closing Room:
* BandMath automatically pulls every band's POS merchandise sales rung up during the **Event Merch Window** (`3:00 PM – 4:00 AM`).
* Each band's declared **Merch Tax Rate** (and Stripe card processing fees) is backed out first so venue merch cuts (`15%–25%`) are calculated strictly on **Net Merch Revenue**—with the exact math printed right on the Deal Sheet (e.g., `15% of €228.77 (Net of 19% VAT & Stripe)`). For full details on EU & US tax math, see [Live Music Touring Tax & Nightly Settlements](/fr/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Touring_Tax_and_Nightly_Settlements).

---

## 2. Role-Scoped Privacy Views

Not everyone in the room needs to see another band's private buyout or internal finances:
* **Master / House View (Closing Officer, Tour Manager, Promoter & Venue):** Displays the complete box office summary, `Door Tickets by Custodian`, the Shared Show Pot, and the Net Closing Envelopes for every party on the show.
* **Band Privacy View:** Every participating band sees the transparent **Shared Show Pot** (ticket pool and shared show expenses) plus **only their own band's specific line items, merch totals, and payout envelope**—keeping other bands' private guarantees or side expenses confidential.

---

## 3. Net Closing Envelopes & Multi-Custodian Netting

Because tickets may have been sold online by one merchant and at the door by multiple custodians, BandMath calculates a final **Net Closing Envelope** for each band and the house:
* **Credits:** Your share of the Net Ticket Pool + any band guarantees/buyouts.
* **Less Deductions:** Your share of Shared Show Expenses + any Venue Merch Cut owed to the house + any **Door Ticket Cash/Card you already collected in your own POS** (net of the Ticket Tax set-aside you keep to pay the tax authority).

---

When a band is handed their payout envelope (or pays out their share of a venue expense), BandMath **never** silently dumps the money into a generic bucket.

When you tap **Settle** on your band's closing item, BandMath prompts you for explicit custody selection (supporting both single-method and **Split-Tender Cash + Bank Transfer** payouts):
1. **Payment Method:** Was it settled via **`Cash`**, **`Bank Transfer`**, or a **Split-Tender** combination of both?
2. **Received By / Paid Out By:** Who physically took custody of the cash or received the wire transfer?
   * **`Cashbox`** (your band's physical cash till)
   * **`Band Bank`** (your band's shared business checking account)
   * **A Specific Active Band Member (e.g., `John`)**

### Why This Is Magic for Touring Bands
Suppose the promoter hands your guitarist **John** a `€400` cash envelope at the end of the night, and John puts it in his jacket pocket so the band can hit the highway. When you select **`Cash` → Received By: `John`**, BandMath commits the settlement straight into your band's **Transaction Feed (`Home`)** and **Standings**:
* Every band member is credited their equal share of the `€400` show payout.
* John's personal balance is debited `€400` because he is holding the physical cash.
* Your band's [Automated Debt Settlement](/fr/docs/Features/The_Ledger#automated-debt-settlement) updates instantaneously—zero double-entry data entry required!

---

## 5. One-Tap Automated Final Closing Statement Emails

Once the numbers are settled, tap **`[ EMAIL FINAL CLOSING RECEIPTS ]`**:
* BandMath dispatches itemized, accountant-ready HTML closing statements to the **Venue**, the **Tour Manager / Promoter**, and **every Band on the bill**.
* Each email is strictly **privacy-scoped**: the Venue and Closing Officer receive the full Master/House statement, while each Band receives the Shared Show Pot breakdown alongside their own band's itemized settlement and payout confirmation.

articles.title: The Ledger
articles.body:
The Ledger is the core of BandMath. It is a double-entry accounting system tailored specifically for the complexities of touring bands.

## Transactions

Adding, modifying, and deleting transactions is simple. BandMath supports recording:

### Income
Anything from nightly venue payouts, to tips, to merch sales.

![Add Income](/doc-assets/fr/Features/assets/add-modify-and-delete-transactions_02.png)

### Expenses
Gas for the van, hotels, gear repairs, or just a round of beers at the bar.

![Add Expense](/doc-assets/fr/Features/assets/add-modify-and-delete-transactions_01.png)

### Transfers
Moving money between the Band Bank, VAT Bank, or individual members.

![Add Transfer](/doc-assets/fr/Features/assets/add-modify-and-delete-transactions_03.png)

### Modifying & Deleting
You have full editing capabilities to ensure the ledger is always perfectly accurate.

![Modify Transaction](/doc-assets/fr/Features/assets/shared-expenses-credits_01.png)

## Shared Expenses & Credits

Touring is a team effort. Anyone in the band can pay for an expense and automatically debit any combination of the other members. 

Similarly, anyone can take a payout (like the cash from the venue) and automatically credit the other members for their cut.

![Shared Expenses](/doc-assets/fr/Features/assets/shared-expenses-credits_02.png)

## Automated Debt Settlement

This is the magic of BandMath. Instead of creating a complex web of "who owes who" (e.g., the drummer owes the singer for gas, but the singer owes the guitarist for dinner), the algorithm analyzes the net balances of everyone in the band.

It outputs the absolute simplest way to settle all debts with the fewest number of cash transfers.

![Automated Debt Settlement](/doc-assets/fr/Features/assets/automated-debt-settlement_01.png)

## Advanced Profit Splitting (The Penny Catcher)

When an expense or income is split among multiple members, the division rarely works out to clean integers ($10.00 split 3 ways is $3.33333...). 

Our proprietary Penny Catcher algorithm ensures that fractions of a cent are never lost or infinitely rounded, guaranteeing that the ledger balances perfectly to the penny.

## Event Settlement & VAT Integration

Need to settle a multi-band show, calculate a venue merch cut, or split door tickets and shared show expenses? BandMath's [Closing Room](/fr/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room) handles the entire nightly settlement and commits your band's exact payout or expense share directly into the Ledger—letting you specify whether it was paid via **Cash** or **Bank Transfer** and whether it landed in the **Cash Box**, **Band Bank**, or a specific band member's pocket.

When you sell merch or log taxable income, the tax portion of the sale is automatically transferred to the **[VAT Bank](/fr/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank)**. This ensures you don't accidentally spend money that you owe to the government.

![Event Settlement & Ledger Sync](/doc-assets/fr/Features/assets/shared-expenses-credits_03.png)

articles.title: Merch Stand & The Merch Warehouse
articles.body:
BandMath provides a complete, touring-grade merchandise management and Point-of-Sale ecosystem built around two connected hubs: the **Merch Warehouse** (where you manage your catalog, categories, and stock) and the **Merch Stand** (where you ring up fans at the show).

## 1. The Merch Warehouse (Inventory & Catalog Hub)

Accessible directly from the **Shop** tab, the **Merch Warehouse** is your centralized backroom for organizing products before and during a tour:

* **Custom Categories & Merch Types:** Organize your catalog into clean categories—T-Shirts, Hoodies, Vinyl, Cassettes, Hats, Posters, Stickers, or any custom merch type your band dreams up.
* **Size & Variant Matrix:** Track independent stock counts across every apparel size (`XS`, `S`, `M`, `L`, `XL`, `XXL`, `3XL`) as well as non-sized items (`N/A`).
* **Historical Batch Cost Tracking:** Because the cost of pressing vinyl or screen-printing shirts changes from run to run, BandMath records the exact unit production cost of every inventory batch you add. That way, your profit splits and [Sales Analyzer](/fr/docs/Features/Sales_Analyzer) ROI metrics stay 100% historically accurate.
* **Low-Stock Visibility:** Spot depleted sizes before you load the van so you know exactly when to reorder with your printer.

## 2. The Merch Stand (Point-of-Sale System)

When the house lights come up and fifty fans rush the merch table at once, speed is everything:

* **Single-Tap Dynamic Cart:** Tap any item and size in the **Merch Stand** to drop it into your active **Cart**.
* **Atomic Inventory Reservation:** The instant an item is placed into an active cart, BandMath reserves that stock so two bandmates ringing up fans on separate phones can never accidentally double-sell the last Medium shirt.
* **Cash, Tap to Pay & Stripe QR Checkout:** Accept [Tap to Pay on iPhone & Android](/fr/docs/Accept_Payments/Tap_to_Pay), [Stripe QR Codes](/fr/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) (ideal for international tours), or [Physical Cash](/fr/docs/Accept_Payments/Accepting_Cash) with explicit cash custody tracking.
* **At-Cost Member Purchases, Discounts & Tips:** Toggle between **Retail** and **At Cost** for band member purchases, apply custom cart discounts, or log fan tips on the fly.
* **Customer Email Receipts:** Send digital receipts straight from the checkout screen.

![POS Checkout Cart](/doc-assets/fr/Features/assets/pos-checkout-cart.png)

## 3. Event Merch Window & Closing Room Integration

Every sale rung up in the **Merch Stand** during a show's **Event Merch Window** (`3:00 PM – 4:00 AM`) is automatically linked to that night's show in the [Multi-Band Closing Room](/fr/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room)—ready for net-of-tax, net-of-Stripe venue merch cut calculations without any manual spreadsheet tallying.

* **Atomic Inventory Reservation:** The instant an item is placed into an active cart, BandMath reserves that stock so two bandmates ringing up fans on separate phones can never accidentally double-sell the last Medium shirt.
* **Cash, Tap to Pay & Stripe QR Checkout:** Accept [Tap to Pay on iPhone & Android](/fr/docs/Accept_Payments/Tap_to_Pay), [Stripe QR Codes](/fr/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) (ideal for international tours), or [Physical Cash](/fr/docs/Accept_Payments/Accepting_Cash) with explicit cash custody tracking.
* **At-Cost Member Purchases, Discounts & Tips:** Toggle between **Retail** and **At Cost** for band member purchases, apply custom cart discounts, or log fan tips on the fly.
* **Customer Email Receipts:** Send digital receipts straight from the checkout screen.

![POS Checkout Cart](/doc-assets/fr/Features/assets/pos-checkout-cart.png)

sections.heading: 3. Event Merch Window & Closing Room Integration
sections.content: Every sale rung up in the **Merch Stand** during a show's **Event Merch Window** (`3:00 PM – 4:00 AM`) is automatically linked to that night's show in the [Multi-Band Closing Room](/fr/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room)—ready for net-of-tax, net-of-Stripe venue merch cut calculations without any manual spreadsheet tallying.

articles.title: The Sales Analyzer
articles.body:
Data is power. The Sales Analyzer is an advanced analytics suite available to Merch Stand subscribers. It provides deep insights into your inventory performance so you can make smarter decisions for the next tour.

![Sales Analyzer Dashboard](/doc-assets/fr/Features/assets/merch-analyzer-dashboard.png)

## Profit & ROI Tracking

Stop guessing which designs are actually making you money. The Sales Analyzer breaks down:
* Total revenue generated per item.
* Exact profit margins (factoring in historical production costs).
* Return on Investment (ROI) for specific merchandise runs.

## Restock Warnings

Never run out of your best sellers mid-tour. The Sales Analyzer tracks your average sales velocity and visually flags items that are running dangerously low on stock.

While this might be giving away some of our "secret sauce", we believe in full transparency so you can decide if you want to make purchasing decisions based on this model. Here is exactly how the restock warning algorithm works under the hood:

1. **Calculate the Timebox Duration:** First, the analyzer looks at the date range you've selected for the report. By default, the app automatically sets the **End Time** to right now, and the **Start Time** to 12 hours ago (which is perfect for analyzing a single night's sales). However, if you manually expand this to analyze a full tour, it will calculate exactly how many days you played a show during that selected timebox (e.g., 14 shows).
2. **Calculate Sales Velocity:** For every individual item and size, it takes the total quantity sold during that timebox and divides it by the number of shows played to get your **Per-Show Sales Velocity**. (e.g., If you sold 28 Large Tour Tees across 14 shows, your velocity is `2.0 / show`).
3. **Project Shows Remaining:** It then takes your current physical stock on hand for that item and divides it by the Per-Show Sales Velocity to predict exactly how many shows worth of inventory you have left. (e.g., If you have 4 Large Tour Tees left, and you're selling 2.0 a show, you have `2.0 shows` of stock remaining).
4. **The Trigger:** If the projection determines you have less than your customized **"Shows until stock alert"** threshold of stock remaining at your current sales velocity, it triggers an Actionable Warning in the UI, recommending that you restock.

## Trophy Awards

We've gamified merch sales! The Analyzer automatically awards trophies to your best-performing items (e.g., "Fastest Seller", "Highest Profit Margin"), so you can quickly identify the stars of your merch table at a glance.

articles.title: Inventory Analyzer
articles.body:
The **Inventory Analyzer** is a powerful built-in tool that provides deep insights into your current merchandise stock. Instead of just showing you a simple list of items, the analyzer automatically calculates the financial weight of your physical inventory, helping you make smarter decisions about reordering and capital allocation.

## Key Insights Provided

When you open the Inventory Analyzer, it immediately calculates a global summary of your entire merch spread:

* **Total Stock Value:** The total amount of money you paid to manufacture or purchase the items you currently have on hand. This tells you exactly how much capital is tied up in physical boxes.
* **Total Potential Profit:** The total amount of pure profit you stand to make once every single item in your current inventory is sold at its set retail price. 
* **Total Units:** A simple count of every physical item you have in stock across all categories.
* **Return on Investment (ROI):** A percentage metric showing your expected return. For example, a 150% ROI means if you spend $100 on merch, you will generate $150 in pure profit (walking away with $250 total). A 100% ROI means you are exactly doubling your money (spending $100 to make $100 in profit). A 0% ROI means you are breaking even.

## Breakdown by Category and Size

Below the high-level financial metrics, the analyzer provides a distribution breakdown:
* **Category Distribution:** A quick view of how your total units are distributed across categories (e.g., how many Shirts vs. Vinyls vs. Accessories).
* **Size Distribution:** A aggregated count of all apparel sizes currently in stock (e.g., 120 Mediums, 80 Larges). This is incredibly useful for spotting overall sizing trends and knowing what sizes you need to order more of globally.

## Item-Level Analysis

The bottom half of the analyzer breaks down your inventory design by design. 

For every specific item and size variation (e.g., "Tour Tee - Large"), the analyzer shows you:
* **Current Quantity**
* **Unit Cost vs Retail Price**
* **Stock Value:** How much capital is tied up in this specific size.
* **Potential Profit:** How much profit this specific size will generate.

This line-by-line breakdown allows you to instantly spot which items are your most valuable assets, and which slow-moving items are tying up your capital. 

## Quick Updates

The Inventory Analyzer isn't just for looking at data. If you spot a discrepancy or need to make a quick adjustment, simply **tap on any item row**. This will instantly slide up the **Update Quantity** sheet, allowing you to seamlessly adjust the stock level, unit cost, or retail price without having to navigate back to the main Merch Stand.
