articles.title: Online Ticketing, First-Sale Lock & Promoter Attribution Links
articles.body:
On DIY and independent tours, the person who creates the event on the calendar isn't always the merchant who holds the Stripe account for online ticket pre-sales. Sometimes the **Venue** sells the pre-sale tickets, sometimes the **Promoter / Tour Manager** runs the box office, and sometimes the **Headliner** handles ticketing for a local bill.

BandMath handles all three scenarios seamlessly with our **3-State Online Ticketing Claim** and automatic **Promoter Attribution Links**.

![Fan Ticketing WebCheckout](/doc-assets/es/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/fan-ticketing-checkout.png)

---

## 1. The 3-State Online Ticketing Claim & First-Sale Lock (`🔒`)

Every event with ticket tiers moves through three clear states:

### State 1: Unclaimed (Free Setup)
Any free `Band`, `Venue`, `Promoter`, or `Tour Manager` account can create an event and configure ticket tiers, pricing, capacities, VIP promo codes, and the [Event Ticket Tax Rate](/es/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Touring_Tax_and_Nightly_Settlements#tier-1-standardized-event-ticket-tax-rate) before a merchant is assigned.

### State 2: Claimed & Switchable (`0` Tickets Sold)
Any participant on the show with an active Merchant subscription and connected Stripe account—whether the **Venue**, the **Promoter**, the **Tour Manager**, or **any Band on the bill**—can tap **`[ CLAIM ONLINE TICKETING ]`**.
* As long as **`0` tickets have been sold**, the designated ticketing merchant can still be switched if the promoter and bands decide a different party should run the online box office.

### State 3: Permanently Locked on Ticket #1 (`🔒`)
The exact instant the **first online ticket is sold** (`total_sold >= 1`), BandMath triggers a permanent database lock (`🔒`):
* The online ticketing merchant can **no longer be changed** for that event.
* This guarantees that all online pre-sale funds, Stripe processing fees, and ticket tax set-asides remain 100% unified inside a single Merchant of Record account for clean nightly settlement.

:::danger Why Locking on Ticket #1 Matters
Splitting online pre-sales across multiple Stripe merchants mid-campaign creates a nightmare of fractured payouts, duplicate tax liabilities, and confused fan refund paths. Locking on Ticket #1 guarantees a single authoritative pre-sale pool at the Closing Table.
:::

---

## 2. Automatic Per-Band Promoter Attribution Links (`?ref=`)

When four bands share a bill, the promoter and bands almost always want to know: **"How many pre-sale tickets did each band actually bring in?"**

BandMath tracks this automatically without requiring separate ticket tiers for every band:
1. Open the event inside the BandMath app and tap **`[ Share Link ]`**.
2. BandMath automatically appends your active band's attribution tag (`?ref=<yourBandId>`) to both your shareable checkout URL and your downloadable **Promoter QR Flyer**.
3. Whenever a fan buys tickets through your link or scans your poster QR code, the sale is credited to your band's **Promoter Attribution Counter** right on the **Closing Table**—making it effortless to settle promoter bonuses or draw-based splits.

---

## 3. Fan / Street-Team Share Pass & Referral Leaderboard

Word of mouth is what fills independent rooms. Alongside band-level attribution, BandMath empowers your fans and street-team promoters to share the show and climb the **Event Referral Leaderboard**:

* **The Fan Share Pass:** After purchasing a ticket on the BandMath WebCheckout portal (or grabbing a promoter share pass), fans receive a personalized referral link and QR pass they can post to their stories or send to friends in group chats.
* **Live Referral Leaderboard:** Every ticket purchased through a fan or street-team promoter's referral link automatically increments their tally on the event's **Referral Leaderboard**—letting bands and venues reward their top street-team advocates with guest list upgrades, free merch at the stand, or VIP perks at the door.

articles.title: Door Ticket POS, QR Hardware Terminals & Bouncer Mode
articles.sidebarLabel: Door Terminals, Cash Drops & Bouncer Mode
articles.body:
Once doors open at a venue or festival, walk-up fans are buying **Door Tickets** while pre-sale ticket holders are getting their **QR Tickets** scanned. BandMath gives venues, promoters, tour managers, and bands a complete box-office hardware and door-staff ecosystem—without ever exposing private financial ledgers.

---

## 1. Multi-Custodian Door Ticket POS (`[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`)

At a live show, the person who ran online pre-sales isn't always the person sitting at the door with a cash box or phone terminal. Sometimes the **Venue** rings up door tickets, sometimes the **Tour Manager** runs the door, and sometimes a **Band** member sells walk-up tickets next to the merch table.

1. Any authorized participant on the show (**Venue**, **Promoter**, **Tour Manager**, or **Band**) can tap **`[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`** (or use the **Cart** tab in the 3-icon Venue/TM bar).
2. Select the ticket tier and ring up the fan via **[Tap to Pay](/es/docs/Accept_Payments/Tap_to_Pay)** or **[Cash](/es/docs/Accept_Payments/Accepting_Cash)**.
3. **Zero Cross-Merchant Bleed:** Whoever rings up the Door Ticket collects those funds directly into **their own Merchant Account or Cashbox**.
4. **Automatic Closing Table Netting:** In [The Closing Room](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room), BandMath breaks down `Door Tickets by Custodian` and automatically deducts whatever cash or card funds each party already collected at the door from their final **Net Closing Envelope** (while keeping the agreed [Event Ticket Tax Set-Aside](/es/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Touring_Tax_and_Nightly_Settlements#tier-1-standardized-event-ticket-tax-rate) with the custodian who processed the sale).

---

## 2. QR Hardware Door Terminal Pairing ("The Box of 25 Phones")

Large venues and festivals often keep a fleet of dedicated box-office smartphones or iPads at the entrance. You shouldn't have to create 25 fake email accounts or type your master admin password onto staff devices.

![Terminal QR Pairing Sheet](/doc-assets/es/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/terminal-qr-pairing-sheet.png)

### How Zero-Email QR Terminal Pairing Works
1. **Generate a Pairing QR Code:** In your main **Venue / Promoter User Settings**, open the **Hardware Door Terminals** panel and tap **Pair New Terminal** (e.g., `Terminal 1 — Sarah` or `Box Office East`).
2. **Scan from the Door Device:** On the hardware phone, tap **Pair as Door Terminal** on the login screen and scan the pairing QR code.
3. **Instant Scoped Provisioning:** The device is immediately bound to your Venue/Promoter merchant account in restricted **Door Terminal Mode**—ready to ring up door tickets via Tap to Pay or Cash and scan QR tickets, with zero access to admin settings or payout bank details.

---

## 3. Active Shift Float & End-of-Shift Cash Drop Reconciliation

When multiple box-office staff members work the door across a night, tracking physical cash tills is critical:

![End Shift Cash Drop Modal](/doc-assets/es/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/end-shift-cash-drop-modal.png)

* **Starting Cash Float:** When a staff member opens a shift on a paired terminal (e.g., `Terminal 1 — Sarah`), they log their starting change float (e.g., `€100.00`).
* **Live Cash Accumulation:** Every cash door ticket rung up during their shift automatically increments their expected drawer total (e.g., `€100.00 Float + €320.00 Cash Sales = €420.00 Expected`).
* **End-of-Shift Cash Drop Modal:** When closing out their shift, the operator counts the physical cash envelope and submits the **End-of-Shift Cash Drop**. BandMath automatically flags any over/short variance and logs the verified cash drop directly into the night's box office settlement.

---

## 4. Bouncer Mode & The "Hand-Off" Safety Lock

### The Real-World Door Problem
At an independent club or DIY show, a Band Admin, Tour Manager, or Venue Operator often needs to hand their own smartphone to a hired door person or volunteer at the entrance to scan tickets for two hours—**without** letting that person snoop through band bank balances, member standings, or settlement numbers.

![Bouncer Scanner Live](/doc-assets/es/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/bouncer-scanner-live.png)

### How the Bouncer Lock Solves It
1. Open the **Bouncer** tab (from the Event page or the 3-icon Venue/TM navigation bar).
2. Toggle on the **Bouncer Safety Lock** and hand your phone to your door staff.
3. While locked in **Bouncer Mode**, the screen is strictly restricted to:
   * **Live Camera QR Ticket Scanner:** Instant validation of fan QR tickets with clear visual and haptic feedback for valid check-ins, duplicate scans, or wrong-date tickets.
   * **Wrong-Date / Wrong-Show Guard:** If a fan presents a ticket for tomorrow night's show on a multi-night run, Bouncer Mode triggers an unmistakable **Wrong Show Date** alert showing the ticket's actual event date so door staff never let the wrong ticket through.
   * **Live Guest List & Manual Check-In:** Searchable guest list and ticket holder roster for fans whose phone battery died.
   * **Headcount Progress Bar:** Real-time `Checked In / Total Sold` counter.
4. **Authentication Required to Exit:** If the door person taps to exit Bouncer Mode or tries to switch back to `Standings`, `Home`, or `Settings`, BandMath requires **biometric / device authentication (Face ID, Touch ID, or Passcode)** before unlocking the rest of the app.

![Bouncer Wrong Show Date Guard](/doc-assets/es/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/bouncer-wrong-show-date.png)

:::note Mobile Camera Requirement for Live QR Scanning
Live camera QR ticket scanning in **Bouncer Mode** is a native mobile app feature available on **iOS and Android**. On desktop web browsers, you can view and search the live Guest List and check in attendees manually.
:::

Large venues and festivals often keep a fleet of dedicated box-office smartphones or iPads at the entrance. You shouldn't have to create 25 fake email accounts or type your master admin password onto staff devices.

![Terminal QR Pairing Sheet](/doc-assets/es/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/terminal-qr-pairing-sheet.png)

screenshots.sectionTitle: 2. QR Hardware Door Terminal Pairing ("The Box of 25 Phones")

sections.heading: How Zero-Email QR Terminal Pairing Works
sections.content:
1. **Generate a Pairing QR Code:** In your main **Venue / Promoter User Settings**, open the **Hardware Door Terminals** panel and tap **Pair New Terminal** (e.g., `Terminal 1 — Sarah` or `Box Office East`).
2. **Scan from the Door Device:** On the hardware phone, tap **Pair as Door Terminal** on the login screen and scan the pairing QR code.
3. **Instant Scoped Provisioning:** The device is immediately bound to your Venue/Promoter merchant account in restricted **Door Terminal Mode**—ready to ring up door tickets via Tap to Pay or Cash and scan QR tickets, with zero access to admin settings or payout bank details.

---

sections.heading: 3. Active Shift Float & End-of-Shift Cash Drop Reconciliation
sections.content:
When multiple box-office staff members work the door across a night, tracking physical cash tills is critical:

![End Shift Cash Drop Modal](/doc-assets/es/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/end-shift-cash-drop-modal.png)

* **Starting Cash Float:** When a staff member opens a shift on a paired terminal (e.g., `Terminal 1 — Sarah`), they log their starting change float (e.g., `€100.00`).
* **Live Cash Accumulation:** Every cash door ticket rung up during their shift automatically increments their expected drawer total (e.g., `€100.00 Float + €320.00 Cash Sales = €420.00 Expected`).
* **End-of-Shift Cash Drop Modal:** When closing out their shift, the operator counts the physical cash envelope and submits the **End-of-Shift Cash Drop**. BandMath automatically flags any over/short variance and logs the verified cash drop directly into the night's box office settlement.

---

screenshots.sectionTitle: 3. Active Shift Float & End-of-Shift Cash Drop Reconciliation

sections.heading: The Real-World Door Problem
sections.content:
At an independent club or DIY show, a Band Admin, Tour Manager, or Venue Operator often needs to hand their own smartphone to a hired door person or volunteer at the entrance to scan tickets for two hours—**without** letting that person snoop through band bank balances, member standings, or settlement numbers.

![Bouncer Scanner Live](/doc-assets/es/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/bouncer-scanner-live.png)

sections.heading: How the Bouncer Lock Solves It
sections.content:
1. Open the **Bouncer** tab (from the Event page or the 3-icon Venue/TM navigation bar).
2. Toggle on the **Bouncer Safety Lock** and hand your phone to your door staff.
3. While locked in **Bouncer Mode**, the screen is strictly restricted to:
   * **Live Camera QR Ticket Scanner:** Instant validation of fan QR tickets with clear visual and haptic feedback for valid check-ins, duplicate scans, or wrong-date tickets.
   * **Wrong-Date / Wrong-Show Guard:** If a fan presents a ticket for tomorrow night's show on a multi-night run, Bouncer Mode triggers an unmistakable **Wrong Show Date** alert showing the ticket's actual event date so door staff never let the wrong ticket through.
   * **Live Guest List & Manual Check-In:** Searchable guest list and ticket holder roster for fans whose phone battery died.
   * **Headcount Progress Bar:** Real-time `Checked In / Total Sold` counter.
4. **Authentication Required to Exit:** If the door person taps to exit Bouncer Mode or tries to switch back to `Standings`, `Home`, or `Settings`, BandMath requires **biometric / device authentication (Face ID, Touch ID, or Passcode)** before unlocking the rest of the app.

![Bouncer Wrong Show Date Guard](/doc-assets/es/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/bouncer-wrong-show-date.png)

:::note Mobile Camera Requirement for Live QR Scanning
Live camera QR ticket scanning in **Bouncer Mode** is a native mobile app feature available on **iOS and Android**. On desktop web browsers, you can view and search the live Guest List and check in attendees manually.
:::

articles.title: The Multi-Band Closing Room & Nightly Settlement
articles.body:
At the end of the night, the back-office settlement shouldn't require a messy spreadsheet, three calculators, and scribbled paper napkins. BandMath's **Closing Room ("The Closing Table")** brings the Venue, Promoter, Tour Manager, and every Band on the bill into a live, mathematically verified Deal Sheet and settlement engine that connects directly to each band's internal Ledger.

![Closing Room Deal Sheet](/doc-assets/es/Events_and_Closing_Room/assets/closing-room-deal-sheet.png)

---

## 1. Shared Show Pot vs. Band-Specific Deal Sheet Items

In a multi-band settlement, some costs and revenues belong to the **entire show**, while others belong to a **single band** or the **house**:

### A. The Shared Show Pot (Dynamic Rebalancing)
The **Closing Officer** (the Tour Manager, Promoter, Venue, or originating/merchant Band) can log shared event incomes and expenses—such as a sound engineer fee, door security, shared backline rental, or a hospitality buyout—and split them across the bill by:
* **Equal Split (`1/N`):** Automatically divides the item equally across all bands on the bill (utilizing the [Penny Catcher](/es/docs/Features/The_Penny_Catcher) so no cent is ever lost).
* **Custom Percentage (`%`):** Splits according to agreed deal percentages (e.g., `60% Headliner / 25% Support / 15% Opener`).
* **Fixed Amount (`€ / $`):** Assigns exact dollar/euro amounts per party.

:::tip Dynamic Mid-Show Rebalancing
If another band joins the bill via `[ JOIN SHOW ]` after shared items have already been entered, BandMath dynamically rebalances all unsettled `1/N` shared items to `1/(N+1)`—while strictly preserving any band rows that have already been marked settled (`is_settled = true`)!
:::

### B. Venue Merch Cuts & Two-Tier Tax Transparency
The standalone Venue Split Calculator is built right into each band's **Deal Sheet** inside the Closing Room:
* BandMath automatically pulls every band's POS merchandise sales rung up during the **Event Merch Window** (`3:00 PM – 4:00 AM`).
* Each band's declared **Merch Tax Rate** (and Stripe card processing fees) is backed out first so venue merch cuts (`15%–25%`) are calculated strictly on **Net Merch Revenue**—with the exact math printed right on the Deal Sheet (e.g., `15% of €228.77 (Net of 19% VAT & Stripe)`). For full details on EU & US tax math, see [Live Music Touring Tax & Nightly Settlements](/es/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Touring_Tax_and_Nightly_Settlements).

---

## 2. Role-Scoped Privacy Views

Not everyone in the room needs to see another band's private buyout or internal finances:
* **Master / House View (Closing Officer, Tour Manager, Promoter & Venue):** Displays the complete box office summary, `Door Tickets by Custodian`, the Shared Show Pot, and the Net Closing Envelopes for every party on the show.
* **Band Privacy View:** Every participating band sees the transparent **Shared Show Pot** (ticket pool and shared show expenses) plus **only their own band's specific line items, merch totals, and payout envelope**—keeping other bands' private guarantees or side expenses confidential.

---

## 3. Net Closing Envelopes & Multi-Custodian Netting

Because tickets may have been sold online by one merchant and at the door by multiple custodians, BandMath calculates a final **Net Closing Envelope** for each band and the house:
* **Credits:** Your share of the Net Ticket Pool + any band guarantees/buyouts.
* **Less Deductions:** Your share of Shared Show Expenses + any Venue Merch Cut owed to the house + any **Door Ticket Cash/Card you already collected in your own POS** (net of the Ticket Tax set-aside you keep to pay the tax authority).

---

## 4. Granular Settlement-to-Ledger Commits (Including Split-Tender)

When a band is handed their payout envelope (or pays out their share of a venue expense), BandMath **never** silently dumps the money into a generic bucket.

When you tap **Settle** on your band's closing item, BandMath prompts you for explicit custody selection (supporting both single-method and **Split-Tender Cash + Bank Transfer** payouts):
1. **Payment Method:** Was it settled via **`Cash`**, **`Bank Transfer`**, or a **Split-Tender** combination of both?
2. **Received By / Paid Out By:** Who physically took custody of the cash or received the wire transfer?
   * **`Cashbox`** (your band's physical cash till)
   * **`Band Bank`** (your band's shared business checking account)
   * **A Specific Active Band Member (e.g., `John`)**

### Why This Is Magic for Touring Bands
Suppose the promoter hands your guitarist **John** a `€400` cash envelope at the end of the night, and John puts it in his jacket pocket so the band can hit the highway. When you select **`Cash` → Received By: `John`**, BandMath commits the settlement straight into your band's **Transaction Feed (`Home`)** and **Standings**:
* Every band member is credited their equal share of the `€400` show payout.
* John's personal balance is debited `€400` because he is holding the physical cash.
* Your band's [Automated Debt Settlement](/es/docs/Features/The_Ledger#automated-debt-settlement) updates instantaneously—zero double-entry data entry required!

---

## 5. One-Tap Automated Final Closing Statement Emails

Once the numbers are settled, tap **`[ EMAIL FINAL CLOSING RECEIPTS ]`**:
* BandMath dispatches itemized, accountant-ready HTML closing statements to the **Venue**, the **Tour Manager / Promoter**, and **every Band on the bill**.
* Each email is strictly **privacy-scoped**: the Venue and Closing Officer receive the full Master/House statement, while each Band receives the Shared Show Pot breakdown alongside their own band's itemized settlement and payout confirmation.

articles.title: The Ledger
articles.body:
The Ledger is the core of BandMath. It is a double-entry accounting system tailored specifically for the complexities of touring bands.

## Transactions

Adding, modifying, and deleting transactions is simple. BandMath supports recording:

### Income
Anything from nightly venue payouts, to tips, to merch sales.

![Add Income](/doc-assets/es/Features/assets/add-modify-and-delete-transactions_02.png)

### Expenses
Gas for the van, hotels, gear repairs, or just a round of beers at the bar.

![Add Expense](/doc-assets/es/Features/assets/add-modify-and-delete-transactions_01.png)

### Transfers
Moving money between the Band Bank, VAT Bank, or individual members.

![Add Transfer](/doc-assets/es/Features/assets/add-modify-and-delete-transactions_03.png)

### Modifying & Deleting
You have full editing capabilities to ensure the ledger is always perfectly accurate.

![Modify Transaction](/doc-assets/es/Features/assets/shared-expenses-credits_01.png)

## Shared Expenses & Credits

Touring is a team effort. Anyone in the band can pay for an expense and automatically debit any combination of the other members. 

Similarly, anyone can take a payout (like the cash from the venue) and automatically credit the other members for their cut.

![Shared Expenses](/doc-assets/es/Features/assets/shared-expenses-credits_02.png)

## Automated Debt Settlement

This is the magic of BandMath. Instead of creating a complex web of "who owes who" (e.g., the drummer owes the singer for gas, but the singer owes the guitarist for dinner), the algorithm analyzes the net balances of everyone in the band.

It outputs the absolute simplest way to settle all debts with the fewest number of cash transfers.

![Automated Debt Settlement](/doc-assets/es/Features/assets/automated-debt-settlement_01.png)

## Advanced Profit Splitting (The Penny Catcher)

When an expense or income is split among multiple members, the division rarely works out to clean integers ($10.00 split 3 ways is $3.33333...). 

Our proprietary Penny Catcher algorithm ensures that fractions of a cent are never lost or infinitely rounded, guaranteeing that the ledger balances perfectly to the penny.

## Event Settlement & VAT Integration

Need to settle a multi-band show, calculate a venue merch cut, or split door tickets and shared show expenses? BandMath's [Closing Room](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room) handles the entire nightly settlement and commits your band's exact payout or expense share directly into the Ledger—letting you specify whether it was paid via **Cash** or **Bank Transfer** and whether it landed in the **Cash Box**, **Band Bank**, or a specific band member's pocket.

When you sell merch or log taxable income, the tax portion of the sale is automatically transferred to the **[VAT Bank](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank)**. This ensures you don't accidentally spend money that you owe to the government.

![Event Settlement & Ledger Sync](/doc-assets/es/Features/assets/shared-expenses-credits_03.png)

articles.title: Merch Stand & The Merch Warehouse
articles.body:
BandMath provides a complete, touring-grade merchandise management and Point-of-Sale ecosystem built around two connected hubs: the **Merch Warehouse** (where you manage your catalog, categories, and stock) and the **Merch Stand** (where you ring up fans at the show).

## 1. The Merch Warehouse (Inventory & Catalog Hub)

Accessible directly from the **Shop** tab, the **Merch Warehouse** is your centralized backroom for organizing products before and during a tour:

* **Custom Categories & Merch Types:** Organize your catalog into clean categories—T-Shirts, Hoodies, Vinyl, Cassettes, Hats, Posters, Stickers, or any custom merch type your band dreams up.
* **Size & Variant Matrix:** Track independent stock counts across every apparel size (`XS`, `S`, `M`, `L`, `XL`, `XXL`, `3XL`) as well as non-sized items (`N/A`).
* **Historical Batch Cost Tracking:** Because the cost of pressing vinyl or screen-printing shirts changes from run to run, BandMath records the exact unit production cost of every inventory batch you add. That way, your profit splits and [Sales Analyzer](/es/docs/Features/Sales_Analyzer) ROI metrics stay 100% historically accurate.
* **Low-Stock Visibility:** Spot depleted sizes before you load the van so you know exactly when to reorder with your printer.

## 2. The Merch Stand (Point-of-Sale System)

When the house lights come up and fifty fans rush the merch table at once, speed is everything:

* **Single-Tap Dynamic Cart:** Tap any item and size in the **Merch Stand** to drop it into your active **Cart**.
* **Atomic Inventory Reservation:** The instant an item is placed into an active cart, BandMath reserves that stock so two bandmates ringing up fans on separate phones can never accidentally double-sell the last Medium shirt.
* **Cash, Tap to Pay & Stripe QR Checkout:** Accept [Tap to Pay on iPhone & Android](/es/docs/Accept_Payments/Tap_to_Pay), [Stripe QR Codes](/es/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) (ideal for international tours), or [Physical Cash](/es/docs/Accept_Payments/Accepting_Cash) with explicit cash custody tracking.
* **At-Cost Member Purchases, Discounts & Tips:** Toggle between **Retail** and **At Cost** for band member purchases, apply custom cart discounts, or log fan tips on the fly.
* **Customer Email Receipts:** Send digital receipts straight from the checkout screen.

![POS Checkout Cart](/doc-assets/es/Features/assets/pos-checkout-cart.png)

## 3. Event Merch Window & Closing Room Integration

Every sale rung up in the **Merch Stand** during a show's **Event Merch Window** (`3:00 PM – 4:00 AM`) is automatically linked to that night's show in the [Multi-Band Closing Room](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room)—ready for net-of-tax, net-of-Stripe venue merch cut calculations without any manual spreadsheet tallying.

articles.title: The Sales Analyzer
articles.body:
Data is power. The Sales Analyzer is an advanced analytics suite available to Merch Stand subscribers. It provides deep insights into your inventory performance so you can make smarter decisions for the next tour.

![Sales Analyzer Dashboard](/doc-assets/es/Features/assets/merch-analyzer-dashboard.png)

## Profit & ROI Tracking

Stop guessing which designs are actually making you money. The Sales Analyzer breaks down:
* Total revenue generated per item.
* Exact profit margins (factoring in historical production costs).
* Return on Investment (ROI) for specific merchandise runs.

## Restock Warnings

Never run out of your best sellers mid-tour. The Sales Analyzer tracks your average sales velocity and visually flags items that are running dangerously low on stock.

While this might be giving away some of our "secret sauce", we believe in full transparency so you can decide if you want to make purchasing decisions based on this model. Here is exactly how the restock warning algorithm works under the hood:

1. **Calculate the Timebox Duration:** First, the analyzer looks at the date range you've selected for the report. By default, the app automatically sets the **End Time** to right now, and the **Start Time** to 12 hours ago (which is perfect for analyzing a single night's sales). However, if you manually expand this to analyze a full tour, it will calculate exactly how many days you played a show during that selected timebox (e.g., 14 shows).
2. **Calculate Sales Velocity:** For every individual item and size, it takes the total quantity sold during that timebox and divides it by the number of shows played to get your **Per-Show Sales Velocity**. (e.g., If you sold 28 Large Tour Tees across 14 shows, your velocity is `2.0 / show`).
3. **Project Shows Remaining:** It then takes your current physical stock on hand for that item and divides it by the Per-Show Sales Velocity to predict exactly how many shows worth of inventory you have left. (e.g., If you have 4 Large Tour Tees left, and you're selling 2.0 a show, you have `2.0 shows` of stock remaining).
4. **The Trigger:** If the projection determines you have less than your customized **"Shows until stock alert"** threshold of stock remaining at your current sales velocity, it triggers an Actionable Warning in the UI, recommending that you restock.

## Trophy Awards

We've gamified merch sales! The Analyzer automatically awards trophies to your best-performing items (e.g., "Fastest Seller", "Highest Profit Margin"), so you can quickly identify the stars of your merch table at a glance.

articles.title: Inventory Analyzer
articles.body:
The **Inventory Analyzer** is a powerful built-in tool that provides deep insights into your current merchandise stock. Instead of just showing you a simple list of items, the analyzer automatically calculates the financial weight of your physical inventory, helping you make smarter decisions about reordering and capital allocation.

## Key Insights Provided

When you open the Inventory Analyzer, it immediately calculates a global summary of your entire merch spread:

* **Total Stock Value:** The total amount of money you paid to manufacture or purchase the items you currently have on hand. This tells you exactly how much capital is tied up in physical boxes.
* **Total Potential Profit:** The total amount of pure profit you stand to make once every single item in your current inventory is sold at its set retail price. 
* **Total Units:** A simple count of every physical item you have in stock across all categories.
* **Return on Investment (ROI):** A percentage metric showing your expected return. For example, a 150% ROI means if you spend $100 on merch, you will generate $150 in pure profit (walking away with $250 total). A 100% ROI means you are exactly doubling your money (spending $100 to make $100 in profit). A 0% ROI means you are breaking even.

## Breakdown by Category and Size

Below the high-level financial metrics, the analyzer provides a distribution breakdown:
* **Category Distribution:** A quick view of how your total units are distributed across categories (e.g., how many Shirts vs. Vinyls vs. Accessories).
* **Size Distribution:** A aggregated count of all apparel sizes currently in stock (e.g., 120 Mediums, 80 Larges). This is incredibly useful for spotting overall sizing trends and knowing what sizes you need to order more of globally.

## Item-Level Analysis

The bottom half of the analyzer breaks down your inventory design by design. 

For every specific item and size variation (e.g., "Tour Tee - Large"), the analyzer shows you:
* **Current Quantity**
* **Unit Cost vs Retail Price**
* **Stock Value:** How much capital is tied up in this specific size.
* **Potential Profit:** How much profit this specific size will generate.

This line-by-line breakdown allows you to instantly spot which items are your most valuable assets, and which slow-moving items are tying up your capital. 

## Quick Updates

The Inventory Analyzer isn't just for looking at data. If you spot a discrepancy or need to make a quick adjustment, simply **tap on any item row**. This will instantly slide up the **Update Quantity** sheet, allowing you to seamlessly adjust the stock level, unit cost, or retail price without having to navigate back to the main Merch Stand.

articles.title: The Setlist Organizer
articles.body:
Great tours run on tight sets. Built directly into your band workspace alongside your shows and calendar, BandMath's **Setlist Organizer** lets your band build a reusable song catalog, craft show-specific setlists, and time your performance down to the minute.

---

## 1. Building Your Master Song Catalog

Instead of typing out song titles from scratch before every gig, you maintain a central **Song Catalog** for your band:
* **Song Details:** Store each song's title, duration (`mm:ss`), musical key, tempo (BPM), tuning notes, and transition cues (e.g., *Segues directly into Track 4* or *Capo 2*).
* **Shared Across the Band:** Every member of your band has live access to the updated catalog on their own phone.

---

## 2. Crafting & Reordering Show Setlists

Whether you are playing a 30-minute festival opener slot or a 90-minute headlining set, you can build custom setlists and link them directly to upcoming shows on your [Band Calendar](/es/docs/Features/Band_Calendar_and_Events):

1. **Add Songs from Your Catalog:** Tap songs from your master catalog to drop them into the setlist, or add one-off covers, medleys, and stage banter/tuning breaks.
2. **Drag-and-Drop Reordering:** Audition different set flows by dragging songs up or down the list.
3. **Encore & Set Dividers:** Group songs into main set and encore blocks so the pacing is crystal clear on stage.

---

## 3. Automatic Runtime vs. Stage Slot Timing

Curfew penalties at venues are real. As you add, remove, or reorder songs in a setlist, BandMath automatically calculates your **Total Set Duration**:
* **Live Runtime Tally:** See your cumulative music runtime updated instantaneously as you tweak the order.
* **Stage Slot Comparison:** When your band is assigned a **Run-of-Show Stage Time** (`set_start_time` and `set_duration_minutes`, such as a `45-minute` support slot) on an Event, you can immediately see whether your setlist leaves enough breathing room for tuning and stage transitions before your changeover.

:::tip Stage Times Never Restrict Your Merch Table
Setting a `45-minute` stage slot (`8:00 PM – 8:45 PM`) on a show helps everyone stay on schedule for the Run of Show and Setlist Organizer, while your band's **Event Merch Window** remains open across the full show day (`3:00 PM – 4:00 AM`) so every shirt sold before doors or after the headliner counts toward your show summary.
:::

articles.title: The Penny Catcher Algorithm
articles.body:
Accounting software is only as good as its ability to balance a ledger. While most apps handle basic arithmetic fine, they often fall apart when dealing with uneven splits and fractions of a cent, leading to ledgers that are perpetually off by $0.01 or $0.02. 

BandMath solves this using our proprietary **Penny Catcher Algorithm**.

## The Problem with Percentages

Imagine your band has 3 members with an equal 33.33% profit split. 

You sell a CD for $10.00. 
* Member A gets $3.333333...
* Member B gets $3.333333...
* Member C gets $3.333333...

Because physical currency cannot be divided into thirds of a cent, traditional spreadsheet formulas will round these numbers down to $3.33 each. 

However, $3.33 + $3.33 + $3.33 = $9.99. 

Where did the remaining $0.01 go? In a standard spreadsheet, that penny is completely lost. Over the course of a 30-date tour with thousands of transactions, these lost pennies snowball, causing the digital ledger to drift away from the actual amount of physical cash in the bank account. 

## How the Penny Catcher Works

BandMath never drops remainders. When an uneven split occurs, the Penny Catcher algorithm intercepts the fractional remainder before it can be lost.

It then algorithmically assigns that stray penny to a band member to ensure the transaction balances perfectly to the exact cent.

1. **Transaction 1 ($10.00 split 3 ways):**
   * Member A receives: $3.34 (Penny Catcher awards the extra cent here)
   * Member B receives: $3.33
   * Member C receives: $3.33
   * *Total: $10.00*

2. **Transaction 2 ($10.00 split 3 ways):**
   * Member A receives: $3.33 
   * Member B receives: $3.34 (Penny Catcher awards the extra cent here)
   * Member C receives: $3.33
   * *Total: $10.00*

articles.plainText:
The Penny Catcher Algorithm

Accounting software is only as good as its ability to balance a ledger. While most apps handle basic arithmetic fine, they often fall apart when dealing with uneven splits and fractions of a cent, leading to ledgers that are perpetually off by $0.01 or $0.02. 

BandMath solves this using our proprietary Penny Catcher Algorithm.

 The Problem with Percentages

Imagine your band has 3 members with an equal 33.33% profit split. 

You sell a CD for $10.00. 
 Member A gets $3.333333...
 Member B gets $3.333333...
 Member C gets $3.333333...

Because physical currency cannot be divided into thirds of a cent, traditional spreadsheet formulas will round these numbers down to $3.33 each. 

However, $3.33 + $3.33 + $3.33 = $9.99. 

Where did the remaining $0.01 go? In a standard spreadsheet, that penny is completely lost. Over the course of a 30-date tour with thousands of transactions, these lost pennies snowball, causing the digital ledger to drift away from the actual amount of physical cash in the bank account. 

 How the Penny Catcher Works

BandMath never drops remainders. When an uneven split occurs, the Penny Catcher algorithm intercepts the fractional remainder before it can be lost.

It then algorithmically assigns that stray penny to a band member to ensure the transaction balances perfectly to the exact cent.

1. Transaction 1 ($10.00 split 3 ways):
    Member A receives: $3.34 (Penny Catcher awards the extra cent here)
    Member B receives: $3.33
    Member C receives: $3.33
    Total: $10.00

2. Transaction 2 ($10.00 split 3 ways):
    Member A receives: $3.33 
    Member B receives: $3.34 (Penny Catcher awards the extra cent here)
    Member C receives: $3.33
    Total: $10.00

By acting in a round-robin fashion, the algorithm ensures that the ledger remains mathematically perfect, while ensuring that the distribution of those fractional pennies remains completely fair and balanced among the band members over time.

articles.title: Data Exports
articles.body:
We believe your data belongs to you. BandMath makes it easy to export your information for accounting, marketing, or personal archives.

## Ledger Export to CSV

Need to send your financial records to an accountant for tax season? 
You can export your entire ledger to a detailed CSV file. The export includes every transaction, the exact date, the payer, the receivers, and the calculated balances.

![Data Exports Screen](/doc-assets/es/Features/assets/data-exports-screen.png)

## Email Contact List Export

If you've been using the POS system to capture customer emails at the merch table, you can easily export this list. 

The exported CSV is perfectly formatted to be imported into any major email marketing platform (like Mailchimp or Klaviyo), allowing you to seamlessly market your next tour or album release to your most loyal fans.

articles.title: Events Dashboard & Band Calendar
articles.body:
Tour routing, rehearsal schedules, studio lockouts, and multi-band show settlements all live inside the **Events** tab. BandMath lets you toggle effortlessly between the chronological **Events List** and the interactive **Band Calendar View** so your entire band always knows where they need to be and when.

---

## 1. Events List vs. Interactive Band Calendar

At the top of the **Events** tab, you can switch between two synchronized views:
* **Events List View:** A focused, chronological feed of upcoming and past events with quick access to ticket links, Bouncer QR scanning, setlists, and the **Closing Room**.
* **Band Calendar View:** An interactive monthly and agenda calendar that visually color-codes your band's schedule so you can spot routing gaps, double-bookings, and member blackouts at a glance.

---

## 2. Supported Calendar Event Types

Tour life is more than just show nights. When adding an entry to the **Band Calendar**, you can categorize it by type so everyone in the band knows what the day entails:

| Event Type | Best Used For |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Show / Concert** | Full live performances with ticketing, Run-of-Show stage times, setlists, and **Closing Room** settlement. |
| **Rehearsal** | Practice space sessions, pre-tour production rehearsals, and soundchecks. |
| **Studio Date** | Tracking, mixing, or mastering sessions with studio call times and notes. |
| **Travel Day** | Long van drives, flights, ferry crossings, and hotel check-in details. |
| **Promo / Press** | Radio sessions, podcast interviews, photo shoots, and content days. |
| **Blackout / Unavailable** | Dates when one or more band members have personal commitments or work conflicts so nobody books a gig by mistake. |

---

## 3. Owned Shows + Joined Multi-Band Shows in One Calendar

On tour, your band won't always be the one creating the event in BandMath—often the **Venue**, **Tour Manager**, or **Headliner** creates the show and hands you a **6-Character Show Access Code**.

Whenever your band taps **`[ JOIN SHOW ]`** and enters a Show Code, BandMath automatically merges that joined multi-band event directly into your **Events List** and **Band Calendar View** alongside the events your band created.

:::tip
Tap any **Show** on your Band Calendar to jump straight into its event details—where you can grab your band's [Promoter Attribution Link (`?ref=`)](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links), check your Run-of-Show stage time, attach your [Setlist](/es/docs/Features/Setlist_Organizer), or open [The Closing Room](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room).
:::

articles.title: The First Tour: A Quick Walkthrough
articles.sidebarLabel: The First Tour: A Quick Walkthrough
articles.body:
Ready to hit the road? Here is a quick 5-minute walkthrough of the core BandMath loop to get you started on your first tour.

:::tip Playing as a Venue or Tour Manager?
If you run a venue, promote shows, or manage tours for multiple artists, BandMath has a dedicated 3-tab workspace built specifically for box office ticketing, QR hardware door terminals, Bouncer QR scanning, and nightly multi-band settlements. Jump straight to the [Venues & Tour Managers Quickstart](/es/docs/Getting_Started/Venues_and_Tour_Managers).
:::

## 1. Navigate the 5-Tab Band Workspace

When you log in as a **Band**, your bottom navigation bar gives you instant access to every part of your touring operation:
* **Home:** Your live **Transaction Feed**, plus quick actions to log expenses, incomes, and transfers.
* **Shop (Merch Stand):** Your in-person Point-of-Sale (POS) and access to the **Merch Warehouse** inventory manager.
* **Events:** Your **Events List**, interactive **Band Calendar**, **Setlist Organizer**, online ticketing links, and nightly **Closing Room** settlements.
* **Standings:** Your real-time member balances, **Band Bank**, **VAT Bank**, and one-tap **Automated Debt Settlement**.
* **Cart:** Your live checkout cart for ringing up fans via **Tap to Pay**, **Stripe QR Codes**, or **Cash**.

## 2. Log an Expense

Did someone buy gas for the van?
1. Open the **Home** tab and tap to add a new transaction.
2. Select **Expense**.
3. Select *who paid* for the gas, enter the description (e.g., `Gas`) and amount, and select the band members who should split the cost under *who owes*.
4. Upload a photo of the receipt. 
5. BandMath automatically splits the expense (catching any uneven pennies via the [Penny Catcher](/es/docs/Features/The_Penny_Catcher)) and updates everyone's internal balances.
6. Check out the results in the Transaction Feed on **Home** and on the **Standings** tab.

![Log Expense](/doc-assets/es/Getting_Started/assets/log-expense.png)

## 3. Stock Your Merch Warehouse

Before you can sell merchandise at a show, set up your catalog and stock levels inside the **Merch Warehouse**:

1. **Create Merch Types:** Define what you print on—from T-Shirts and hoodies to vinyl, hats, lighters, or custom tour posters. Merch types are completely customizable and unlimited.

![Create Merch Types](/doc-assets/es/Getting_Started/assets/create-items-1.png)

2. **Add Designs:** Attach designs to your merch types. Give the design a name and upload artwork—or submit right away to use a default Groovatar placeholder.

![Add Designs](/doc-assets/es/Getting_Started/assets/add-designs.png)

3. **Add Inventory:** Choose your Product Type and Design, input the unit production cost and retail price, and enter the quantity on hand for each size (items without sizes like vinyl, hats, or stickers use `N/A`).

![Add Inventory Flow](/doc-assets/es/Getting_Started/assets/add-inventory-flow.png)

## 4. Ring Up a Sale in the Merch Stand

When you are at the merch table after a set:
1. Open the **Shop (Merch Stand)** tab.
2. Tap the items and sizes the fan wants to buy to add them to your active **Cart**.

![POS Add to Cart](/doc-assets/es/Getting_Started/assets/pos-add-to-cart.png)

3. Open the **Cart** tab, select the payment method (**Cash**, **Tap to Pay**, or **Stripe QR Code**), and hit **Checkout**.

![POS Checkout](/doc-assets/es/Getting_Started/assets/pos-checkout.png)

BandMath atomically deducts the items from your inventory, sets aside any configured sales tax into your **VAT Bank**, and records the net profit across your band roster.

![POS Log Sale](/doc-assets/es/Getting_Started/assets/pos-log-sale.png)

## 5. Settle the Show & Check Standings

At the end of the night:
* Head to the **Events** tab to settle door tickets, shared show expenses, and venue merch cuts in [The Closing Room](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room).
* Open the **Standings** tab to see [Automated Debt Settlement](/es/docs/Features/The_Ledger#automated-debt-settlement) in action—computing the exact minimum number of transfers required for every member to be 100% square.

![Standings Summary](/doc-assets/es/Getting_Started/assets/standings-summary.png)

articles.title: Elegir tu Perfil y Crear una Banda
articles.body:
¡Bienvenido a BandMath! Ya sea que toques en una banda en gira, dirijas una sala de conciertos independiente o trabajes como Tour Manager, BandMath adapta tu espacio de trabajo a tu rol exacto en el show.

## 1. Inicio de Sesión Rápido sin Contraseña (Código OTP de 6 Dígitos)

Al abrir la app de BandMath o el portal web en **[account.itsbandmath.com](https://account.itsbandmath.com)**, puedes registrarte o iniciar sesión mediante:
* **Código Único por Correo (OTP de 6 dígitos):** Introduce tu correo electrónico y escribe el código de verificación de 6 dígitos enviado a tu bandeja de entrada.
* **Inicio de Sesión con Google o Apple:** Autenticación en un solo toque.

## 2. Elegir tu Perfil de Cuenta (`Band`, `Venue` o `Tour Manager`)

Durante la configuración inicial, puedes elegir cómo trabajas:
* **Band (Banda — Por defecto):** Desbloquea el espacio completo de 5 pestañas (**Home**, **Shop**, **Events**, **Standings**, **Cart**), contabilidad compartida, **Merch Warehouse**, **Setlist Organizer** y **Band Calendar**.
* **Venue (Sala):** Desbloquea una consola ágil de 3 pestañas (**Events**, **Bouncer**, **Cart**) diseñada para crear eventos, escanear entradas QR, vender entradas en puerta y liquidar conciertos multi-banda.
* **Tour Manager:** Desbloquea la consola de 3 pestañas (**Events**, **Bouncer**, **Cart**) para coordinar el bote común del show y enviar recibos finales de liquidación.

:::tip Cambia de Perfil en Cualquier Momento
¿Cumples varios roles en tu escena musical? Abre **User Settings** (arriba a la derecha) en cualquier momento para cambiar entre **Band**, **Venue** y **Tour Manager**. Consulta nuestra [Guía Rápida para Salas y Tour Managers](/es/docs/Getting_Started/Venues_and_Tour_Managers).
:::

## 3. Configurar el Perfil de tu Banda

En el modo **Band**, podrás crear tu primer **Perfil de Banda** (o unirte a una banda existente con un código de invitación).

### Configurar tu Moneda Base

Durante la creación, selecciona la moneda base de tu banda (por ejemplo, `EUR`, `USD`, `GBP`, `PLN`).

![Band Creation Dashboard](/doc-assets/es/Getting_Started/assets/band-creation-dashboard.png)

:::note
BandMath realiza todos los cálculos internamente con centavos enteros, por lo que la moneda es un **símbolo de visualización**. Para giras internacionales, consulta nuestra guía de [Giras Multi-Moneda](/es/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Multi_Currency_Touring).
:::

## 4. Las Cuentas del Sistema por Defecto

Al crear tu banda, BandMath configura automáticamente cuentas especiales para la contabilidad de partida doble:
1. **[The Band Bank](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_Band_Bank):** Representa la cuenta bancaria compartida del grupo.
2. **[The Cash Box](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_Cash_Box):** Registra el efectivo físico en tu caja de merch o sobre de liquidación.

articles.title: Inviting the Band
articles.body:
BandMath is built for collaboration. To get the most out of the platform, you should invite your bandmates and tour managers to join your band's workspace.

:::tip

If you are working with hired, hourly merch sellers, we recommend setting up generic profiles rather than inviting them directly. See [Working with Hired Merch Sellers](/es/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Hired_Merch_Sellers).

:::
## How to Invite Members

As an Admin, you can invite new members to your band by generating an **Invite Code**.

1. Navigate to the **Band Settings** page.
2. Select **Manage Members**.
3. Click **Add Member** and enter their name and role.
4. An invite code will be automatically generated. Once the new member appears in the roster, **press and hold on their card** and the invite code will be copied to your clipboard to easily share with them.

![Team Roster Invite](/doc-assets/es/Getting_Started/assets/team-roster-invite.png)

## The Invite Code Process

When your bandmate downloads the BandMath app, they will create their own user account. On the welcome screen, they will select **Join Existing Band** and enter the 6-character invite code you provided. 

This securely links their user account to your band's workspace and grants them access to view the ledger and log transactions.

## Shadow Profiles (For Members Without the App)

We know that not everyone in the band will want to download a finance app (we're looking at you, drummers!). 

BandMath solves this with **Shadow Profiles**. When you add a member to the roster, they are initially created as a Shadow Profile. This means they exist in the ledger so you can track their shares, debts, and payouts, even if they never download the app.

If a member *does* eventually download the app and uses their invite code, their account is instantly bound to their Shadow Profile, and they gain access to all their historical transaction data.

For more details on member permissions, see [Admins vs. Members](/es/docs/Team_Management/Admins_vs_Members).

articles.title: Guía Rápida para Salas y Tour Managers
articles.body:
BandMath también está diseñado para **Salas de Conciertos Independientes (Venues)**, **Promotores** y **Tour Managers** que gestionan la taquilla, el acceso en puerta y la liquidación nocturna del show.

Al seleccionar el perfil **Venue** o **Tour Manager** durante el registro (o en **User Settings**), BandMath se convierte en una consola enfocada en taquilla y liquidación.

---

## 1. La Barra de Navegación de 3 Iconos

1. **Events:** Crea nuevos conciertos (`[ + CREATE EVENT ]`), desbloquea cualquier show mediante su **Código de Acceso de 6 Caracteres (Show Code)**, gestiona el cartel multi-banda y dirige **The Closing Room**.
2. **Bouncer:** Abre el **Escáner QR de Entradas y Lista de Invitados** con el bloqueo de seguridad (**Bouncer Lock**) para el personal de puerta.
3. **Cart:** Vende entradas en taquilla al instante mediante **`[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`** con **Tap to Pay** o **Efectivo (Cash)**.

---

## 2. Tu Cuenta de Comerciante y Pagos con Stripe

En **User Settings**, la tarjeta **`MERCHANT & STRIPE PAYOUTS`** te permite:
* **Conectar con Stripe:** Vincula tu cuenta bancaria mediante Stripe Connect para gestionar la venta anticipada online y aceptar **Tap to Pay** en puerta.
* **Configurar tu Moneda Base:** Elige tu símbolo de moneda (`€`, `$`, `£`, etc.).
* **Gestionar Facturación (`account.itsbandmath.com`):** Accede al portal de facturación (`20 €/mes` Pro o pase de por vida **Bootstrapper's Club** por `100 €`).

Para ver el flujo completo, continúa en [Crear y Unirse a Conciertos](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Creating_and_Joining_Shows).

articles.title: Localization and Currency
articles.body:
Because BandMath is used by touring bands around the world, you can easily customize the app to fit your region.

## Setting Your Base Currency

When you first [create your band workspace](/es/docs/Getting_Started/Creating_a_Band), you will be prompted to select a **Base Currency**. 

:::note

BandMath handles all math natively using integers, which means the currency setting is purely a **display symbol**. You can change your workspace's currency symbol at any time in the settings without breaking your ledger!

However, because it is purely a display symbol, **BandMath does not perform automated currency conversion or exchange rates**. All transactions in a workspace are assumed to be 1:1 with whatever base currency you have selected.

:::

The base currency symbol is used to format all:
* Ledger calculations
* Debt settlements and payouts
* Merch inventory valuations
* Profit and loss reporting

## Currency Formatting

BandMath automatically formats your financial inputs and displays based on your selected base currency. This means that if you choose Euro (€) as your base currency, the app will automatically inject the `€` symbol into input fields like the merch inventory pricing, preventing typos and ensuring a clean user experience.

![Currency Formatting](/doc-assets/es/Settings_and_Preferences/assets/currency-formatting.png)

If you notice a currency symbol is missing or incorrect, please reach out to support.

## The Unified User Settings Hub

In addition to Band Settings, tapping the settings icon in the top navigation bar opens your personal **User Settings** hub, where you can:
* **Switch Your Active Persona:** Toggle seamlessly between **Band**, **Venue**, and **Tour Manager** modes at any time.
* **Switch Active Bands (Band Persona):** Jump between any of the bands you belong to via the Band Switcher dropdown.
* **Configure Merchant & Stripe Payouts (Venue & Tour Manager Personas):** Connect your Stripe account, set your base currency symbol, and launch the Web Billing Portal (`account.itsbandmath.com`).
* **Send Support & Feedback:** Open the built-in Support modal to message the BandMath team directly from the app.

articles.title: Notifications
articles.body:
BandMath keeps you informed about important financial events in your band's workspace.

## System Alerts

Currently, BandMath relies primarily on in-app alerts and transactional emails (such as payment receipts or subscription warnings from Stripe). 

If a recurring subscription payment fails, you will receive an email from our billing provider to the email address associated with the Admin account.

## Future Notification Updates

We are actively developing push notifications to alert you when:
* You are added to a transaction by another member
* Your band's inventory levels drop below a critical threshold (The Sales Analyzer currently provides these warnings in-app, but soon they will be pushed to your phone).
* A settlement period has closed.

Stay tuned to our blog for updates on these features!

articles.title: Admins vs. Members
articles.body:
BandMath uses a simple but strict role-based permission system to ensure your financial data remains secure and organized. There are two primary roles in any band workspace: **Admins** and **Members**.

![Admin vs Member Roles](/doc-assets/es/Team_Management/assets/admin-member-roles.png)

## Admins

The user who creates the band profile is automatically assigned as the first Admin. 

Admins have full control over the band's workspace. Their capabilities include:
* **Managing Members:** Adding new members, generating invite codes, and removing members.
* **Managing Settings:** Changing the band's name, base currency, and other core settings.
* **Managing Billing:** Upgrading or downgrading the band's subscription tier.
* **Merch Management:** Full access to add, edit, and delete merchandise inventory and product definitions.

## Members

Members are the standard users within a band workspace. They have the ability to participate in the financial ecosystem but with restricted administrative access.

Members can:
* **Log Transactions:** Add new expenses, incomes, or transfers to the ledger.
* **Edit Transactions:** Edit or delete any transaction in the ledger, regardless of who created it.
* **View the Ledger:** See all transactions and the current standings/settlements.
* **Sell Merchandise:** Use the Point-of-Sale (POS) system to log merch sales.

Members **cannot**:
* Access the Band Settings page.
* Remove other members from the band.
* Change the band's core settings or billing tier.


:::tip

A band can have multiple Admins. An existing Admin can promote any Member to an Admin role from the Band Settings page.

:::

## Leaving a Band vs. Removing a Member

Lineups change, and BandMath makes it clean to step away from a band without breaking historical accounting:

* **Leaving a Band Voluntarily (`Leave Band`):** Any member can leave a band at any time from **Settings**. Leaving a band marks your membership profile as inactive (`is_active = false` and `receives_merch_cut = false`). You will no longer be included in future expense splits or merch sales, while 100% of your past transactions and historical ledger math remain intact.
* **The Sole Admin Guard:** Every active band must have at least one Admin. If you are the **only Admin** in a band that still has other active members, BandMath will prevent you from leaving until you first promote another bandmate to **Admin** in Band Settings (or, if you are the final remaining member, you can delete the band workspace).
* **Leaving vs. Deleting Your Account:** Leaving a single band only disconnects you from that specific band workspace—your personal BandMath login and any other bands you belong to remain completely untouched. For full GDPR/CCPA account deletion across all bands, see [Deleted Users](/es/docs/Team_Management/Deleted_Users).

articles.title: Shadow Profiles
articles.body:
BandMath's architecture is designed around a unique concept called **Shadow Profiles**. This feature exists because we understand the reality of touring bands: not everyone wants to download a finance app. 

Whether it's a stubborn drummer or a temporary hired musician, you still need to track their financial shares and debts accurately.

## What is a Shadow Profile?

When an Admin adds a new member to the band's roster, BandMath creates a "Shadow Profile" in the database. This profile has a name and a role, but it is not yet attached to a real user account.

Because the Shadow Profile exists in your band's ledger, you can immediately start assigning transactions to them. You can log that the Shadow Profile paid for gas, or that they owe a split of the hotel bill. BandMath will calculate their balances and settlements perfectly, just as it would for an active user.

## Active Profiles vs. Shadow Profiles

* **Active Profiles:** These are members who have downloaded the BandMath app, created an account, and joined the band using an invite code. They can log in and see their own balances on their phone.
* **Shadow Profiles:** These are placeholders in your ledger. The Admin tracks their finances on their behalf.

## Transitioning to an Active Profile

If a member with a Shadow Profile decides they *do* want to download the app, they can easily claim their profile and instantly access all their historical data. See [Claiming a Profile](/es/docs/Team_Management/Claiming_a_Profile) for instructions on how this process works.

articles.title: Claiming a Profile
articles.body:
Users can claim a [Shadow Profile](/es/docs/Team_Management/Shadow_Profiles) to view balances and log transactions.

## The Invite Code

Every Shadow Profile automatically generates a unique 6-character **Invite Code**. This code acts as a secure key to bind your new user account to the existing financial data your band has been tracking for you.

Admins: Long press on the member name in the roster on the **Manage Members** screen in the Band Settings to copy the invite code.

## How to Claim Your Profile

1. Open the app and create a new user account using your email address.
2. On the welcome screen, select **Join Existing Band**.
3. Enter the 6-character Invite Code provided by your Admin.

:::info

Once you enter the invite code, your new user account is permanently bound to the Shadow Profile. You will instantly inherit all past transactions, debts, and credits associated with that profile, and your Admin will no longer need to track your finances on your behalf.

:::

articles.title: The Band Bank
articles.body:
**The Band Bank** is a permanent profile in BandMath that acts as a proxy for your real-world checking account.

BandMath uses **Entity-Based Accounting**. This means it doesn't just calculate a flat percentage of your overall bank balance (e.g., "Alice owns 25% of the total revenue"). Instead, it tracks each member's individual share on a *per-transaction* basis. Because of this, when money goes into the Band Bank, the Bank now *owes* each individual member their respective share of that deposit.

## How it Tracks Ownership

Instead of waiting until the end of the year to slice up a massive pie, BandMath calculates this debt instantly. Every time a $100 merch sale hits the Band Bank, the ledger records that the Bank now owes the individual band members for their specific share of that $100 (using the [Penny Catcher](/es/docs/Features/The_Penny_Catcher) algorithm to perfectly balance fractional cents).

The Band Bank isn't a savings account where money just sits indefinitely. That money always belongs to somebody. Because it acts purely as a container holding the cash, the exact dollar amount it owes to each member gets routed directly into BandMath's overall debt settlement algorithm. This means the Band Bank's balance simply becomes part of the final settle-up equation.

When it comes time to pay out the band at the end of a tour, you simply look at the standings and log a **Transfer** from the Band Bank to the individual members to settle those exact debts.

## Keeping it Synced

While the Band Bank is not digitally linked to your real bank account, its balance in the app should always stay perfectly synced with the actual amount of communal money you have. 

This happens in two ways:
1. **Automated Payouts:** When you accept a digital merch sale, the funds automatically flow into the Band Bank's balance as soon as Stripe processes the payout.
2. **Manual Income:** When a venue wires you a performance guarantee (or any other income that hits the bank account directly), you manually log it as an **Income** transaction. By setting the recipient to the Band Bank and selecting the active members in the "Split By" section, the app knows the bank is holding the money, but owes it back to those specific members.

By treating the band as its own profile, BandMath can elegantly handle scenarios that spreadsheets fail at, such as using the band's communal funds to pay a local sound engineer, or settling out the [Cash Box](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_Cash_Box), all while keeping everyone's personal standings mathematically perfect.

articles.title: The Cash Box
articles.body:
When you set up a band in BandMath, you are automatically provisioned a special account known as the **Cash Box**. 

While the [Band Bank](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_Band_Bank) represents the overarching pool of money owned by the business entity, the **Cash Box** serves a very specific, physical purpose: it represents the actual, physical cash sitting at your merch table.

## Why Do We Need a Cash Box?

When you sell merchandise for cash, that money physically exists at the merch table. Until someone takes that cash home or deposits it into a real bank account, it is considered "unclaimed."

If you log a cash sale directly to a band member, it assumes that member put the money straight into their pocket. However, in reality, the cash usually goes into a lockbox or a zipper pouch at the table for the duration of the show.

## How to Use the Cash Box

1. **Accepting Cash:** When logging a cash sale in the Point-of-Sale (POS) system, select the **Cash Box** as the recipient. This tells BandMath that the money is sitting in the lockbox.
2. **End of Night Distribution:** At the end of the night, you should never leave cash in the box unattended. When a band member takes the cash home for safekeeping (or to deposit it into a real bank account the next day), you simply log a **Cash Transfer** from the Cash Box to that band member.

By using the Cash Box as a temporary holding area, your digital ledger will always perfectly reflect the physical reality of where your cash is located at any given moment.

articles.title: The VAT Bank
articles.body:
If the [Band Bank](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_Band_Bank) is a proxy for your shared checking account, the **VAT Bank** is a proxy for the government. 

It is an invisible, provisioned shadow profile designed to hold tax liabilities. It doesn't represent a physical bank account or a physical cash box—it represents the reality that at the end of the touring season, somebody is going to have to write a check to the tax authority.

## The Inverse of the Band Bank

The VAT Bank operates as the exact inverse of the Band Bank within our Entity-Based Accounting system:

* **Band Bank:** The *Bank* holds the physical cash, which means the Bank **owes** money back out to the individual band members for their respective shares. 
* **VAT Bank:** The *Members* hold the physical cash (collected at the merch table), but a percentage of that cash doesn't actually belong to them. Therefore, the Members **owe** money back out to the VAT Bank.

## How It Works in Practice

When you play shows in regions that require you to remit VAT (Value Added Tax) or sales tax, you are collecting that tax from the fans on behalf of the government. 

1. **Collecting Tax:** As you log transactions or settle up nightly merch sales, any tax collected is assigned to the VAT Bank profile. 
2. **Accruing Debt:** Because the physical cash from the show was handed to the band members (or deposited into the checking account), the ledger records that the members now *owe* the VAT Bank for that collected tax. 
3. **Writing the Check:** Over the course of the tour, the VAT Bank will accumulate a positive balance in the Standings (because everyone owes it money). At the end of the quarter or tour, when you file your taxes, whoever physically writes the check to the government simply logs a **Transfer** for the tax amount and assigns the VAT Bank as the **payee**. 

If the money to pay the tax comes out of the shared checking account, the Band Bank is logged as the **payer**. If a member (like Charlie) pays the tax out of his own pocket, Charlie is logged as the **payer**. This instantly zeroes out the VAT Bank's balance, and whoever wrote the check is properly credited for covering the band's tax liability through the standard automated debt settlement system.

## Configuring Your Tax Rate

You can update your band's active tax rate at any time by navigating to the **Band Settings** page and looking under **Financial Settings**.

* If you leave your tax rate set to **0%**, you won't ever have to deal with the VAT Bank, and it will remain dormant. 
* If you want to use the VAT Bank to track your tax liabilities, simply plug your local tax rate in there and BandMath will automatically calculate and route the appropriate funds.

## The Stripe Tax Alternative

If you rely heavily on digital transactions, you have the option to use Stripe's built-in tax services. [Stripe Tax](https://stripe.com/docs/tax) automatically calculates, collects, and reports sales tax and VAT based on your customer's location. 

However, before enabling Stripe Tax, you must consider the following:

* **Cash Transactions:** Stripe Tax only monitors digital transactions processed through the Stripe terminal. It cannot calculate or track tax liability for cash sales logged at the merch table.
* **Double-Taxing the Ledger:** If you enable Stripe Tax on your merchant account *and* plug a tax rate into BandMath, your books will essentially get "double-taxed." BandMath will deduct tax for the VAT Bank, while Stripe will separately deduct tax for its own compliance system.
* **Debt Settlement Disconnect:** Tax liabilities calculated entirely on Stripe's end will not natively flow back into BandMath's internal debt settlement algorithm.

**Our Advice:** Choose one system. If you need to track tax liability for cash sales or want everything cleanly tied into your band's internal debt settlement, use the **VAT Bank** (by setting your rate in Band Settings). If you want Stripe to handle complex multi-region compliance and don't care about cash taxes, you can use **Stripe Tax**—but you must set your BandMath tax rate to **0%** to prevent double-counting.

:::tip Touring Across Borders & Settling With Venues
Wondering how Ticket VAT vs. Merch VAT works in the EU, how US state sales tax affects flat merch pricing, or how BandMath backs out tax before calculating Venue Merch Cuts? Read our deep-dive guide on [Live Music Touring Tax, Ticket VAT & Nightly Settlements](/es/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Touring_Tax_and_Nightly_Settlements).
:::

 Double-Taxing the Ledger: If you enable Stripe Tax on your merchant account and plug a tax rate into BandMath, your books will essentially get "double-taxed." BandMath will deduct tax for the VAT Bank, while Stripe will separately deduct tax for its own compliance system.
 Debt Settlement Disconnect: Tax liabilities calculated entirely on Stripe's end will not natively flow back into BandMath's internal debt settlement algorithm.

sections.heading: The VAT Bank
sections.content:
If the [Band Bank](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_Band_Bank) is a proxy for your shared checking account, the **VAT Bank** is a proxy for the government. 

It is an invisible, provisioned shadow profile designed to hold tax liabilities. It doesn't represent a physical bank account or a physical cash box—it represents the reality that at the end of the touring season, somebody is going to have to write a check to the tax authority.

sections.heading: The Inverse of the Band Bank
sections.content:
The VAT Bank operates as the exact inverse of the Band Bank within our Entity-Based Accounting system:

* **Band Bank:** The *Bank* holds the physical cash, which means the Bank **owes** money back out to the individual band members for their respective shares. 
* **VAT Bank:** The *Members* hold the physical cash (collected at the merch table), but a percentage of that cash doesn't actually belong to them. Therefore, the Members **owe** money back out to the VAT Bank.

sections.heading: How It Works in Practice
sections.content:
When you play shows in regions that require you to remit VAT (Value Added Tax) or sales tax, you are collecting that tax from the fans on behalf of the government. 

1. **Collecting Tax:** As you log transactions or settle up nightly merch sales, any tax collected is assigned to the VAT Bank profile. 
2. **Accruing Debt:** Because the physical cash from the show was handed to the band members (or deposited into the checking account), the ledger records that the members now *owe* the VAT Bank for that collected tax. 
3. **Writing the Check:** Over the course of the tour, the VAT Bank will accumulate a positive balance in the Standings (because everyone owes it money). At the end of the quarter or tour, when you file your taxes, whoever physically writes the check to the government simply logs a **Transfer** for the tax amount and assigns the VAT Bank as the **payee**. 

If the money to pay the tax comes out of the shared checking account, the Band Bank is logged as the **payer**. If a member (like Charlie) pays the tax out of his own pocket, Charlie is logged as the **payer**. This instantly zeroes out the VAT Bank's balance, and whoever wrote the check is properly credited for covering the band's tax liability through the standard automated debt settlement system.

sections.heading: Configuring Your Tax Rate
sections.content:
You can update your band's active tax rate at any time by navigating to the **Band Settings** page and looking under **Financial Settings**.

* If you leave your tax rate set to **0%**, you won't ever have to deal with the VAT Bank, and it will remain dormant. 
* If you want to use the VAT Bank to track your tax liabilities, simply plug your local tax rate in there and BandMath will automatically calculate and route the appropriate funds.

sections.heading: The Stripe Tax Alternative
sections.content:
If you rely heavily on digital transactions, you have the option to use Stripe's built-in tax services. [Stripe Tax](https://stripe.com/docs/tax) automatically calculates, collects, and reports sales tax and VAT based on your customer's location. 

However, before enabling Stripe Tax, you must consider the following:

* **Cash Transactions:** Stripe Tax only monitors digital transactions processed through the Stripe terminal. It cannot calculate or track tax liability for cash sales logged at the merch table.
* **Double-Taxing the Ledger:** If you enable Stripe Tax on your merchant account *and* plug a tax rate into BandMath, your books will essentially get "double-taxed." BandMath will deduct tax for the VAT Bank, while Stripe will separately deduct tax for its own compliance system.
* **Debt Settlement Disconnect:** Tax liabilities calculated entirely on Stripe's end will not natively flow back into BandMath's internal debt settlement algorithm.

**Our Advice:** Choose one system. If you need to track tax liability for cash sales or want everything cleanly tied into your band's internal debt settlement, use the **VAT Bank** (by setting your rate in Band Settings). If you want Stripe to handle complex multi-region compliance and don't care about cash taxes, you can use **Stripe Tax**—but you must set your BandMath tax rate to **0%** to prevent double-counting.

Wondering how Ticket VAT vs. Merch VAT works in the EU, how US state sales tax affects flat merch pricing, or how BandMath backs out tax before calculating Venue Merch Cuts? Read our deep-dive guide on [Live Music Touring Tax, Ticket VAT & Nightly Settlements](/es/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Touring_Tax_and_Nightly_Settlements).
:::

articles.title: Deleted Users
articles.body:
Under privacy laws like GDPR and CCPA, users have the right to completely delete their accounts and all associated personal data. However, in a double-entry accounting system like BandMath, simply deleting a member from the database would mathematically destroy every historical transaction they were ever a part of, throwing the entire band's ledger out of balance.

BandMath handles this elegantly through a secure anonymization process:

## 1. Profile Anonymization

Instead of removing the member's profile from the band entirely, BandMath securely wipes all Personally Identifiable Information (PII):
* The member's name is permanently changed to **"Deleted User"**.
* Their underlying authentication `user_id` connection is completely severed.
* Their profile is marked as inactive, meaning they are automatically excluded from any future splits (like the Penny Catcher or venue settlements) and will no longer receive a cut of merch sales.

## 2. Preserving Mathematical Integrity

By preserving this anonymized "ghost" profile, all historical ledger math remains perfectly intact. If that user paid for gas or owed the band $50 before they left, the ledger will accurately reflect those past balances attributed to "Deleted User". 

This ensures that the rest of the band's finances and historical records are never compromised when someone decides to delete their account.

:::note Leaving One Band vs. Deleting Your Entire Account
If a bandmate is simply leaving your band (or wrapping up a tour as a hired session player) and does **not** want to erase their entire BandMath account, they should use **Leave Band** in Settings (or an Admin can deactivate them in **Band Settings**). Deactivating a member excludes them from future splits and merch cuts while keeping their name and historical ledger records intact. See [Admins vs. Members](/es/docs/Team_Management/Admins_vs_Members#leaving-a-band-vs-removing-a-member) for details.
:::

articles.title: The Retroactive VAT Correction
articles.body:
**The Scenario:** 
A band records a full night's worth of merch transactions using the Point-of-Sale system. At the end of the night, they realize their band's tax rate was set incorrectly. As a result, the `VAT Bank` has collected either too much or too little of the profit pool across dozens of transactions. 

**The Nightmare:** 
In a traditional spreadsheet, the band would have to manually edit every single line item and recalculate the split for every band member.

**The BandMath Solution ("The Grand Adjustment"):**
Bands do not need to delete a single transaction or mess with their merch inventory. Because of the double-entry routing algorithm, they can fix the entire night in seconds with a single manual transaction.

First, calculate the total discrepancy (e.g., "We collected $100 for tax, but it should have been $150. We are short $50").

### Scenario A: The VAT was too LOW (Short $50)
If the band is short $50 in tax, it means the band members accidentally pocketed $50 of profit that rightfully belongs to the government.
1. Go to the ledger and click **Add Transaction**.
2. Create a manual **Expense** for **$50** and title it "VAT Correction".
3. Set the "Paid By" field to the **VAT Bank**.

*Result:* The algorithm instantly registers that the VAT Bank covered a $50 expense for the group. It automatically deducts the respective split from each active member's standings and routes that money directly into the VAT Bank's balance.

### Scenario B: The VAT was too HIGH (Overpaid $50)
If the VAT bank accidentally captured $50 too much, it means the VAT Bank is holding $50 of the band's rightful profit.
1. Go to the ledger and click **Add Transaction**.
2. Create a manual **Income** for **$50** and title it "VAT Refund".
3. Set the "Collected By" field to the **VAT Bank**.

*Result:* The algorithm sees that the VAT Bank just collected $50 of band income. It instantly forces the VAT Bank to surrender that money and evenly distributes it back into the band members' balances.

articles.title: The Incorrect Merch Transaction
articles.body:
**The Scenario:** 
A band member was rushing at the merch table and accidentally checked out the wrong item or size (e.g., ringing up a Medium shirt instead of a Large). They realize the mistake a few minutes later and need to fix it.

**The Solution: Manual Inventory Override**
Whether the customer paid with Cash or Credit Card, you **should not delete the transaction** if the total dollar amount charged was correct. Deleting a transaction that was paid via Credit Card in BandMath does not automatically refund your payment processor (like Stripe or Square), and you do not want to force the customer to swipe their card again or hand back cash for a simple inventory logging mistake.

To fix the error:
1. Leave the transaction alone in the Ledger. The financial amount perfectly matches the money deposited into your cash box or bank account. 
2. An Admin should navigate to the **Merch Inventory** page and long press the item. 
3. Manually adjust the stock counts to reflect reality (e.g., manually add +1 to the Medium shirt stock, and subtract -1 from the Large shirt stock). 

This instantly corrects your physical inventory counts for the rest of the tour without creating a messy trail of deleted transactions in your financial ledger.
