articles.title: Issuing a Refund (Merch Returns)
articles.body:
**The Scenario:** 
You sell a customer a shirt, but they immediately realize it's the wrong size. You don't have their correct size in stock, so they ask for their money back.

**The Best Practice:**
When a customer needs a full refund, you need to return their money and take the physical item back. BandMath handles the accounting for this beautifully through our "Self-Healing Ledger."

1. **Refund the Money:** Hand the cash back to the customer, or issue a refund through your credit card processor's app (Stripe, Square, etc.).
2. **Delete the Transaction in BandMath:** Go to the **Transaction Feed** (the Ledger), locate the original Merch Sale, and tap **Delete**.

**Why this works flawlessly:**
When you hit "Delete" on a Merch Sale to process a return, the backend triggers a cascading self-heal:
* **The Math Realignment:** The primary transaction and all associated profit splits are instantly removed, perfectly resetting every band member's standings back to where they were before the sale. You are no longer financially responsible for that income.
* **The Auto-Restock:** The backend opens up the associated order, looks at every single item and size that was in the cart, and automatically adds those exact quantities back into your active inventory (since you physically took the shirt back).
* **The Analytics:** The order records are purged, meaning your Sales Analyzer's ROI and velocity metrics remain completely uncontaminated by the refunded sale.

## Issuing a Partial Refund

Sometimes a full return isn't necessary. For example, if you accidentally overcharge a fan by €3 because the physical sign at the merch stand was outdated, or if there was a miscommunication on pricing, you can issue a **partial refund** without deleting the original transaction in BandMath.

Because BandMath provisions your band with a fully-featured Standard Stripe Connect account, you have direct control over your transactions. 

1. **Log into your Stripe Dashboard** (the same account you connected to BandMath).
2. Locate the specific payment in your **Payments** tab.
3. Click the **Refund** button and enter the exact amount you want to return to the fan (e.g., €3.00).

For more detailed help on navigating your merchant account, check out the [Stripe Knowledge Base on Issuing Refunds](https://support.stripe.com/questions/how-to-issue-a-refund).

## Sending Automated Refund Receipts

Because BandMath uses Stripe Connect (Standard), your band acts as the actual merchant of record and you own your own fully-featured Stripe account. This gives you complete liability protection, but it also means that automated email receipts are controlled by *your* Stripe settings, not BandMath's platform.

To automatically email your fans a receipt when you issue a refund (or a successful payment), you must turn it on in your Stripe Dashboard:

1. Log into your band's connected Stripe dashboard.
2. Click the **Settings** gear icon in the top right.
3. Under the *Business settings* section, click on **Customer emails**.
4. In the *Email customers about...* section, toggle on **Successful refunds** (and **Successful payments** if desired).
5. Hit **Save**.

articles.title: Inventory Missing or Showing Zero
articles.body:
**The Problem:** 
You are looking at your Merch Stand and an item is showing a much lower quantity than you physically have on hand, or it is reporting `0` inventory entirely—but you know for a fact that you still have some in the merch bin!

**The Cause:** 
You likely have items sitting in your active shopping cart. 

To prevent two band members from accidentally selling the same physical shirt at the exact same time (double-selling), BandMath automatically reserves inventory the moment it is added to a cart. If a shirt is sitting in an active or abandoned cart, it is immediately deducted from the available inventory count, even if the sale hasn't been finalized yet.

**The Solution:**
1. Navigate to the **Checkout** or **Cart** screen in the BandMath app.
2. Review the items currently sitting in the cart.
3. Tap **Clear Cart** (or swipe to remove the individual items).

As soon as the cart is emptied, the reserved items are instantly released back into your available inventory, and your counts will return to normal!

If a shirt is sitting in an active or abandoned cart, it is immediately deducted from the available inventory count, even if the sale hasn't been finalized yet.

**The Solution:**
1. Navigate to the **Checkout** or **Cart** screen in the BandMath app.
2. Review the items currently sitting in the cart.
3. Tap **Clear Cart** (or swipe to remove the individual items).

As soon as the cart is emptied, the reserved items are instantly released back into your available inventory, and your counts will return to normal!

Furthermore, you agree not to use the BandMath point-of-sale system to sell any illegal goods or items that violate Stripe's restricted business policies. By using the point-of-sale features, you agree to the Stripe Connected Account Agreement (or applicable Stripe Services Agreement).

### User Uploads & Content

Our platform allows you to upload photos and documents for receipt tracking. You retain full ownership of any files you upload. By uploading a file, you grant BandMath a license strictly to host and display that file within your account. You agree not to upload any content that is illegal, highly explicit, or infringes on the intellectual property rights of others. We reserve the right to remove any files that violate these terms.

Our core software features are provided free of charge. Access to our credit card processing infrastructure and automated revenue-splitting requires a Merchant Services Subscription. Payments for the Merchant Services Subscription and Bootstrappers Club memberships are non-refundable unless explicitly stated otherwise. We reserve the right to modify our pricing, but active lifetime memberships will be honored. All disputes involving consumers will be subject to the competent courts of the consumer's domicile, and we do not enforce mandatory arbitration for consumers.

articles.title: Frequently Asked Questions
articles.body:
How do I upgrade my subscription? All subscriptions are managed securely via our web portal. To upgrade, simply log in at [account.itsbandmath.com](https://account.itsbandmath.com) using your Admin credentials and select the tier that fits your band's needs. For more details, see [Upgrading and Downgrading](/es/docs/Billing_and_Account/Upgrading_and_Downgrading).
Can I be in multiple bands on BandMath? Yes! BandMath supports multiple bands for each user. You can be a member of an unlimited number of bands and an Admin for up to 5 bands. You can easily switch between your bands at any time from the Band Dropdown on the User Settings page.
Does BandMath handle multiple currencies for international tours? Yes! You do not need to create a new workspace or change your base currency when touring abroad. For in-person card payments, you can seamlessly accept foreign currencies using our [Stripe QR Codes](/es/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) workflow. Stripe handles the foreign exchange conversion dynamically, and deposits the funds into your home bank account. For physical cash, see our guide on the [Merch Float](/es/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Multi_Currency_Touring#the-merch-float--foreign-cash-walkthrough).
What is the "Band Bank"? The Band Bank is a permanent member profile created automatically for your band. It acts as a proxy for your shared business checking account. Unlike traditional spreadsheets that only compute a flat percentage of overall ownership, BandMath continuously tracks exactly how much of that communal money belongs to each individual member on an ongoing basis. Learn more about entity-based accounting in [The Band Bank](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_Band_Bank) article.
Can I use BandMath if some of my band members don't want to download the app? Yes! You can create a "Shadow Profile" for them. An Admin can log transactions on their behalf, allowing you to track their balances perfectly without them ever needing to open the app. Learn more in our [Shadow Profiles guide](/es/docs/Team_Management/Shadow_Profiles).
How does Automated Debt Settlement work? Instead of tracking a tangled web of "who owes who" for every individual receipt, BandMath analyzes the net balances of everyone in the band. It then calculates the absolute simplest way to settle all debts with the fewest number of cash transfers. For a deep dive into the math behind this, see [The Ledger](/es/docs/Features/The_Ledger).
How do we handle taxes on merch sales? BandMath features a "VAT Bank" – a special, automated profile that holds Value-Added Tax (or sales tax). When you sell merch, the tax portion is automatically transferred to the VAT Bank, ensuring you don't accidentally spend money you owe to the government. Learn exactly how this proxy account works in our [VAT Bank Guide](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank). If you ever need to apply taxes to past transactions, check out our guide on [Retroactive VAT](/es/docs/Troubleshooting/Retroactive_VAT).
What is a Groovatar? A Groovy Avatar! These are funky, musically-themed characters that pop up on loading screens throughout the app. They are also used as default placeholder images when transaction receipts or merch inventory photos are not available.
Can we export our data for tax season? Absolutely. You can export your entire ledger to a detailed CSV file at any time, which includes every transaction, date, payer, and calculated balance. For more details on what's included and how to run the report, read about [Data Exports](/es/docs/Features/Data_Exports).
What happens if I make a mistake on a transaction? Anyone in the band can edit or delete any transaction at any time, regardless of who created it. For a walk-through on how to handle refunds or incorrect logs, see [Incorrect Merch Transactions](/es/docs/Troubleshooting/Incorrect_Merch_Transaction) or [Issuing a Refund](/es/docs/Troubleshooting/Issuing_a_Refund).
Can we sell items at-cost to band members? Yes! When logging a sale in the Point-of-Sale (POS) system, you can toggle the "At Cost" switch for any band member, which allows them to take an item at its exact unit cost rather than the retail markup. Read the full walkthrough on [At Cost Member Purchases](/es/docs/Advanced_Workflows/At_Cost_Member_Purchase).
How does BandMath handle fractions of a cent? Our "Penny Catcher" algorithm ensures that when an expense is split unevenly (e.g. $10.00 split 3 ways), fractions of a cent are never lost or infinitely rounded. The ledger will always balance perfectly to the penny. For a deep dive into how we handle fractional remainders, read about [The Penny Catcher](/es/docs/Features/The_Penny_Catcher).
How can I get help or contact support? To get help, simply log into the BandMath app, open the end drawer (the menu on the right side of the screen), and tap **Support** at the bottom of the list. From there, you can send a message directly to our team, and you'll receive a response straight to your email inbox. Alternatively, you can always reach out to us directly by emailing { e.preventDefault(); if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined') { navigator.clipboard.writeText('support@itsbandmath.com'); const originalText = e.target.innerText; e.target.innerText = 'Copied!'; setTimeout(() => e.target.innerText = originalText, 2000); } }} style={{cursor: 'pointer', color: 'var(--ifm-color-primary)', fontWeight: 'bold', textDecoration: 'underline'}} title="Click to copy email">support{'@'}itsbandmath.com.
What are the processing fees for card payments? When you accept an in-person card payment using Tap to Pay on iPhone or Android, the transaction is processed through Stripe Terminal. The standard processing rate is **1.4% + €0.10** per transaction. Additionally, Stripe charges a **€0.10** "Tap on Mobile" fee for every physical tap. Instead of taking this out of each transaction, Stripe batches them together and bills your account once at the end of the day. For a full breakdown of fees (including Radar fraud protection for manually entered cards), see the [Tap to Pay Guide](/es/docs/Accept_Payments/Tap_to_Pay#processing-fees).
How do I send receipts to my fans? Immediately after completing a transaction in the Merch Stand, you will be prompted with an option to email a receipt to the customer on the success screen. If you accidentally close that screen, or if the customer typed their email address wrong, don't panic! Simply go to your **Transaction Feed**, tap on that specific transaction to open the detail page, and scroll to the bottom. From there, you can see where the receipt was sent, update the email address, and resend it. **For Automated & Refund Receipts:** Because BandMath uses Stripe Connect, your band owns its own merchant account. To automatically email your fans a receipt for refunds or successful payments without doing it manually, be sure to enable **Customer Emails** in your Stripe Dashboard. (Settings > Business Settings > Customer Emails).
What is the Cash Box? The Cash Box is a special account that represents the physical cash currently sitting at your merch table. It acts as a temporary holding area for unclaimed cash that needs to be distributed or deposited before the end of the night. Learn more in our [Cash Box](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_Cash_Box) guide.
What happens to the ledger if a member deletes their account? When a user deletes their account under GDPR or CCPA, BandMath securely anonymizes their profile instead of destroying it. Their name is permanently changed to "Deleted User" and their personal data is wiped, but the ledger math stays perfectly intact. You can read the full mechanical breakdown of this process in our [Deleted Users](/es/docs/Team_Management/Deleted_Users) article.
How do I log a merch sale? Before you can log a sale, you first need to define your items and input your stock inside the **Merch Warehouse** on the **Shop** tab. Once your inventory is set up, tap the items in the **Merch Stand** to add them to your cart and complete the checkout. For a complete step-by-step walkthrough of this process, check out our guide on [The First Tour](/es/docs/Getting_Started/The_First_Tour#3-stock-your-merch-warehouse).
What is the difference between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas? BandMath supports three account personas tailored to your role at the show: * **Band:** Gives you the full 5-tab workspace (`Home`, `Shop`, `Events`, `Standings`, `Cart`), multi-member ledger accounting, the Merch Warehouse, Setlist Organizer, and Band Calendar. * **Venue & Tour Manager:** Gives you a focused 3-tab box office and settlement hub (`Events`, `Bouncer`, `Cart`) with your own dedicated Merchant Account & Cashbox. You can switch between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas at any time inside **User Settings**. Read the full [Venues & Tour Managers Quickstart](/es/docs/Getting_Started/Venues_and_Tour_Managers).
How do multiple bands and venues connect to the same show? Every event in BandMath generates a unique **6-Character Show Access Code**. Any free Band, Venue, or Tour Manager can create the event (`[ + CREATE EVENT ]`) and share the 6-character code with everyone on the bill. Bands can join (`[ JOIN SHOW ]`) as Headliner, Co-Headliner, Support, or Opener at any time—even mid-show! See [Creating & Joining Multi-Band Shows](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Creating_and_Joining_Shows).
Who claims online ticket sales on a multi-band bill, and when does it lock? Any participant on the show with an active Pro subscription and connected Stripe account (Venue, Tour Manager, or Band) can click **`[ CLAIM ONLINE TICKETING ]`**. It remains switchable while `0` tickets have been sold, and permanently locks (`🔒`) the instant the first online ticket is purchased so all pre-sale funds and ticket tax set-asides remain unified in one merchant account. Learn more in [Online Ticketing & Promo Links](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links).
How do we track how many pre-sale tickets each band sold? When any band on the bill taps **`[ Share Link ]`** on the event page, BandMath automatically attaches their band's attribution tag (`?ref=`) to their checkout link and QR flyer so the Closing Table tracks exact pre-sale tickets sold per band. Fans and street-team promoters can also share their own referral pass to climb the event's **Referral Leaderboard**! See [Online Ticketing & Promo Links](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links#2-automatic-per-band-promoter-attribution-links-ref).
Can I hand my phone to a door person to scan QR tickets without showing them our band's money? Yes! Open **Bouncer Mode** and enable the **Bouncer Safety Lock** before handing your phone to door staff. They will be able to scan QR tickets with the mobile camera (on iOS and Android) and check off the Guest List all night, but exiting Bouncer Mode requires your device's Face ID, Touch ID, or Passcode. Read more in [Door Tickets & Bouncer Mode](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Door_Tickets_and_Bouncer_Mode#2-bouncer-mode--the-hand-off-safety-lock).
What happens when a band member pockets the cash payout envelope at the end of a show? When your band's payout or expense share is marked settled in [The Closing Room](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room#4-granular-settlement-to-ledger-commits), you choose **`Cash` vs. `Bank Transfer`** and select who received or paid it (`Cashbox`, `Band Bank`, or a specific active member like `John`). If John pockets the cash envelope, BandMath automatically credits every bandmate their share of the show income and records that John is holding the cash—updating your **Standings** immediately.

What happens to the ledger if a member deletes their account?

When a user deletes their account under GDPR or CCPA, BandMath securely anonymizes their profile instead of destroying it. Their name is permanently changed to "Deleted User" and their personal data is wiped, but the ledger math stays perfectly intact. You can read the full mechanical breakdown of this process in our Deleted Users article.

How do I log a merch sale?

Before you can log a sale, you first need to define your items and input your stock inside the Merch Warehouse on the Shop tab. Once your inventory is set up, tap the items in the Merch Stand to add them to your cart and complete the checkout. For a complete step-by-step walkthrough of this process, check out our guide on The First Tour.

What is the difference between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas?

BandMath supports three account personas tailored to your role at the show:
 Band: Gives you the full 5-tab workspace (Home, Shop, Events, Standings, Cart), multi-member ledger accounting, the Merch Warehouse, Setlist Organizer, and Band Calendar.
 Venue & Tour Manager: Gives you a focused 3-tab box office and settlement hub (Events, Bouncer, Cart) with your own dedicated Merchant Account & Cashbox. You can switch between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas at any time inside User Settings. Read the full Venues & Tour Managers Quickstart.

How do multiple bands and venues connect to the same show?

Every event in BandMath generates a unique 6-Character Show Access Code. Any free Band, Venue, or Tour Manager can create the event ([ + CREATE EVENT ]) and share the 6-character code with everyone on the bill. Bands can join ([ JOIN SHOW ]) as Headliner, Co-Headliner, Support, or Opener at any time—even mid-show! See Creating & Joining Multi-Band Shows.

Who claims online ticket sales on a multi-band bill, and when does it lock?

Any participant on the show with an active Pro subscription and connected Stripe account (Venue, Tour Manager, or Band) can click [ CLAIM ONLINE TICKETING ]. It remains switchable while 0 tickets have been sold, and permanently locks (🔒) the instant the first online ticket is purchased so all pre-sale funds and ticket tax set-asides remain unified in one merchant account. Learn more in Online Ticketing & Promo Links.

How do we track how many pre-sale tickets each band sold?

When any band on the bill taps [ Share Link ] on the event page, BandMath automatically attaches their band's attribution tag (?ref=) to their checkout link and QR flyer so the Closing Table tracks exact pre-sale tickets sold per band. Fans and street-team promoters can also share their own referral pass to climb the event's Referral Leaderboard! See Online Ticketing & Promo Links.

Can I hand my phone to a door person to scan QR tickets without showing them our band's money?

Yes! Open Bouncer Mode and enable the Bouncer Safety Lock before handing your phone to door staff. They will be able to scan QR tickets with the mobile camera (on iOS and Android) and check off the Guest List all night, but exiting Bouncer Mode requires your device's Face ID, Touch ID, or Passcode. Read more in Door Tickets & Bouncer Mode.

What happens when a band member pockets the cash payout envelope at the end of a show?

When your band's payout or expense share is marked settled in The Closing Room, you choose Cash vs. Bank Transfer and select who received or paid it (Cashbox, Band Bank, or a specific active member like John). If John pockets the cash envelope, BandMath automatically credits every bandmate their share of the show income and records that John is holding the cash—updating your Standings immediately.

articles.title: Privacy Policy
articles.body:
### 1\. The Short Version

We built BandMath to help musicians manage their money, not to mine your personal data. We only collect the information we absolutely need to make the app function, process your subscription, and allow your band to track expenses and take payments. We will never sell your personal data to advertisers or third parties.

### 2\. What Information We Collect

To provide the BandMath service, we collect:

*   **Account Data:** Your email address and basic profile information to create and secure your account.
*   **Financial & App Data:** The numerical data, expense logs, and inventory numbers you input into the ledger.
*   **User Uploads:** Any photos or documents you choose to upload for receipt tracking.
*   **Payment Information:** If you activate a Merchant Services Subscription, your payment details are collected directly by Stripe. BandMath does not store or have access to your full credit card number.

### 3\. Stripe Connect & In-Person Payments (Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android)

If your band uses our Stripe Connect integration to process fan payments via Tap to Pay on iPhone or Tap to Pay on Android, you will be required to provide identity verification (KYC) and business details directly to Stripe. This highly sensitive data is handled entirely by Stripe’s secure infrastructure. BandMath does not host or store your government ID, bank account routing numbers, or your fans' credit card data.

### 4\. Third-Party Services We Use

We run a lean operation and rely on a few trusted third-party categories of service providers to keep the app running securely. Your data interacts with:

*   **Cloud Hosting & Database Providers:** To securely store your user account, app data, and receipt uploads.
*   **App Framework Providers:** To build and host the app interface you interact with.
*   **Payment Processors:** To process your Merchant Services Subscription and facilitate your band's Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android transactions.
*   **Communication Platforms:** To manage our email list and send you transparent development updates.

### 5\. Your Data Rights (GDPR)

You own your data. Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you have the right to:

*   Ask for a copy of the personal data we hold about you (which you can do via the native export tool in the app).
*   Request that we correct any inaccurate information.
*   Withdraw your consent for marketing emails at any time.
*   Request that we completely delete your account and data from our active systems.

### 6\. Cookies

We keep things simple and respect your privacy. The BandMath website and web app only use strictly necessary cookies required for the site to function, to keep you securely logged in, and to route you to our payment processor. We do not use non-essential, invasive marketing or tracking cookies.

Yes! When logging a sale in the Point-of-Sale (POS) system, you can toggle the "At Cost" switch for any band member, which allows them to take an item at its exact unit cost rather than the retail markup. Read the full walkthrough on At Cost Member Purchases.

faqPairs.question: How does BandMath handle fractions of a cent?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Our "Penny Catcher" algorithm ensures that when an expense is split unevenly (e.g. $10.00 split 3 ways), fractions of a cent are never lost or infinitely rounded. The ledger will always balance perfectly to the penny. For a deep dive into how we handle fractional remainders, read about [The Penny Catcher](/es/docs/Features/The_Penny_Catcher).

faqPairs.question: What are the processing fees for card payments?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown:
When you accept an in-person card payment using Tap to Pay on iPhone or Android, the transaction is processed through Stripe Terminal. The standard processing rate is **1.4% + €0.10** per transaction. 

Additionally, Stripe charges a **€0.10** "Tap on Mobile" fee for every physical tap. Instead of taking this out of each transaction, Stripe batches them together and bills your account once at the end of the day. For a full breakdown of fees (including Radar fraud protection for manually entered cards), see the [Tap to Pay Guide](/es/docs/Accept_Payments/Tap_to_Pay#processing-fees).

faqPairs.question: How do I send receipts to my fans?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown:
Immediately after completing a transaction in the Merch Stand, you will be prompted with an option to email a receipt to the customer on the success screen. 

If you accidentally close that screen, or if the customer typed their email address wrong, don't panic! Simply go to your **Transaction Feed**, tap on that specific transaction to open the detail page, and scroll to the bottom. From there, you can see where the receipt was sent, update the email address, and resend it.

**For Automated & Refund Receipts:** Because BandMath uses Stripe Connect, your band owns its own merchant account. To automatically email your fans a receipt for refunds or successful payments without doing it manually, be sure to enable **Customer Emails** in your Stripe Dashboard. (Settings > Business Settings > Customer Emails).

faqPairs.question: What is the Cash Box?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: The Cash Box is a special account that represents the physical cash currently sitting at your merch table. It acts as a temporary holding area for unclaimed cash that needs to be distributed or deposited before the end of the night. Learn more in our [Cash Box](/es/docs/Team_Management/The_Cash_Box) guide.

faqPairs.question: What happens to the ledger if a member deletes their account?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: When a user deletes their account under GDPR or CCPA, BandMath securely anonymizes their profile instead of destroying it. Their name is permanently changed to "Deleted User" and their personal data is wiped, but the ledger math stays perfectly intact. You can read the full mechanical breakdown of this process in our [Deleted Users](/es/docs/Team_Management/Deleted_Users) article.

faqPairs.question: What is the difference between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown:
BandMath supports three account personas tailored to your role at the show:
* **Band:** Gives you the full 5-tab workspace (`Home`, `Shop`, `Events`, `Standings`, `Cart`), multi-member ledger accounting, the Merch Warehouse, Setlist Organizer, and Band Calendar.
* **Venue & Tour Manager:** Gives you a focused 3-tab box office and settlement hub (`Events`, `Bouncer`, `Cart`) with your own dedicated Merchant Account & Cashbox. You can switch between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas at any time inside **User Settings**. Read the full [Venues & Tour Managers Quickstart](/es/docs/Getting_Started/Venues_and_Tour_Managers).

faqPairs.question: How do multiple bands and venues connect to the same show?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Every event in BandMath generates a unique **6-Character Show Access Code**. Any free Band, Venue, or Tour Manager can create the event (`[ + CREATE EVENT ]`) and share the 6-character code with everyone on the bill. Bands can join (`[ JOIN SHOW ]`) as Headliner, Co-Headliner, Support, or Opener at any time—even mid-show! See [Creating & Joining Multi-Band Shows](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Creating_and_Joining_Shows).

faqPairs.question: Who claims online ticket sales on a multi-band bill, and when does it lock?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Any participant on the show with an active Pro subscription and connected Stripe account (Venue, Tour Manager, or Band) can click **`[ CLAIM ONLINE TICKETING ]`**. It remains switchable while `0` tickets have been sold, and permanently locks (`🔒`) the instant the first online ticket is purchased so all pre-sale funds and ticket tax set-asides remain unified in one merchant account. Learn more in [Online Ticketing & Promo Links](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links).

faqPairs.question: How do we track how many pre-sale tickets each band sold?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: When any band on the bill taps **`[ Share Link ]`** on the event page, BandMath automatically attaches their band's attribution tag (`?ref=`) to their checkout link and QR flyer so the Closing Table tracks exact pre-sale tickets sold per band. Fans and street-team promoters can also share their own referral pass to climb the event's **Referral Leaderboard**! See [Online Ticketing & Promo Links](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links#2-automatic-per-band-promoter-attribution-links-ref).

faqPairs.question: Can I hand my phone to a door person to scan QR tickets without showing them our band's money?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Yes! Open **Bouncer Mode** and enable the **Bouncer Safety Lock** before handing your phone to door staff. They will be able to scan QR tickets with the mobile camera (on iOS and Android) and check off the Guest List all night, but exiting Bouncer Mode requires your device's Face ID, Touch ID, or Passcode. Read more in [Door Tickets & Bouncer Mode](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Door_Tickets_and_Bouncer_Mode#2-bouncer-mode--the-hand-off-safety-lock).

faqPairs.question: What happens when a band member pockets the cash payout envelope at the end of a show?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: When your band's payout or expense share is marked settled in [The Closing Room](/es/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room#4-granular-settlement-to-ledger-commits), you choose **`Cash` vs. `Bank Transfer`** and select who received or paid it (`Cashbox`, `Band Bank`, or a specific active member like `John`). If John pockets the cash envelope, BandMath automatically credits every bandmate their share of the show income and records that John is holding the cash—updating your **Standings** immediately.

![Apple Tap to Pay on iPhone Lifestyle](/doc-assets/pl/Accept_Payments/assets/apple_tap_to_pay_goods.jpg) Accepting in-person contactless payments is easier than ever with **Tap to Pay on iPhone** and **Tap to Pay on Android**. These technologies turn your standard smartphone into a secure contactless card reader. This allows **Bands**, **Venues**, and **Tour Managers** to accept physical contactless credit and debit cards, as well as digital wallets like **Apple Pay** and **Google Pay**, directly on your device—no extra terminals or dongles needed. :::warning International Touring Limitation Due to strict banking regulations, Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android will **only function in your home country** (the country where your bank account is registered). If you are embarking on an international tour, you must use the [Stripe QR Codes](/pl/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) workflow to accept card payments. ::: ## Selling Merch vs. Selling Door Tickets You can use Tap to Pay across both in-person checkout flows in BandMath: * **At the Merch Stand (Bands):** Ring up shirts, vinyl, and hoodies in the **Shop / Cart** tabs. * **At the Box Office / Door (Venues, Tour Managers & Bands):** Tap **`[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`** on any event to ring up walk-up admissions via Tap to Pay directly into your own connected Stripe Merchant Account. See [Multi-Custodian Door Ticket POS](/pl/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Door_Tickets_and_Bouncer_Mode) for details on how door card sales reconcile in the Closing Room. :::tip Connecting Stripe for Venues & Tour Managers Operating in the **Venue** or **Tour Manager** persona? Open **User Settings** and use the **`MERCHANT & STRIPE PAYOUTS`** card to connect your Stripe account in minutes. ::: ## How to Accept a Payment (iPhone) When you are ready to check out a fan at the merch table or box office: 1. Complete your checkout flow in the BandMath **Cart** as usual. 2. Select **Tap to Pay on iPhone** as the payment method. 3. Present your iPhone to the customer. The screen will clearly indicate the charge amount, your merchant name, and an instruction for the customer on where to tap. 4. Ask the customer to hold their contactless card horizontally, or their device (like an iPhone or Apple Watch), at the **top edge of your iPhone**, over the contactless symbol. 5. When you see the "Done" checkmark, the transaction is complete! ## How to Accept a Payment (Android) 1. Complete your checkout flow in the BandMath **Cart** as usual. 2. Select **Tap to Pay on Android** as the payment method. 3. Present your Android phone to the customer. 4. Ask the customer to hold their contactless card or smart device against the **back of your phone**. 5. When the payment is approved, the transaction is complete! ### PIN Collection (SCA) If the customer's bank requires a PIN for security (common in Europe), the Android interface will automatically transform into a secure PIN pad, allowing the customer to type their PIN directly on your screen. *Note: This requires the customer's physical card to support "Online PINs". Older cards that only support "Offline PINs" will be rejected because your smartphone does not have a physical microchip slot to read the offline PIN data.* ## Processing Fees When you accept a payment via Tap to Pay on iPhone or Android, the transaction is processed securely through Stripe Terminal. It can be confusing because Stripe batches some of these fees together at the end of the day. Here is exactly how the fees break down for European cards: 1. **Standard Transaction Fee (1.4% + €0.10)**: This is Stripe's standard payment processing fee, taken out of every single transaction individually at the time of the sale. (e.g., on a €15 charge, the fee is €0.21 + €0.10 = €0.31). 2. **Terminal "Tap on Mobile" Fee (€0.10)**: Stripe charges an additional flat fee of €0.10 per physical tap/authorization. Instead of taking this out of each transaction, Stripe batches them up and bills you once at the end of the day (e.g., 9 taps = €0.90 billed for that day). 3. **Radar Fraud Fee (€0.05)**: Normally, in-person Tap to Pay transactions do not incur this fee because the physical card is present. However, if a tap fails and you manually type the card number in, or you send the fan a payment link to pay on their own phone, Stripe treats it as an "online" transaction. This triggers their machine-learning fraud protection tool, Radar, which charges a single €0.05 fee per screened transaction. ## Security and Privacy Tap to Pay uses the built-in features of your smartphone to keep your business and your customers' data private and secure. * **Encrypted Transactions:** All transactions are encrypted and processed securely. * **No Stored Data:** Card numbers are not stored on your device or on merchant servers. ## Accessibility Features The Tap to Pay PIN entry screen includes built-in accessibility options. This ensures that customers who are blind or have low vision can securely and independently enter their PIN with audio assistance if required. ## Requirements **For iPhone:** * You must have an iPhone XS or later. * Your device must be running the latest version of iOS. **For Android:** * Your device must have NFC enabled. * **Developer Options must be turned OFF** in your Android Settings. If Developer Options are enabled, Stripe's security protocols will block PIN collection and fail the transaction.
[Terms apply.](/pl/docs/Terms_of_Service#apple-disclaimers)
articles.plainText:
Merchant Education for Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android

Accepting in-person contactless payments is easier than ever with Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android. 

These technologies turn your standard smartphone into a secure contactless card reader. This allows Bands, Venues, and Tour Managers to accept physical contactless credit and debit cards, as well as digital wallets like Apple Pay and Google Pay, directly on your device—no extra terminals or dongles needed.

 International Touring Limitation
Due to strict banking regulations, Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android will only function in your home country (the country where your bank account is registered). If you are embarking on an international tour, you must use the Stripe QR Codes workflow to accept card payments.

 Selling Merch vs. Selling Door Tickets

You can use Tap to Pay across both in-person checkout flows in BandMath:
 At the Merch Stand (Bands): Ring up shirts, vinyl, and hoodies in the Shop / Cart tabs.
 At the Box Office / Door (Venues, Tour Managers & Bands): Tap [ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ] on any event to ring up walk-up admissions via Tap to Pay directly into your own connected Stripe Merchant Account. See Multi-Custodian Door Ticket POS for details on how door card sales reconcile in the Closing Room.

 Connecting Stripe for Venues & Tour Managers
Operating in the Venue or Tour Manager persona? Open User Settings and use the MERCHANT & STRIPE PAYOUTS card to connect your Stripe account in minutes.

 How to Accept a Payment (iPhone)

When you are ready to check out a fan at the merch table or box office:
1. Complete your checkout flow in the BandMath Cart as usual.
2. Select Tap to Pay on iPhone as the payment method.
3. Present your iPhone to the customer. The screen will clearly indicate the charge amount, your merchant name, and an instruction for the customer on where to tap.
4. Ask the customer to hold their contactless card horizontally, or their device (like an iPhone or Apple Watch), at the top edge of your iPhone, over the contactless symbol.
5. When you see the "Done" checkmark, the transaction is complete!

 How to Accept a Payment (Android)

1. Complete your checkout flow in the BandMath Cart as usual.
2. Select Tap to Pay on Android as the payment method.
3. Present your Android phone to the customer. 
4. Ask the customer to hold their contactless card or smart device against the back of your phone. 
5. When the payment is approved, the transaction is complete!

 PIN Collection (SCA)
If the customer's bank requires a PIN for security (common in Europe), the Android interface will automatically transform into a secure PIN pad, allowing the customer to type their PIN directly on your screen.

Note: This requires the customer's physical card to support "Online PINs". Older cards that only support "Offline PINs" will be rejected because your smartphone does not have a physical microchip slot to read the offline PIN data.

 Processing Fees

When you accept a payment via Tap to Pay on iPhone or Android, the transaction is processed securely through Stripe Terminal. It can be confusing because Stripe batches some of these fees together at the end of the day. Here is exactly how the fees break down for European cards:

1. Standard Transaction Fee (1.4% + €0.10): This is Stripe's standard payment processing fee, taken out of every single transaction individually at the time of the sale. (e.g., on a €15 charge, the fee is €0.21 + €0.10 = €0.31).
2. Terminal "Tap on Mobile" Fee (€0.10): Stripe charges an additional flat fee of €0.10 per physical tap/authorization. Instead of taking this out of each transaction, Stripe batches them up and bills you once at the end of the day (e.g., 9 taps = €0.90 billed for that day).
3. Radar Fraud Fee (€0.05): Normally, in-person Tap to Pay transactions do not incur this fee because the physical card is present. However, if a tap fails and you manually type the card number in, or you send the fan a payment link to pay on their own phone, Stripe treats it as an "online" transaction. This triggers their machine-learning fraud protection tool, Radar, which charges a single €0.05 fee per screened transaction.

 Security and Privacy

Tap to Pay uses the built-in features of your smartphone to keep your business and your customers' data private and secure. 
 Encrypted Transactions: All transactions are encrypted and processed securely.
 No Stored Data: Card numbers are not stored on your device or on merchant servers.

 Accessibility Features

The Tap to Pay PIN entry screen includes built-in accessibility options. This ensures that customers who are blind or have low vision can securely and independently enter their PIN with audio assistance if required. 

 Requirements

For iPhone:
 You must have an iPhone XS or later.
 Your device must be running the latest version of iOS.

For Android:
 Your device must have NFC enabled.
 Developer Options must be turned OFF in your Android Settings. If Developer Options are enabled, Stripe's security protocols will block PIN collection and fail the transaction.

<br /
<small

Terms apply.

</small

articles.title: Stripe QR Codes
articles.body:
Stripe QR Code Checkout provides a secure, reliable way to accept card payments from fans without relying on physical Tap to Pay hardware. It is the required workflow for [Multi-Currency Touring](/pl/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Multi_Currency_Touring) when your band travels abroad, as Tap to Pay requires you to be in your home country.

## How It Works

When a fan makes a purchase at the merch table:
1. In the BandMath Merch Stand, complete the checkout flow as usual.
2. Select **Card** as the payment method, and then tap **Show QR Code**.
3. A unique, 30-minute expiring QR code is generated on your screen.
4. The fan scans the QR code with their own smartphone camera.
5. They are seamlessly redirected to a Stripe Hosted Checkout page on their device.
6. The fan pays securely using **Apple Pay**, **Google Pay**, or by manually entering their physical card details.

## Real-Time Sync & Fulfillment

The BandMath app automatically listens to your backend database via real-time websockets. 

As soon as the fan completes their payment on their device, Stripe alerts our servers. The BandMath app instantly detects this, automatically dismisses the QR code screen, and displays your success receipt. 

Behind the scenes, BandMath automatically deducts the inventory, creates the transaction ledger entry, and handles complex band member splits—all atomically and securely.

### Check Payment Status (Fallback)

If you are playing in a basement club or a venue with spotty Wi-Fi, the real-time websocket connection to your app might drop. If the fan has completed the payment but your app hasn't updated yet, simply tap the **Check Payment Status** button on the QR code screen. This forces the app to manually poll the database and fetch the updated order status immediately.

## Canceling an Order

If the merch line is moving fast and a fan changes their mind (or takes too long), you can simply dismiss the QR code modal in the app. 

When you dismiss the modal, BandMath automatically reaches out to the Stripe API and **explicitly invalidates the checkout session**. This ensures the fan cannot accidentally (or maliciously) complete the payment on their phone five minutes later after you've already moved on to the next customer. The order is safely marked as failed in your ledger.

articles.title: Accepting Cash
articles.body:
BandMath's cash management system is built around the concept of **Cash Custody**. Because BandMath tracks every penny your band, venue, or tour package earns, it needs to know exactly who is holding the physical cash at the end of the night so the ledger stays perfectly balanced.

## How to Accept a Cash Payment

When a fan wants to pay with physical cash at the merch table or box office:

1. **Build the Cart:** Add merchandise items in the **Merch Stand** (or tap **`[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`** to add door admission tickets to your cart).
2. **Select Cash:** Choose **Cash** as the payment method.
3. **Assign Custody:** You will see a dropdown asking **"Who received it?"** Select your own name, the **Cashbox**, or the name of the band member physically taking the money.
4. **Pocket the Cash:** Take the physical cash from the fan and place it in your cash box, lockbox, or pocket.
5. **Complete the Sale:** Tap to finalize the order.

## How the Ledger Handles Cash

When you select your own name as the person who received the cash, you are taking "custody" of that money. 

Behind the scenes, BandMath automatically does the heavy lifting:
* It logs the total revenue for the band (and routes any applicable tax set-aside into the [VAT Bank](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank)).
* It deducts the items from your inventory (or increments the Door Ticket count on the event).
* It instantly calculates the profit splits for the rest of the group.
* It debits your personal account in the ledger, because you are now holding the band's money. 

At the end of the tour, you don't have to worry about counting up huge stacks of cash and dividing it manually. The **Standings** page will simply show that you owe the band money, which is perfectly offset by the cash already sitting in your pocket!

:::tip Multi-Custodian Door Cash & The Cashbox
When a **Venue**, **Tour Manager**, or **Band** rings up cash Door Tickets via `[ QUICK SELL DOOR TICKETS ]`, BandMath tracks those cash receipts under `Door Tickets by Custodian` in [The Closing Room](/pl/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room) and automatically nets that already-collected cash against your final settlement envelope. For foreign cash tours, see our [Multi-Currency Touring](/pl/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Multi_Currency_Touring#the-merch-float--foreign-cash-walkthrough) guide.
:::

articles.title: The "At-Cost" Member Purchase
articles.body:
**The Scenario:** 
A band member wants to buy one of the band's shirts for themselves, but they only want to pay the wholesale cost (e.g., the shirt costs $5 to print, but retails for $25). They want to take the shirt, ensure the inventory stays accurate, and properly reimburse the rest of the band for the wholesale cost.

**The Nightmare:** 
In a spreadsheet, you'd have to manually deduct the inventory, calculate the cost basis, and then somehow inject a $5 debt for that specific member without inflating your gross retail sales numbers.

**The BandMath Solution (The "At Cost" POS Checkout):**
Because BandMath handles inventory and double-entry routing seamlessly, this is processed exactly like a normal fan sale, but utilizing the built-in "At Cost" toggle.

1. Go to the **Point of Sale (POS)** and add the shirt to the cart.
2. Under the Merch Total, toggle the pricing selector from **Retail** to **At Cost**. This automatically reduces the cart total to match the exact wholesale cost of the items.
3. Tap **Cash**, ensure the active band member is set to the person taking the shirt, and tap **Go!** to checkout.
*Note: No physical cash actually needs to change hands.*

![POS At Cost Toggle](/doc-assets/pl/Advanced_Workflows/assets/pos-at-cost-toggle.png)

**Why this works flawlessly:**
* **Inventory & Analytics:** The POS system automatically deducts the shirt from inventory and logs the sale at $5. This ensures the Sales Analyzer's ROI and profit margins remain 100% accurate (it doesn't look like a shirt was "lost" or stolen).
* **The Settlement Routing:** The algorithm registers that the band member "collected" $5 in cash. Since no actual cash was put into a lockbox, that member is personally holding the $5. The algorithm will automatically split that $5 revenue among the band, meaning the member will effectively "owe" the rest of the band out of their share, perfectly reimbursing the group for the cost of the shirt!

articles.title: Multi-Currency Touring
articles.body:
When your band embarks on an international tour, dealing with foreign currencies, fluctuating exchange rates, and cross-border payment processing can quickly become an accounting nightmare. 

BandMath simplifies this entirely: **You do not need to create a new workspace or change your base currency when touring abroad.**

Instead, keep logging all of your transactions in your primary Band Workspace exactly as you would at home. 

## In-Person Card Payments Abroad

Due to strict international banking regulations, **Tap to Pay on iPhone** and **Tap to Pay on Android** will **only function in your home country** (the country where your bank account is registered). The physical address associated with your payout bank account must match the geographical location where the payment is being taken.

If you attempt to use Tap to Pay while in a foreign country, the transactions will be blocked by Stripe.

### The Solution: Stripe QR Codes

To accept card payments seamlessly when touring internationally, BandMath uses the **Stripe QR Code Checkout** workflow. 

When a fan wants to pay with a card:
1. Select **Card** at checkout and choose **Show QR Code**.
2. The fan scans the QR code with their own smartphone camera.
3. They are taken to a secure, localized Stripe checkout page on their device, where they can pay using Apple Pay, Google Pay, or by manually entering their credit card details.

Because the fan is initiating the payment on their own device rather than your hardware, this bypasses the strict hardware location restrictions of Tap to Pay. 

### Automatic Currency Conversion

When using Stripe QR Codes abroad, you will continue to price your merchandise in your home currency inside the BandMath app. 

Stripe handles the complex foreign exchange (FX) conversion dynamically behind the scenes. The fan is charged the equivalent amount in their local currency, while the funds are deposited into your band's bank account in your home currency. This keeps your BandMath ledger perfectly unified and clean, completely shielding you from the headache of manual exchange rate calculations!

For full technical details, see the [Stripe QR Codes](/pl/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) guide.

## The Merch Float & Foreign Cash Walkthrough

While card payments are converted automatically by Stripe, you will inevitably collect a pile of physical foreign cash at the merch table. To handle this, you need a "Merch Float" (a starting pool of local currency to make change). 

Here is the recommended workflow to handle foreign cash flawlessly using BandMath’s double-entry accounting. 

### 1. Create a "Cashbox"
First, create a [Shadow Profile](/pl/docs/Team_Management/Shadow_Profiles) in your band called **Merch Cashbox**. This acts as a virtual band member that "holds" your physical cash during the tour.

### 2. Fund the Float
When you arrive in the foreign country, one member (e.g., Alice) goes to an ATM, withdraws money from her personal checking account (e.g., $220 USD), and receives local currency (e.g., €200 EUR) to put in the physical lockbox.
* **In BandMath:** Alice logs a **Cash Transfer** from herself to the *Merch Cashbox* for $220. 
*(Alice is credited $220. The Cashbox now owes the band $220).*

### 3. Log Nightly Sales
Every night, log your cash sales normally in your home currency. Do not worry about exact daily exchange rates—just estimate! 
* **In BandMath:** Select *Merch Cashbox* as the person who "collected" the cash. If you sell $2,000 worth of merch, the Cashbox balance grows.
*(The Cashbox now owes the band $2,220 total).*

### 4. Exchange Before You Leave
Before you cross the border or board your flight home, take the massive pile of foreign cash to a currency exchange desk and convert it all back into your home currency. Suppose after exchange rates and fees, you are handed **$2,150 USD** in physical cash.

### 5. Assign Custody
Another band member (e.g., Bob) puts that $2,150 USD in his backpack to take home.
* **In BandMath:** Log a **Cash Transfer** from the *Merch Cashbox* to *Bob* for $2,150.
*(Bob now owes the band $2,150. The Cashbox is left owing the band $70).*

### 6. The True-Up
That missing $70 is the cost of doing business. It acts as a "catch-all" bucket that absorbs the bank fees, market fluctuations, and any mental math errors you made when logging sales over the tour!
* **In BandMath:** Log an **Expense** called "Foreign Exchange Fees" for $70, marked as Paid By: *Merch Cashbox*.
*(The Cashbox balance drops exactly to $0!)*

By doing this, the ledger balances perfectly without anyone having to do manual currency conversions on the road.

:::tip FX Gains
If the foreign currency *strengthens* during the tour, you might get back more than the Cashbox owes (e.g., $2,250 USD). In this edge case, the Cashbox would have a $30 surplus. Instead of an Expense, you would log a $30 **Income** (FX Gain) collected by the Cashbox to zero it out!
:::

For full technical details, see the [Stripe QR Codes](/pl/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) guide.

sections.heading: The Merch Float & Foreign Cash Walkthrough
sections.content:
While card payments are converted automatically by Stripe, you will inevitably collect a pile of physical foreign cash at the merch table. To handle this, you need a "Merch Float" (a starting pool of local currency to make change). 

Here is the recommended workflow to handle foreign cash flawlessly using BandMath’s double-entry accounting.

sections.heading: 1. Create a "Cashbox"
sections.content: First, create a [Shadow Profile](/pl/docs/Team_Management/Shadow_Profiles) in your band called **Merch Cashbox**. This acts as a virtual band member that "holds" your physical cash during the tour.

sections.heading: 2. Fund the Float
sections.content:
When you arrive in the foreign country, one member (e.g., Alice) goes to an ATM, withdraws money from her personal checking account (e.g., $220 USD), and receives local currency (e.g., €200 EUR) to put in the physical lockbox.
* **In BandMath:** Alice logs a **Cash Transfer** from herself to the *Merch Cashbox* for $220. 
*(Alice is credited $220. The Cashbox now owes the band $220).*

sections.heading: 3. Log Nightly Sales
sections.content:
Every night, log your cash sales normally in your home currency. Do not worry about exact daily exchange rates—just estimate! 
* **In BandMath:** Select *Merch Cashbox* as the person who "collected" the cash. If you sell $2,000 worth of merch, the Cashbox balance grows.
*(The Cashbox now owes the band $2,220 total).*

sections.heading: 4. Exchange Before You Leave
sections.content: Before you cross the border or board your flight home, take the massive pile of foreign cash to a currency exchange desk and convert it all back into your home currency. Suppose after exchange rates and fees, you are handed **$2,150 USD** in physical cash.

sections.heading: 5. Assign Custody
sections.content:
Another band member (e.g., Bob) puts that $2,150 USD in his backpack to take home.
* **In BandMath:** Log a **Cash Transfer** from the *Merch Cashbox* to *Bob* for $2,150.
*(Bob now owes the band $2,150. The Cashbox is left owing the band $70).*

sections.heading: 6. The True-Up
sections.content:
That missing $70 is the cost of doing business. It acts as a "catch-all" bucket that absorbs the bank fees, market fluctuations, and any mental math errors you made when logging sales over the tour!
* **In BandMath:** Log an **Expense** called "Foreign Exchange Fees" for $70, marked as Paid By: *Merch Cashbox*.
*(The Cashbox balance drops exactly to $0!)*

By doing this, the ledger balances perfectly without anyone having to do manual currency conversions on the road.

:::tip FX Gains
If the foreign currency *strengthens* during the tour, you might get back more than the Cashbox owes (e.g., $2,250 USD). In this edge case, the Cashbox would have a $30 surplus. Instead of an Expense, you would log a $30 **Income** (FX Gain) collected by the Cashbox to zero it out!
:::

articles.title: Working with Hired Merch Sellers
articles.body:
If your band frequently hires local hourly workers to sell merchandise at shows, it might seem complicated to track their cash tills and credit card sales. However, you can perfectly track their cash custody without needing to invite temporary workers to your BandMath workspace using their personal phone numbers or emails.

Instead, we recommend setting up dedicated, generic "Merch Station" accounts.

## 1. Creating Generic Accounts

Rather than inviting the individual, an Admin can create a generic **Active Profile** for the merch table.

1. Create a dummy email address or use a band alias (e.g., `merch1@yourband.com`).
2. Generate an invite code from the **Band Settings** page for a new member named "Merch Station 1".
3. Download the BandMath app on your dedicated merch iPad or mobile device.
4. Use the dummy email to create an account and join the band using the invite code.
5. The device can now remain permanently logged into this generic account.

:::tip

If you run multiple merch tables at large venues, you can create "Merch Station 2", "Merch Station 3", etc., each with its own device.

:::

## 2. Working the Table (POS)

During the show, the hired seller uses the POS on their dedicated device just like any other band member.

* **Cash Sales:** When the seller logs a cash sale, BandMath automatically attributes that cash to the "Merch Station 1" profile. In the ledger, Merch Station 1 now "owes" the band that cash because they are physically holding it in their cash box.
* **Credit Card Sales:** When they log a card sale, the money goes straight to your Band Bank (or the connected Stripe/bank account). Credit card transactions do not affect the seller's physical cash balance in BandMath.

## 3. End-of-Night Cash Handoff

At the end of the night, it's time to reconcile the till and collect the cash. The BandMath ledger will show exactly how much cash "Merch Station 1" is supposed to be holding based on their cash sales.

1. The hired seller counts their cash box and physically hands the cash over to a bandmate or the Tour Manager.
2. In BandMath, log a **Transfer** transaction:
   * **Who Paid:** Merch Station 1
   * **Who Owes:** Tour Manager (or whoever took the cash)
   * **Amount:** The total cash handed over (e.g., $500)
3. **The Magic:** This instantly zeroes out the Merch Station's balance (they no longer owe the band anything) and transfers that cash custody to the Tour Manager, who is now responsible for depositing it or keeping it safe!

:::note

Since the hired sellers are paid separately (e.g. hourly via an eventual paycheck), their pay is completely decoupled from the nightly merch till reconciliation. When you eventually pay them, you can just log that as a standard Expense paid for by the Band Bank!

:::

articles.title: Live Music Touring Tax, Ticket VAT & Nightly Settlements (EU & US)
articles.body:
When the lights come up after an encore and everyone gathers in the back office to settle the show, the fastest way for a band, promoter, or venue to accidentally lose money is by splitting **Gross** receipts without backing out consumer tax first.

Whether you are dealing with **Value-Added Tax (VAT)** in the European Union and UK or **Sales Tax** across state lines in the United States, tax collected from fans at the door or the merch table is **not** show revenue—it is money held in trust for the government.

This guide breaks down how live music taxes work in the real world across Europe and North America, why ticket tax and merch tax are almost never the same rate, and how BandMath's **Two-Tier Tax Model** protects every band, tour manager, and venue at the closing table.

---

## 1. Why Tax Matters at the Night-of-Show Closing Table

Every ticket or T-shirt sold to a fan in a taxable jurisdiction includes a portion owed to the tax authority. To find the true **Net Revenue** from a tax-inclusive sale, you divide the gross price by `1 + Tax Rate`:

```text
Net Revenue = Gross Receipts / (1 + Tax Rate)
Tax Set-Aside = Gross Receipts - Net Revenue
```

### The "Gross Split" Trap

Imagine a venue processes **€5,350** in ticket sales in a country with **7% Ticket VAT** (`€5,000` Net Revenue + `€350` VAT):
* **If you split Gross (`80% / 20%` of €5,350):** The band walks out with €4,280 and the venue keeps €1,070. At the end of the quarter, the venue (as the merchant of record who processed those sales) still owes the government the full **€350** in VAT—leaving the venue with only €720 (`14.4%` instead of `20%`).
* **If you split Net (`80% / 20%` after backing out 7% VAT):** The **€350** tax set-aside stays with the merchant who processed the tickets so they can pay the government. The remaining **€5,000 Net Ticket Pool** is split cleanly: **€4,000** to the band and **€1,000** to the venue.

### Venue Merch Cuts (`15%–25%`)

The exact same rule applies when a venue takes a percentage of a band's merchandise sales (a "venue merch cut" or "hall fee"):
* Because the band is the merchant of record on their own **Merch Stand**, the band is legally responsible for remitting the VAT or sales tax on every shirt sold, plus absorbing any Stripe card processing fees.
* Standard industry practice calculates the venue's merch commission **Net of Tax and Card Processing Fees**. Otherwise, the band would be paying the venue a 20% commission on tax money that belongs to the government and processing fees already kept by Stripe!

:::tip
In BandMath, every settlement calculation—both for **Ticket Pools** and **Venue Merch Cuts**—automatically backs out the applicable tax set-aside and card processing fees first, ensuring neither the band nor the house ever pays commission on government tax money.
:::

---

## 2. How Touring Tax Works in the European Union (EU & UK)

Under EU VAT law, live concerts and in-person merchandise sales follow the **Place of Supply Rule**: both event admission (tickets) and physical goods sold to fans on-site (merch) are taxed at the rates of the country where the venue is physically located.

When touring Europe, two critical tax realities affect nearly every show settlement:

### Crucial EU Nuance #1: Ticket VAT ≠ Merch VAT

Almost every EU member state treats live concert admission as a protected cultural activity with a **reduced VAT rate**, while taxing physical merchandise (T-shirts, hoodies, vinyl, hats) at the **standard goods rate**:

| Country | Concert Ticket VAT (Reduced Cultural Rate) | Physical Merch VAT (Standard Goods Rate) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Germany** | `7%` | `19%` |
| **France** | `5.5%` *(or `2.1%` for qualifying early runs)* | `20%` |
| **Netherlands** | `9%` | `21%` |
| **Belgium** | `6%` | `21%` |
| **Spain** | `10%` | `21%` |
| **Austria** | `13%` | `20%` |
| **Poland** | `8%` | `23%` |

Because of this gap, a single "Show Tax Rate" can never accurately settle both the box office and the merch table in Europe.

### Crucial EU Nuance #2: VAT-Registered Headliners vs. VAT-Exempt Openers (`0%` SME)

On a multi-band bill, different bands on the exact same stage often have completely different legal tax statuses:
* **VAT-Registered Touring Acts & Venues:** Established touring bands and venues registered for VAT must back out `19%–21%` VAT on their merch sales.
* **VAT-Exempt Indie & Support Bands (`0%`):** Emerging bands operating under their country's small-business exemption (such as Germany's *Kleinunternehmerregelung*, France's *Franchise en base de TVA*, or the **EU Cross-Border SME Scheme**) are legally **VAT-exempt (`0%`)**. They do not charge VAT on their merch and cannot deduct input VAT.

If a closing room forced a flat `20%` merch VAT rate onto a VAT-exempt opener, it would artificially shrink their net merch total before calculating a venue cut. Conversely, if it forced `0%` onto a VAT-registered headliner, the headliner would overpay the venue cut out of their VAT liability.

---

## 3. How Touring Sales Tax Works in the United States

In the United States, there is no federal VAT. Instead, retail sales are governed by state, county, and municipal **Sales Tax** (plus local **Admissions / Amusement Taxes** on tickets in certain cities and states).

### Physical Presence Nexus on Tour

When your band sets up a merch table inside a venue in another state, selling physical goods in person generally creates temporary **physical presence nexus** in that jurisdiction for the night of the show:
* **Local Rate Variations:** A Tuesday night show in Austin, Texas (`8.25%` combined state + city sales tax) has a completely different rate than a Thursday night show in Portland, Oregon (`0%` state sales tax).
* **Product-Specific Exemptions:** A few US states exempt everyday clothing (like T-shirts and hoodies) below a certain dollar threshold while still taxing vinyl, posters, and accessories (for example, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Massachusetts, and New York below `$110`).

### Tax-Inclusive Flat Pricing at the Merch Table

No band wants to make change with coins in a dark club because a `$30` T-shirt rang up at `$32.48` with tax. Working bands across the US price their merch in clean, round, **tax-inclusive** numbers (`$30 T-Shirt`, `$40 Vinyl`).

During the show, fans pay flat round prices. At the end of the night, BandMath uses tax-inclusive math (`$30 / 1.0825 = $27.71 Net`, `$2.29 Tax Set-Aside`) to route the exact tax portion into your [VAT Bank](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank) and compute the venue's merch cut strictly on your `$27.71` net revenue.

---

## 4. How BandMath Models This Cleanly: Two-Tier Transparency

To support both EU reduced-ticket / standard-merch VAT rules and multi-band bills with mixed tax statuses, BandMath separates show taxation into two transparent, independent tiers:

### Tier 1: Standardized Event Ticket Tax Rate

Ticket tax applies to admission to a specific event in a specific venue, so it is standardized across the entire show:
1. **Set Upfront on the Event:** The Event Organizer (Venue, Tour Manager, or Originating Band) sets the **Event Ticket Tax Rate** when creating or editing the event.
2. **Visible in the Event Header:** Every participant on the bill can see the active ticket tax badge (e.g., **`[ TICKET TAX 7% ]`**) right in the Event Header, and the organizer can adjust it prior to locking the final settlement.
3. **Protects Every Ticket Collector:** Every ticket sold for that event—whether an online pre-sale or a Door Ticket rung up in cash or Tap to Pay by the Venue, Tour Manager, or any Band—uses that single agreed **Event Ticket Tax Rate**. Whoever processed the ticket sale retains the exact tax set-aside in their own account so they are never left short when filing taxes, while the **Net Ticket Pool** flows into the Closing Room for the split.

### Tier 2: Per-Band Merch Tax Rate with Deal Sheet Transparency

Because every band is the legal merchant of record for their own merchandise, each band controls their own **Merch Tax Rate** inside their Band Settings (or directly from their **Show Call Sheet** card):
1. **Automatic VAT Bank Routing:** Whenever a band sells merch in the **Merch Stand** at a show, their configured Merch Tax Rate automatically sets aside the tax liability into their band's [VAT Bank](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank) in **Standings**.
2. **Call Sheet & Deal Sheet Transparency:** In a multi-band closing room, a venue or promoter should never have to guess why two bands with similar gross merch sales have different net numbers. BandMath prints each band's declared Merch Tax Rate directly on:
   * Their **Show Call Sheet Info Card** (visible to the Closing Officer and band).
   * Every **Deal Sheet** merch cut line item—displaying the exact math in plain sight (for example, `15% of €228.77 (Net of 19% VAT & Stripe)` for a VAT-registered headliner, or `15% of €142.50 (0% VAT · Net of Stripe)` for a VAT-exempt opener).

:::note
Need to change your band's Merch Tax Rate when crossing a border on tour? Update your tax rate in **Band Settings** before opening your Merch Stand for the night, and BandMath will apply the new rate to that night's sales and Deal Sheet without altering any of your previous shows!
:::
