articles.title: Admins vs. Members
articles.body:
BandMath uses a simple but strict role-based permission system to ensure your financial data remains secure and organized. There are two primary roles in any band workspace: **Admins** and **Members**.

![Admin vs Member Roles](/doc-assets/pl/Team_Management/assets/admin-member-roles.png)

## Admins

The user who creates the band profile is automatically assigned as the first Admin. 

Admins have full control over the band's workspace. Their capabilities include:
* **Managing Members:** Adding new members, generating invite codes, and removing members.
* **Managing Settings:** Changing the band's name, base currency, and other core settings.
* **Managing Billing:** Upgrading or downgrading the band's subscription tier.
* **Merch Management:** Full access to add, edit, and delete merchandise inventory and product definitions.

## Members

Members are the standard users within a band workspace. They have the ability to participate in the financial ecosystem but with restricted administrative access.

Members can:
* **Log Transactions:** Add new expenses, incomes, or transfers to the ledger.
* **Edit Transactions:** Edit or delete any transaction in the ledger, regardless of who created it.
* **View the Ledger:** See all transactions and the current standings/settlements.
* **Sell Merchandise:** Use the Point-of-Sale (POS) system to log merch sales.

Members **cannot**:
* Access the Band Settings page.
* Remove other members from the band.
* Change the band's core settings or billing tier.


:::tip

A band can have multiple Admins. An existing Admin can promote any Member to an Admin role from the Band Settings page.

:::

## Leaving a Band vs. Removing a Member

Lineups change, and BandMath makes it clean to step away from a band without breaking historical accounting:

* **Leaving a Band Voluntarily (`Leave Band`):** Any member can leave a band at any time from **Settings**. Leaving a band marks your membership profile as inactive (`is_active = false` and `receives_merch_cut = false`). You will no longer be included in future expense splits or merch sales, while 100% of your past transactions and historical ledger math remain intact.
* **The Sole Admin Guard:** Every active band must have at least one Admin. If you are the **only Admin** in a band that still has other active members, BandMath will prevent you from leaving until you first promote another bandmate to **Admin** in Band Settings (or, if you are the final remaining member, you can delete the band workspace).
* **Leaving vs. Deleting Your Account:** Leaving a single band only disconnects you from that specific band workspace—your personal BandMath login and any other bands you belong to remain completely untouched. For full GDPR/CCPA account deletion across all bands, see [Deleted Users](/pl/docs/Team_Management/Deleted_Users).

articles.title: Shadow Profiles
articles.body:
BandMath's architecture is designed around a unique concept called **Shadow Profiles**. This feature exists because we understand the reality of touring bands: not everyone wants to download a finance app. 

Whether it's a stubborn drummer or a temporary hired musician, you still need to track their financial shares and debts accurately.

## What is a Shadow Profile?

When an Admin adds a new member to the band's roster, BandMath creates a "Shadow Profile" in the database. This profile has a name and a role, but it is not yet attached to a real user account.

Because the Shadow Profile exists in your band's ledger, you can immediately start assigning transactions to them. You can log that the Shadow Profile paid for gas, or that they owe a split of the hotel bill. BandMath will calculate their balances and settlements perfectly, just as it would for an active user.

## Active Profiles vs. Shadow Profiles

* **Active Profiles:** These are members who have downloaded the BandMath app, created an account, and joined the band using an invite code. They can log in and see their own balances on their phone.
* **Shadow Profiles:** These are placeholders in your ledger. The Admin tracks their finances on their behalf.

## Transitioning to an Active Profile

If a member with a Shadow Profile decides they *do* want to download the app, they can easily claim their profile and instantly access all their historical data. See [Claiming a Profile](/pl/docs/Team_Management/Claiming_a_Profile) for instructions on how this process works.

articles.title: Claiming a Profile
articles.body:
Users can claim a [Shadow Profile](/pl/docs/Team_Management/Shadow_Profiles) to view balances and log transactions.

## The Invite Code

Every Shadow Profile automatically generates a unique 6-character **Invite Code**. This code acts as a secure key to bind your new user account to the existing financial data your band has been tracking for you.

Admins: Long press on the member name in the roster on the **Manage Members** screen in the Band Settings to copy the invite code.

## How to Claim Your Profile

1. Open the app and create a new user account using your email address.
2. On the welcome screen, select **Join Existing Band**.
3. Enter the 6-character Invite Code provided by your Admin.

:::info

Once you enter the invite code, your new user account is permanently bound to the Shadow Profile. You will instantly inherit all past transactions, debts, and credits associated with that profile, and your Admin will no longer need to track your finances on your behalf.

:::

articles.title: The Band Bank
articles.body:
**The Band Bank** is a permanent profile in BandMath that acts as a proxy for your real-world checking account.

BandMath uses **Entity-Based Accounting**. This means it doesn't just calculate a flat percentage of your overall bank balance (e.g., "Alice owns 25% of the total revenue"). Instead, it tracks each member's individual share on a *per-transaction* basis. Because of this, when money goes into the Band Bank, the Bank now *owes* each individual member their respective share of that deposit.

## How it Tracks Ownership

Instead of waiting until the end of the year to slice up a massive pie, BandMath calculates this debt instantly. Every time a $100 merch sale hits the Band Bank, the ledger records that the Bank now owes the individual band members for their specific share of that $100 (using the [Penny Catcher](/pl/docs/Features/The_Penny_Catcher) algorithm to perfectly balance fractional cents).

The Band Bank isn't a savings account where money just sits indefinitely. That money always belongs to somebody. Because it acts purely as a container holding the cash, the exact dollar amount it owes to each member gets routed directly into BandMath's overall debt settlement algorithm. This means the Band Bank's balance simply becomes part of the final settle-up equation.

When it comes time to pay out the band at the end of a tour, you simply look at the standings and log a **Transfer** from the Band Bank to the individual members to settle those exact debts.

## Keeping it Synced

While the Band Bank is not digitally linked to your real bank account, its balance in the app should always stay perfectly synced with the actual amount of communal money you have. 

This happens in two ways:
1. **Automated Payouts:** When you accept a digital merch sale, the funds automatically flow into the Band Bank's balance as soon as Stripe processes the payout.
2. **Manual Income:** When a venue wires you a performance guarantee (or any other income that hits the bank account directly), you manually log it as an **Income** transaction. By setting the recipient to the Band Bank and selecting the active members in the "Split By" section, the app knows the bank is holding the money, but owes it back to those specific members.

By treating the band as its own profile, BandMath can elegantly handle scenarios that spreadsheets fail at, such as using the band's communal funds to pay a local sound engineer, or settling out the [Cash Box](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_Cash_Box), all while keeping everyone's personal standings mathematically perfect.

articles.title: The Cash Box
articles.body:
When you set up a band in BandMath, you are automatically provisioned a special account known as the **Cash Box**. 

While the [Band Bank](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_Band_Bank) represents the overarching pool of money owned by the business entity, the **Cash Box** serves a very specific, physical purpose: it represents the actual, physical cash sitting at your merch table.

## Why Do We Need a Cash Box?

When you sell merchandise for cash, that money physically exists at the merch table. Until someone takes that cash home or deposits it into a real bank account, it is considered "unclaimed."

If you log a cash sale directly to a band member, it assumes that member put the money straight into their pocket. However, in reality, the cash usually goes into a lockbox or a zipper pouch at the table for the duration of the show.

## How to Use the Cash Box

1. **Accepting Cash:** When logging a cash sale in the Point-of-Sale (POS) system, select the **Cash Box** as the recipient. This tells BandMath that the money is sitting in the lockbox.
2. **End of Night Distribution:** At the end of the night, you should never leave cash in the box unattended. When a band member takes the cash home for safekeeping (or to deposit it into a real bank account the next day), you simply log a **Cash Transfer** from the Cash Box to that band member.

By using the Cash Box as a temporary holding area, your digital ledger will always perfectly reflect the physical reality of where your cash is located at any given moment.

articles.title: The VAT Bank
articles.body:
If the [Band Bank](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_Band_Bank) is a proxy for your shared checking account, the **VAT Bank** is a proxy for the government. 

It is an invisible, provisioned shadow profile designed to hold tax liabilities. It doesn't represent a physical bank account or a physical cash box—it represents the reality that at the end of the touring season, somebody is going to have to write a check to the tax authority.

## The Inverse of the Band Bank

The VAT Bank operates as the exact inverse of the Band Bank within our Entity-Based Accounting system:

* **Band Bank:** The *Bank* holds the physical cash, which means the Bank **owes** money back out to the individual band members for their respective shares. 
* **VAT Bank:** The *Members* hold the physical cash (collected at the merch table), but a percentage of that cash doesn't actually belong to them. Therefore, the Members **owe** money back out to the VAT Bank.

## How It Works in Practice

When you play shows in regions that require you to remit VAT (Value Added Tax) or sales tax, you are collecting that tax from the fans on behalf of the government. 

1. **Collecting Tax:** As you log transactions or settle up nightly merch sales, any tax collected is assigned to the VAT Bank profile. 
2. **Accruing Debt:** Because the physical cash from the show was handed to the band members (or deposited into the checking account), the ledger records that the members now *owe* the VAT Bank for that collected tax. 
3. **Writing the Check:** Over the course of the tour, the VAT Bank will accumulate a positive balance in the Standings (because everyone owes it money). At the end of the quarter or tour, when you file your taxes, whoever physically writes the check to the government simply logs a **Transfer** for the tax amount and assigns the VAT Bank as the **payee**. 

If the money to pay the tax comes out of the shared checking account, the Band Bank is logged as the **payer**. If a member (like Charlie) pays the tax out of his own pocket, Charlie is logged as the **payer**. This instantly zeroes out the VAT Bank's balance, and whoever wrote the check is properly credited for covering the band's tax liability through the standard automated debt settlement system.

## Configuring Your Tax Rate

You can update your band's active tax rate at any time by navigating to the **Band Settings** page and looking under **Financial Settings**.

* If you leave your tax rate set to **0%**, you won't ever have to deal with the VAT Bank, and it will remain dormant. 
* If you want to use the VAT Bank to track your tax liabilities, simply plug your local tax rate in there and BandMath will automatically calculate and route the appropriate funds.

## The Stripe Tax Alternative

If you rely heavily on digital transactions, you have the option to use Stripe's built-in tax services. [Stripe Tax](https://stripe.com/docs/tax) automatically calculates, collects, and reports sales tax and VAT based on your customer's location. 

However, before enabling Stripe Tax, you must consider the following:

* **Cash Transactions:** Stripe Tax only monitors digital transactions processed through the Stripe terminal. It cannot calculate or track tax liability for cash sales logged at the merch table.
* **Double-Taxing the Ledger:** If you enable Stripe Tax on your merchant account *and* plug a tax rate into BandMath, your books will essentially get "double-taxed." BandMath will deduct tax for the VAT Bank, while Stripe will separately deduct tax for its own compliance system.
* **Debt Settlement Disconnect:** Tax liabilities calculated entirely on Stripe's end will not natively flow back into BandMath's internal debt settlement algorithm.

**Our Advice:** Choose one system. If you need to track tax liability for cash sales or want everything cleanly tied into your band's internal debt settlement, use the **VAT Bank** (by setting your rate in Band Settings). If you want Stripe to handle complex multi-region compliance and don't care about cash taxes, you can use **Stripe Tax**—but you must set your BandMath tax rate to **0%** to prevent double-counting.

:::tip Touring Across Borders & Settling With Venues
Wondering how Ticket VAT vs. Merch VAT works in the EU, how US state sales tax affects flat merch pricing, or how BandMath backs out tax before calculating Venue Merch Cuts? Read our deep-dive guide on [Live Music Touring Tax, Ticket VAT & Nightly Settlements](/pl/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Touring_Tax_and_Nightly_Settlements).
:::

articles.title: Deleted Users
articles.body:
Under privacy laws like GDPR and CCPA, users have the right to completely delete their accounts and all associated personal data. However, in a double-entry accounting system like BandMath, simply deleting a member from the database would mathematically destroy every historical transaction they were ever a part of, throwing the entire band's ledger out of balance.

BandMath handles this elegantly through a secure anonymization process:

## 1. Profile Anonymization

Instead of removing the member's profile from the band entirely, BandMath securely wipes all Personally Identifiable Information (PII):
* The member's name is permanently changed to **"Deleted User"**.
* Their underlying authentication `user_id` connection is completely severed.
* Their profile is marked as inactive, meaning they are automatically excluded from any future splits (like the Penny Catcher or venue settlements) and will no longer receive a cut of merch sales.

## 2. Preserving Mathematical Integrity

By preserving this anonymized "ghost" profile, all historical ledger math remains perfectly intact. If that user paid for gas or owed the band $50 before they left, the ledger will accurately reflect those past balances attributed to "Deleted User". 

This ensures that the rest of the band's finances and historical records are never compromised when someone decides to delete their account.

:::note Leaving One Band vs. Deleting Your Entire Account
If a bandmate is simply leaving your band (or wrapping up a tour as a hired session player) and does **not** want to erase their entire BandMath account, they should use **Leave Band** in Settings (or an Admin can deactivate them in **Band Settings**). Deactivating a member excludes them from future splits and merch cuts while keeping their name and historical ledger records intact. See [Admins vs. Members](/pl/docs/Team_Management/Admins_vs_Members#leaving-a-band-vs-removing-a-member) for details.
:::

articles.title: The Retroactive VAT Correction
articles.body:
**The Scenario:** 
A band records a full night's worth of merch transactions using the Point-of-Sale system. At the end of the night, they realize their band's tax rate was set incorrectly. As a result, the `VAT Bank` has collected either too much or too little of the profit pool across dozens of transactions. 

**The Nightmare:** 
In a traditional spreadsheet, the band would have to manually edit every single line item and recalculate the split for every band member.

**The BandMath Solution ("The Grand Adjustment"):**
Bands do not need to delete a single transaction or mess with their merch inventory. Because of the double-entry routing algorithm, they can fix the entire night in seconds with a single manual transaction.

First, calculate the total discrepancy (e.g., "We collected $100 for tax, but it should have been $150. We are short $50").

### Scenario A: The VAT was too LOW (Short $50)
If the band is short $50 in tax, it means the band members accidentally pocketed $50 of profit that rightfully belongs to the government.
1. Go to the ledger and click **Add Transaction**.
2. Create a manual **Expense** for **$50** and title it "VAT Correction".
3. Set the "Paid By" field to the **VAT Bank**.

*Result:* The algorithm instantly registers that the VAT Bank covered a $50 expense for the group. It automatically deducts the respective split from each active member's standings and routes that money directly into the VAT Bank's balance.

### Scenario B: The VAT was too HIGH (Overpaid $50)
If the VAT bank accidentally captured $50 too much, it means the VAT Bank is holding $50 of the band's rightful profit.
1. Go to the ledger and click **Add Transaction**.
2. Create a manual **Income** for **$50** and title it "VAT Refund".
3. Set the "Collected By" field to the **VAT Bank**.

*Result:* The algorithm sees that the VAT Bank just collected $50 of band income. It instantly forces the VAT Bank to surrender that money and evenly distributes it back into the band members' balances.

articles.title: The Incorrect Merch Transaction
articles.body:
**The Scenario:** 
A band member was rushing at the merch table and accidentally checked out the wrong item or size (e.g., ringing up a Medium shirt instead of a Large). They realize the mistake a few minutes later and need to fix it.

**The Solution: Manual Inventory Override**
Whether the customer paid with Cash or Credit Card, you **should not delete the transaction** if the total dollar amount charged was correct. Deleting a transaction that was paid via Credit Card in BandMath does not automatically refund your payment processor (like Stripe or Square), and you do not want to force the customer to swipe their card again or hand back cash for a simple inventory logging mistake.

To fix the error:
1. Leave the transaction alone in the Ledger. The financial amount perfectly matches the money deposited into your cash box or bank account. 
2. An Admin should navigate to the **Merch Inventory** page and long press the item. 
3. Manually adjust the stock counts to reflect reality (e.g., manually add +1 to the Medium shirt stock, and subtract -1 from the Large shirt stock). 

This instantly corrects your physical inventory counts for the rest of the tour without creating a messy trail of deleted transactions in your financial ledger.

articles.title: Issuing a Refund (Merch Returns)
articles.body:
**The Scenario:** 
You sell a customer a shirt, but they immediately realize it's the wrong size. You don't have their correct size in stock, so they ask for their money back.

**The Best Practice:**
When a customer needs a full refund, you need to return their money and take the physical item back. BandMath handles the accounting for this beautifully through our "Self-Healing Ledger."

1. **Refund the Money:** Hand the cash back to the customer, or issue a refund through your credit card processor's app (Stripe, Square, etc.).
2. **Delete the Transaction in BandMath:** Go to the **Transaction Feed** (the Ledger), locate the original Merch Sale, and tap **Delete**.

**Why this works flawlessly:**
When you hit "Delete" on a Merch Sale to process a return, the backend triggers a cascading self-heal:
* **The Math Realignment:** The primary transaction and all associated profit splits are instantly removed, perfectly resetting every band member's standings back to where they were before the sale. You are no longer financially responsible for that income.
* **The Auto-Restock:** The backend opens up the associated order, looks at every single item and size that was in the cart, and automatically adds those exact quantities back into your active inventory (since you physically took the shirt back).
* **The Analytics:** The order records are purged, meaning your Sales Analyzer's ROI and velocity metrics remain completely uncontaminated by the refunded sale.

## Issuing a Partial Refund

Sometimes a full return isn't necessary. For example, if you accidentally overcharge a fan by €3 because the physical sign at the merch stand was outdated, or if there was a miscommunication on pricing, you can issue a **partial refund** without deleting the original transaction in BandMath.

Because BandMath provisions your band with a fully-featured Standard Stripe Connect account, you have direct control over your transactions. 

1. **Log into your Stripe Dashboard** (the same account you connected to BandMath).
2. Locate the specific payment in your **Payments** tab.
3. Click the **Refund** button and enter the exact amount you want to return to the fan (e.g., €3.00).

For more detailed help on navigating your merchant account, check out the [Stripe Knowledge Base on Issuing Refunds](https://support.stripe.com/questions/how-to-issue-a-refund).

## Sending Automated Refund Receipts

Because BandMath uses Stripe Connect (Standard), your band acts as the actual merchant of record and you own your own fully-featured Stripe account. This gives you complete liability protection, but it also means that automated email receipts are controlled by *your* Stripe settings, not BandMath's platform.

To automatically email your fans a receipt when you issue a refund (or a successful payment), you must turn it on in your Stripe Dashboard:

1. Log into your band's connected Stripe dashboard.
2. Click the **Settings** gear icon in the top right.
3. Under the *Business settings* section, click on **Customer emails**.
4. In the *Email customers about...* section, toggle on **Successful refunds** (and **Successful payments** if desired).
5. Hit **Save**.

1. Log into your Stripe Dashboard (the same account you connected to BandMath).
2. Locate the specific payment in your Payments tab.
3. Click the Refund button and enter the exact amount you want to return to the fan (e.g., €3.00).

For more detailed help on navigating your merchant account, check out the Stripe Knowledge Base on Issuing Refunds.

 Sending Automated Refund Receipts

Because BandMath uses Stripe Connect (Standard), your band acts as the actual merchant of record and you own your own fully-featured Stripe account. This gives you complete liability protection, but it also means that automated email receipts are controlled by your Stripe settings, not BandMath's platform.

To automatically email your fans a receipt when you issue a refund (or a successful payment), you must turn it on in your Stripe Dashboard:

1. Log into your band's connected Stripe dashboard.
2. Click the Settings gear icon in the top right.
3. Under the Business settings section, click on Customer emails.
4. In the Email customers about... section, toggle on Successful refunds (and Successful payments if desired).
5. Hit Save.

sections.heading: Issuing a Refund (Merch Returns)
sections.content:
**The Scenario:** 
You sell a customer a shirt, but they immediately realize it's the wrong size. You don't have their correct size in stock, so they ask for their money back.

**The Best Practice:**
When a customer needs a full refund, you need to return their money and take the physical item back. BandMath handles the accounting for this beautifully through our "Self-Healing Ledger."

1. **Refund the Money:** Hand the cash back to the customer, or issue a refund through your credit card processor's app (Stripe, Square, etc.).
2. **Delete the Transaction in BandMath:** Go to the **Transaction Feed** (the Ledger), locate the original Merch Sale, and tap **Delete**.

**Why this works flawlessly:**
When you hit "Delete" on a Merch Sale to process a return, the backend triggers a cascading self-heal:
* **The Math Realignment:** The primary transaction and all associated profit splits are instantly removed, perfectly resetting every band member's standings back to where they were before the sale. You are no longer financially responsible for that income.
* **The Auto-Restock:** The backend opens up the associated order, looks at every single item and size that was in the cart, and automatically adds those exact quantities back into your active inventory (since you physically took the shirt back).
* **The Analytics:** The order records are purged, meaning your Sales Analyzer's ROI and velocity metrics remain completely uncontaminated by the refunded sale.

articles.title: Inventory Missing or Showing Zero
articles.body:
**The Problem:** 
You are looking at your Merch Stand and an item is showing a much lower quantity than you physically have on hand, or it is reporting `0` inventory entirely—but you know for a fact that you still have some in the merch bin!

**The Cause:** 
You likely have items sitting in your active shopping cart. 

To prevent two band members from accidentally selling the same physical shirt at the exact same time (double-selling), BandMath automatically reserves inventory the moment it is added to a cart. If a shirt is sitting in an active or abandoned cart, it is immediately deducted from the available inventory count, even if the sale hasn't been finalized yet.

**The Solution:**
1. Navigate to the **Checkout** or **Cart** screen in the BandMath app.
2. Review the items currently sitting in the cart.
3. Tap **Clear Cart** (or swipe to remove the individual items).

As soon as the cart is emptied, the reserved items are instantly released back into your available inventory, and your counts will return to normal!

articles.title: Frequently Asked Questions
articles.body:
How do I upgrade my subscription? All subscriptions are managed securely via our web portal. To upgrade, simply log in at [account.itsbandmath.com](https://account.itsbandmath.com) using your Admin credentials and select the tier that fits your band's needs. For more details, see [Upgrading and Downgrading](/pl/docs/Billing_and_Account/Upgrading_and_Downgrading).
Can I be in multiple bands on BandMath? Yes! BandMath supports multiple bands for each user. You can be a member of an unlimited number of bands and an Admin for up to 5 bands. You can easily switch between your bands at any time from the Band Dropdown on the User Settings page.
Does BandMath handle multiple currencies for international tours? Yes! You do not need to create a new workspace or change your base currency when touring abroad. For in-person card payments, you can seamlessly accept foreign currencies using our [Stripe QR Codes](/pl/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) workflow. Stripe handles the foreign exchange conversion dynamically, and deposits the funds into your home bank account. For physical cash, see our guide on the [Merch Float](/pl/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Multi_Currency_Touring#the-merch-float--foreign-cash-walkthrough).
What is the "Band Bank"? The Band Bank is a permanent member profile created automatically for your band. It acts as a proxy for your shared business checking account. Unlike traditional spreadsheets that only compute a flat percentage of overall ownership, BandMath continuously tracks exactly how much of that communal money belongs to each individual member on an ongoing basis. Learn more about entity-based accounting in [The Band Bank](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_Band_Bank) article.
Can I use BandMath if some of my band members don't want to download the app? Yes! You can create a "Shadow Profile" for them. An Admin can log transactions on their behalf, allowing you to track their balances perfectly without them ever needing to open the app. Learn more in our [Shadow Profiles guide](/pl/docs/Team_Management/Shadow_Profiles).
How does Automated Debt Settlement work? Instead of tracking a tangled web of "who owes who" for every individual receipt, BandMath analyzes the net balances of everyone in the band. It then calculates the absolute simplest way to settle all debts with the fewest number of cash transfers. For a deep dive into the math behind this, see [The Ledger](/pl/docs/Features/The_Ledger).
How do we handle taxes on merch sales? BandMath features a "VAT Bank" – a special, automated profile that holds Value-Added Tax (or sales tax). When you sell merch, the tax portion is automatically transferred to the VAT Bank, ensuring you don't accidentally spend money you owe to the government. Learn exactly how this proxy account works in our [VAT Bank Guide](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank). If you ever need to apply taxes to past transactions, check out our guide on [Retroactive VAT](/pl/docs/Troubleshooting/Retroactive_VAT).
What is a Groovatar? A Groovy Avatar! These are funky, musically-themed characters that pop up on loading screens throughout the app. They are also used as default placeholder images when transaction receipts or merch inventory photos are not available.
Can we export our data for tax season? Absolutely. You can export your entire ledger to a detailed CSV file at any time, which includes every transaction, date, payer, and calculated balance. For more details on what's included and how to run the report, read about [Data Exports](/pl/docs/Features/Data_Exports).
What happens if I make a mistake on a transaction? Anyone in the band can edit or delete any transaction at any time, regardless of who created it. For a walk-through on how to handle refunds or incorrect logs, see [Incorrect Merch Transactions](/pl/docs/Troubleshooting/Incorrect_Merch_Transaction) or [Issuing a Refund](/pl/docs/Troubleshooting/Issuing_a_Refund).
Can we sell items at-cost to band members? Yes! When logging a sale in the Point-of-Sale (POS) system, you can toggle the "At Cost" switch for any band member, which allows them to take an item at its exact unit cost rather than the retail markup. Read the full walkthrough on [At Cost Member Purchases](/pl/docs/Advanced_Workflows/At_Cost_Member_Purchase).
How does BandMath handle fractions of a cent? Our "Penny Catcher" algorithm ensures that when an expense is split unevenly (e.g. $10.00 split 3 ways), fractions of a cent are never lost or infinitely rounded. The ledger will always balance perfectly to the penny. For a deep dive into how we handle fractional remainders, read about [The Penny Catcher](/pl/docs/Features/The_Penny_Catcher).
How can I get help or contact support? To get help, simply log into the BandMath app, open the end drawer (the menu on the right side of the screen), and tap **Support** at the bottom of the list. From there, you can send a message directly to our team, and you'll receive a response straight to your email inbox. Alternatively, you can always reach out to us directly by emailing { e.preventDefault(); if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined') { navigator.clipboard.writeText('support@itsbandmath.com'); const originalText = e.target.innerText; e.target.innerText = 'Copied!'; setTimeout(() => e.target.innerText = originalText, 2000); } }} style={{cursor: 'pointer', color: 'var(--ifm-color-primary)', fontWeight: 'bold', textDecoration: 'underline'}} title="Click to copy email">support{'@'}itsbandmath.com.
What are the processing fees for card payments? When you accept an in-person card payment using Tap to Pay on iPhone or Android, the transaction is processed through Stripe Terminal. The standard processing rate is **1.4% + €0.10** per transaction. Additionally, Stripe charges a **€0.10** "Tap on Mobile" fee for every physical tap. Instead of taking this out of each transaction, Stripe batches them together and bills your account once at the end of the day. For a full breakdown of fees (including Radar fraud protection for manually entered cards), see the [Tap to Pay Guide](/pl/docs/Accept_Payments/Tap_to_Pay#processing-fees).
How do I send receipts to my fans? Immediately after completing a transaction in the Merch Stand, you will be prompted with an option to email a receipt to the customer on the success screen. If you accidentally close that screen, or if the customer typed their email address wrong, don't panic! Simply go to your **Transaction Feed**, tap on that specific transaction to open the detail page, and scroll to the bottom. From there, you can see where the receipt was sent, update the email address, and resend it. **For Automated & Refund Receipts:** Because BandMath uses Stripe Connect, your band owns its own merchant account. To automatically email your fans a receipt for refunds or successful payments without doing it manually, be sure to enable **Customer Emails** in your Stripe Dashboard. (Settings > Business Settings > Customer Emails).
What is the Cash Box? The Cash Box is a special account that represents the physical cash currently sitting at your merch table. It acts as a temporary holding area for unclaimed cash that needs to be distributed or deposited before the end of the night. Learn more in our [Cash Box](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_Cash_Box) guide.
What happens to the ledger if a member deletes their account? When a user deletes their account under GDPR or CCPA, BandMath securely anonymizes their profile instead of destroying it. Their name is permanently changed to "Deleted User" and their personal data is wiped, but the ledger math stays perfectly intact. You can read the full mechanical breakdown of this process in our [Deleted Users](/pl/docs/Team_Management/Deleted_Users) article.
How do I log a merch sale? Before you can log a sale, you first need to define your items and input your stock inside the **Merch Warehouse** on the **Shop** tab. Once your inventory is set up, tap the items in the **Merch Stand** to add them to your cart and complete the checkout. For a complete step-by-step walkthrough of this process, check out our guide on [The First Tour](/pl/docs/Getting_Started/The_First_Tour#3-stock-your-merch-warehouse).
What is the difference between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas? BandMath supports three account personas tailored to your role at the show: * **Band:** Gives you the full 5-tab workspace (`Home`, `Shop`, `Events`, `Standings`, `Cart`), multi-member ledger accounting, the Merch Warehouse, Setlist Organizer, and Band Calendar. * **Venue & Tour Manager:** Gives you a focused 3-tab box office and settlement hub (`Events`, `Bouncer`, `Cart`) with your own dedicated Merchant Account & Cashbox. You can switch between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas at any time inside **User Settings**. Read the full [Venues & Tour Managers Quickstart](/pl/docs/Getting_Started/Venues_and_Tour_Managers).
How do multiple bands and venues connect to the same show? Every event in BandMath generates a unique **6-Character Show Access Code**. Any free Band, Venue, or Tour Manager can create the event (`[ + CREATE EVENT ]`) and share the 6-character code with everyone on the bill. Bands can join (`[ JOIN SHOW ]`) as Headliner, Co-Headliner, Support, or Opener at any time—even mid-show! See [Creating & Joining Multi-Band Shows](/pl/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Creating_and_Joining_Shows).
Who claims online ticket sales on a multi-band bill, and when does it lock? Any participant on the show with an active Pro subscription and connected Stripe account (Venue, Tour Manager, or Band) can click **`[ CLAIM ONLINE TICKETING ]`**. It remains switchable while `0` tickets have been sold, and permanently locks (`🔒`) the instant the first online ticket is purchased so all pre-sale funds and ticket tax set-asides remain unified in one merchant account. Learn more in [Online Ticketing & Promo Links](/pl/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links).
How do we track how many pre-sale tickets each band sold? Frequently Asked Questions

How do I upgrade my subscription?

All subscriptions are managed securely via our web portal. To upgrade, simply log in at account.itsbandmath.com using your Admin credentials and select the tier that fits your band's needs. For more details, see Upgrading and Downgrading.

Can I be in multiple bands on BandMath?

Yes! BandMath supports multiple bands for each user. You can be a member of an unlimited number of bands and an Admin for up to 5 bands. You can easily switch between your bands at any time from the Band Dropdown on the User Settings page.

Does BandMath handle multiple currencies for international tours?

Yes! You do not need to create a new workspace or change your base currency when touring abroad. For in-person card payments, you can seamlessly accept foreign currencies using our Stripe QR Codes workflow. Stripe handles the foreign exchange conversion dynamically, and deposits the funds into your home bank account. For physical cash, see our guide on the Merch Float.

What is the "Band Bank"?

The Band Bank is a permanent member profile created automatically for your band. It acts as a proxy for your shared business checking account. Unlike traditional spreadsheets that only compute a flat percentage of overall ownership, BandMath continuously tracks exactly how much of that communal money belongs to each individual member on an ongoing basis. Learn more about entity-based accounting in The Band Bank article.

Can I use BandMath if some of my band members don't want to download the app?

Yes! You can create a "Shadow Profile" for them. An Admin can log transactions on their behalf, allowing you to track their balances perfectly without them ever needing to open the app. Learn more in our Shadow Profiles guide.

How does Automated Debt Settlement work?

Instead of tracking a tangled web of "who owes who" for every individual receipt, BandMath analyzes the net balances of everyone in the band. It then calculates the absolute simplest way to settle all debts with the fewest number of cash transfers. For a deep dive into the math behind this, see The Ledger.

How do we handle taxes on merch sales?

BandMath features a "VAT Bank" – a special, automated profile that holds Value-Added Tax (or sales tax). When you sell merch, the tax portion is automatically transferred to the VAT Bank, ensuring you don't accidentally spend money you owe to the government. Learn exactly how this proxy account works in our VAT Bank Guide. If you ever need to apply taxes to past transactions, check out our guide on Retroactive VAT.

What is a Groovatar?

A Groovy Avatar! These are funky, musically-themed characters that pop up on loading screens throughout the app. They are also used as default placeholder images when transaction receipts or merch inventory photos are not available.

Can we export our data for tax season?

Absolutely. You can export your entire ledger to a detailed CSV file at any time, which includes every transaction, date, payer, and calculated balance. For more details on what's included and how to run the report, read about Data Exports.

What happens if I make a mistake on a transaction?

Anyone in the band can edit or delete any transaction at any time, regardless of who created it. For a walk-through on how to handle refunds or incorrect logs, see Incorrect Merch Transactions or Issuing a Refund.

Can we sell items at-cost to band members?

Yes! When logging a sale in the Point-of-Sale (POS) system, you can toggle the "At Cost" switch for any band member, which allows them to take an item at its exact unit cost rather than the retail markup. Read the full walkthrough on At Cost Member Purchases.

How does BandMath handle fractions of a cent?

Our "Penny Catcher" algorithm ensures that when an expense is split unevenly (e.g. $10.00 split 3 ways), fractions of a cent are never lost or infinitely rounded. The ledger will always balance perfectly to the penny. For a deep dive into how we handle fractional remainders, read about The Penny Catcher.

How can I get help or contact support?

To get help, simply log into the BandMath app, open the end drawer (the menu on the right side of the screen), and tap Support at the bottom of the list. From there, you can send a message directly to our team, and you'll receive a response straight to your email inbox. 

Alternatively, you can always reach out to us directly by emailing  { e.preventDefault(); if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined') { navigator.clipboard.writeText('support@itsbandmath.com'); const originalText = e.target.innerText; e.target.innerText = 'Copied!'; setTimeout(() = e.target.innerText = originalText, 2000); } }} style={{cursor: 'pointer', color: 'var(--ifm-color-primary)', fontWeight: 'bold', textDecoration: 'underline'}} title="Click to copy email"support{'@'}itsbandmath.com.

What are the processing fees for card payments?

When you accept an in-person card payment using Tap to Pay on iPhone or Android, the transaction is processed through Stripe Terminal. The standard processing rate is 1.4% + €0.10 per transaction. 

Additionally, Stripe charges a €0.10 "Tap on Mobile" fee for every physical tap. Instead of taking this out of each transaction, Stripe batches them together and bills your account once at the end of the day. For a full breakdown of fees (including Radar fraud protection for manually entered cards), see the Tap to Pay Guide.

How do I send receipts to my fans?

Immediately after completing a transaction in the Merch Stand, you will be prompted with an option to email a receipt to the customer on the success screen. 

If you accidentally close that screen, or if the customer typed their email address wrong, don't panic! Simply go to your Transaction Feed, tap on that specific transaction to open the detail page, and scroll to the bottom. From there, you can see where the receipt was sent, update the email address, and resend it.

For Automated & Refund Receipts: Because BandMath uses Stripe Connect, your band owns its own merchant account. To automatically email your fans a receipt for refunds or successful payments without doing it manually, be sure to enable Customer Emails in your Stripe Dashboard. (Settings  Business Settings  Customer Emails).

What is the Cash Box?

The Cash Box is a special account that represents the physical cash currently sitting at your merch table. It acts as a temporary holding area for unclaimed cash that needs to be distributed or deposited before the end of the night. Learn more in our Cash Box guide.

What happens to the ledger if a member deletes their account?

When a user deletes their account under GDPR or CCPA, BandMath securely anonymizes their profile instead of destroying it. Their name is permanently changed to "Deleted User" and their personal data is wiped, but the ledger math stays perfectly intact. You can read the full mechanical breakdown of this process in our Deleted Users article.

How do I log a merch sale?

Before you can log a sale, you first need to define your items and input your stock inside the Merch Warehouse on the Shop tab. Once your inventory is set up, tap the items in the Merch Stand to add them to your cart and complete the checkout. For a complete step-by-step walkthrough of this process, check out our guide on The First Tour.

What is the difference between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas?

BandMath supports three account personas tailored to your role at the show:
 Band: Gives you the full 5-tab workspace (Home, Shop, Events, Standings, Cart), multi-member ledger accounting, the Merch Warehouse, Setlist Organizer, and Band Calendar.
 Venue & Tour Manager: Gives you a focused 3-tab box office and settlement hub (Events, Bouncer, Cart) with your own dedicated Merchant Account & Cashbox. You can switch between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas at any time inside User Settings. Read the full Venues & Tour Managers Quickstart.

How do multiple bands and venues connect to the same show?

Every event in BandMath generates a unique 6-Character Show Access Code. Any free Band, Venue, or Tour Manager can create the event ([ + CREATE EVENT ]) and share the 6-character code with everyone on the bill. Bands can join ([ JOIN SHOW ]) as Headliner, Co-Headliner, Support, or Opener at any time—even mid-show! See Creating & Joining Multi-Band Shows.

Who claims online ticket sales on a multi-band bill, and when does it lock?

Any participant on the show with an active Pro subscription and connected Stripe account (Venue, Tour Manager, or Band) can click [ CLAIM ONLINE TICKETING ]. It remains switchable while 0 tickets have been sold, and permanently locks (🔒) the instant the first online ticket is purchased so all pre-sale funds and ticket tax set-asides remain unified in one merchant account. Learn more in Online Ticketing & Promo Links.

How do we track how many pre-sale tickets each band sold?

When any band on the bill taps [ Share Link ] on the event page, BandMath automatically attaches their band's attribution tag (?ref=) to their checkout link and QR flyer so the Closing Table tracks exact pre-sale tickets sold per band. Fans and street-team promoters can also share their own referral pass to climb the event's Referral Leaderboard! See Online Ticketing & Promo Links.

Can I hand my phone to a door person to scan QR tickets without showing them our band's money?

Yes! Open Bouncer Mode and enable the Bouncer Safety Lock before handing your phone to door staff. They will be able to scan QR tickets with the mobile camera (on iOS and Android) and check off the Guest List all night, but exiting Bouncer Mode requires your device's Face ID, Touch ID, or Passcode. Read more in Door Tickets & Bouncer Mode.

What happens when a band member pockets the cash payout envelope at the end of a show?

When your band's payout or expense share is marked settled in The Closing Room, you choose Cash vs. Bank Transfer and select who received or paid it (Cashbox, Band Bank, or a specific active member like John). If John pockets the cash envelope, BandMath automatically credits every bandmate their share of the show income and records that John is holding the cash—updating your Standings immediately.

articles.title: Privacy Policy
articles.body:
### 1\. The Short Version

We built BandMath to help musicians manage their money, not to mine your personal data. We only collect the information we absolutely need to make the app function, process your subscription, and allow your band to track expenses and take payments. We will never sell your personal data to advertisers or third parties.

### 2\. What Information We Collect

To provide the BandMath service, we collect:

*   **Account Data:** Your email address and basic profile information to create and secure your account.
*   **Financial & App Data:** The numerical data, expense logs, and inventory numbers you input into the ledger.
*   **User Uploads:** Any photos or documents you choose to upload for receipt tracking.
*   **Payment Information:** If you activate a Merchant Services Subscription, your payment details are collected directly by Stripe. BandMath does not store or have access to your full credit card number.

### 3\. Stripe Connect & In-Person Payments (Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android)

If your band uses our Stripe Connect integration to process fan payments via Tap to Pay on iPhone or Tap to Pay on Android, you will be required to provide identity verification (KYC) and business details directly to Stripe. This highly sensitive data is handled entirely by Stripe’s secure infrastructure. BandMath does not host or store your government ID, bank account routing numbers, or your fans' credit card data.

### 4\. Third-Party Services We Use

We run a lean operation and rely on a few trusted third-party categories of service providers to keep the app running securely. Your data interacts with:

*   **Cloud Hosting & Database Providers:** To securely store your user account, app data, and receipt uploads.
*   **App Framework Providers:** To build and host the app interface you interact with.
*   **Payment Processors:** To process your Merchant Services Subscription and facilitate your band's Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android transactions.
*   **Communication Platforms:** To manage our email list and send you transparent development updates.

### 5\. Your Data Rights (GDPR)

You own your data. Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you have the right to:

*   Ask for a copy of the personal data we hold about you (which you can do via the native export tool in the app).
*   Request that we correct any inaccurate information.
*   Withdraw your consent for marketing emails at any time.
*   Request that we completely delete your account and data from our active systems.

### 6\. Cookies

We keep things simple and respect your privacy. The BandMath website and web app only use strictly necessary cookies required for the site to function, to keep you securely logged in, and to route you to our payment processor. We do not use non-essential, invasive marketing or tracking cookies.

All subscriptions are managed securely via our web portal. To upgrade, simply log in at account.itsbandmath.com using your Admin credentials and select the tier that fits your band's needs. For more details, see Upgrading and Downgrading.

faqPairs.question: Can I be in multiple bands on BandMath?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Yes! BandMath supports multiple bands for each user. You can be a member of an unlimited number of bands and an Admin for up to 5 bands. You can easily switch between your bands at any time from the Band Dropdown on the User Settings page.

faqPairs.question: Does BandMath handle multiple currencies for international tours?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Yes! You do not need to create a new workspace or change your base currency when touring abroad. For in-person card payments, you can seamlessly accept foreign currencies using our [Stripe QR Codes](/pl/docs/Accept_Payments/Stripe_QR_Codes) workflow. Stripe handles the foreign exchange conversion dynamically, and deposits the funds into your home bank account. For physical cash, see our guide on the [Merch Float](/pl/docs/Advanced_Workflows/Multi_Currency_Touring#the-merch-float--foreign-cash-walkthrough).

faqPairs.question: What is the "Band Bank"?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: The Band Bank is a permanent member profile created automatically for your band. It acts as a proxy for your shared business checking account. Unlike traditional spreadsheets that only compute a flat percentage of overall ownership, BandMath continuously tracks exactly how much of that communal money belongs to each individual member on an ongoing basis. Learn more about entity-based accounting in [The Band Bank](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_Band_Bank) article.

faqPairs.question: Can I use BandMath if some of my band members don't want to download the app?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Yes! You can create a "Shadow Profile" for them. An Admin can log transactions on their behalf, allowing you to track their balances perfectly without them ever needing to open the app. Learn more in our [Shadow Profiles guide](/pl/docs/Team_Management/Shadow_Profiles).

faqPairs.question: How does Automated Debt Settlement work?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Instead of tracking a tangled web of "who owes who" for every individual receipt, BandMath analyzes the net balances of everyone in the band. It then calculates the absolute simplest way to settle all debts with the fewest number of cash transfers. For a deep dive into the math behind this, see [The Ledger](/pl/docs/Features/The_Ledger).

faqPairs.question: How do we handle taxes on merch sales?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: BandMath features a "VAT Bank" – a special, automated profile that holds Value-Added Tax (or sales tax). When you sell merch, the tax portion is automatically transferred to the VAT Bank, ensuring you don't accidentally spend money you owe to the government. Learn exactly how this proxy account works in our [VAT Bank Guide](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_VAT_Bank). If you ever need to apply taxes to past transactions, check out our guide on [Retroactive VAT](/pl/docs/Troubleshooting/Retroactive_VAT).

faqPairs.question: What happens if I make a mistake on a transaction?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Anyone in the band can edit or delete any transaction at any time, regardless of who created it. faqPairs.question: Can we sell items at-cost to band members?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Yes! When logging a sale in the Point-of-Sale (POS) system, you can toggle the "At Cost" switch for any band member, which allows them to take an item at its exact unit cost rather than the retail markup. Read the full walkthrough on [At Cost Member Purchases](/pl/docs/Advanced_Workflows/At_Cost_Member_Purchase).

faqPairs.question: How does BandMath handle fractions of a cent?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Our "Penny Catcher" algorithm ensures that when an expense is split unevenly (e.g. $10.00 split 3 ways), fractions of a cent are never lost or infinitely rounded. The ledger will always balance perfectly to the penny. For a deep dive into how we handle fractional remainders, read about [The Penny Catcher](/pl/docs/Features/The_Penny_Catcher).

faqPairs.question: What are the processing fees for card payments?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown:
When you accept an in-person card payment using Tap to Pay on iPhone or Android, the transaction is processed through Stripe Terminal. The standard processing rate is **1.4% + €0.10** per transaction. 

Additionally, Stripe charges a **€0.10** "Tap on Mobile" fee for every physical tap. Instead of taking this out of each transaction, Stripe batches them together and bills your account once at the end of the day. For a full breakdown of fees (including Radar fraud protection for manually entered cards), see the [Tap to Pay Guide](/pl/docs/Accept_Payments/Tap_to_Pay#processing-fees).

faqPairs.question: How do I send receipts to my fans?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown:
Immediately after completing a transaction in the Merch Stand, you will be prompted with an option to email a receipt to the customer on the success screen. 

If you accidentally close that screen, or if the customer typed their email address wrong, don't panic! Simply go to your **Transaction Feed**, tap on that specific transaction to open the detail page, and scroll to the bottom. From there, you can see where the receipt was sent, update the email address, and resend it.

**For Automated & Refund Receipts:** Because BandMath uses Stripe Connect, your band owns its own merchant account. To automatically email your fans a receipt for refunds or successful payments without doing it manually, be sure to enable **Customer Emails** in your Stripe Dashboard. (Settings > Business Settings > Customer Emails).

faqPairs.question: What is the Cash Box?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: The Cash Box is a special account that represents the physical cash currently sitting at your merch table. It acts as a temporary holding area for unclaimed cash that needs to be distributed or deposited before the end of the night. Learn more in our [Cash Box](/pl/docs/Team_Management/The_Cash_Box) guide.

faqPairs.question: What happens to the ledger if a member deletes their account?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: When a user deletes their account under GDPR or CCPA, BandMath securely anonymizes their profile instead of destroying it. Their name is permanently changed to "Deleted User" and their personal data is wiped, but the ledger math stays perfectly intact. You can read the full mechanical breakdown of this process in our [Deleted Users](/pl/docs/Team_Management/Deleted_Users) article.

faqPairs.question: How do I log a merch sale?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Before you can log a sale, you first need to define your items and input your stock inside the **Merch Warehouse** on the **Shop** tab. Once your inventory is set up, tap the items in the **Merch Stand** to add them to your cart and complete the checkout. For a complete step-by-step walkthrough of this process, check out our guide on [The First Tour](/pl/docs/Getting_Started/The_First_Tour#3-stock-your-merch-warehouse).

faqPairs.question: What is the difference between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown:
BandMath supports three account personas tailored to your role at the show:
* **Band:** Gives you the full 5-tab workspace (`Home`, `Shop`, `Events`, `Standings`, `Cart`), multi-member ledger accounting, the Merch Warehouse, Setlist Organizer, and Band Calendar.
* **Venue & Tour Manager:** Gives you a focused 3-tab box office and settlement hub (`Events`, `Bouncer`, `Cart`) with your own dedicated Merchant Account & Cashbox. You can switch between Band, Venue, and Tour Manager personas at any time inside **User Settings**. Read the full [Venues & Tour Managers Quickstart](/pl/docs/Getting_Started/Venues_and_Tour_Managers).

faqPairs.question: How do multiple bands and venues connect to the same show?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Every event in BandMath generates a unique **6-Character Show Access Code**. Any free Band, Venue, or Tour Manager can create the event (`[ + CREATE EVENT ]`) and share the 6-character code with everyone on the bill. Bands can join (`[ JOIN SHOW ]`) as Headliner, Co-Headliner, Support, or Opener at any time—even mid-show! See [Creating & Joining Multi-Band Shows](/pl/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Creating_and_Joining_Shows).

faqPairs.question: Who claims online ticket sales on a multi-band bill, and when does it lock?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Any participant on the show with an active Pro subscription and connected Stripe account (Venue, Tour Manager, or Band) can click **`[ CLAIM ONLINE TICKETING ]`**. It remains switchable while `0` tickets have been sold, and permanently locks (`🔒`) the instant the first online ticket is purchased so all pre-sale funds and ticket tax set-asides remain unified in one merchant account. Learn more in [Online Ticketing & Promo Links](/pl/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links).

faqPairs.question: How do we track how many pre-sale tickets each band sold?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: When any band on the bill taps **`[ Share Link ]`** on the event page, BandMath automatically attaches their band's attribution tag (`?ref=`) to their checkout link and QR flyer so the Closing Table tracks exact pre-sale tickets sold per band. Fans and street-team promoters can also share their own referral pass to climb the event's **Referral Leaderboard**! See [Online Ticketing & Promo Links](/pl/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Online_Ticketing_and_Promoter_Links#2-automatic-per-band-promoter-attribution-links-ref).

faqPairs.question: Can I hand my phone to a door person to scan QR tickets without showing them our band's money?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: Yes! Open **Bouncer Mode** and enable the **Bouncer Safety Lock** before handing your phone to door staff. They will be able to scan QR tickets with the mobile camera (on iOS and Android) and check off the Guest List all night, but exiting Bouncer Mode requires your device's Face ID, Touch ID, or Passcode. Read more in [Door Tickets & Bouncer Mode](/pl/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Door_Tickets_and_Bouncer_Mode#2-bouncer-mode--the-hand-off-safety-lock).

faqPairs.question: What happens when a band member pockets the cash payout envelope at the end of a show?
faqPairs.answerMarkdown: When your band's payout or expense share is marked settled in [The Closing Room](/pl/docs/Events_and_Closing_Room/Multi_Band_Closing_Room#4-granular-settlement-to-ledger-commits), you choose **`Cash` vs. `Bank Transfer`** and select who received or paid it (`Cashbox`, `Band Bank`, or a specific active member like `John`). If John pockets the cash envelope, BandMath automatically credits every bandmate their share of the show income and records that John is holding the cash—updating your **Standings** immediately.
